title: Control POSTs must fail closed when no API token is configured

body:
# Mission

Make this exporter safe and sane to run in production, unattended, for months, against a **large
Meraki organization**. Today it should not be offered to a 500-network / 5,000-device customer: an
unauthenticated control endpoint can force full collections, the scale model projects an
unsustainable API plan and a multi-million-series registry for a plausible switch-heavy fleet, and
two rate limiters pace the same traffic without knowing about each other.

Source: an adversarial nine-lane read-only audit run on 2026-08-12 against `5579b26`, with live
contention testing against the homelab org. It produced **43 findings** (1 BLOCKER, 10 HIGH, 26
MEDIUM, 5 LOW, 1 INFO after adjudication). Triage added **3 more items**: two vendor-limit findings
the audit missed and one arithmetic contradiction it under-stated. All 46 are mapped onto the child
issues below — the mapping is the audit trail, and no finding was dropped.

# Binding operating rules

1. **Every child issue is self-contained.** Mechanism, `file:line` refs and acceptance criteria live
   in the issue body. A future session with no memory of this one must be able to work any issue
   from GitHub alone.
2. **One issue per deliverable, not per finding.** Each issue lists the finding IDs it closes as
   acceptance checkboxes. Several findings collapse into one change — the pacing facade alone closes
   four.
3. **Commit straight to `main`** with `Closes #NN` in the completing commit. Never a PR flow.
4. **Validate before implementing.** The audit was against `5579b26`; re-confirm the mechanism at
   `file:line` on the current tree before writing a fix. If a premise is stale, say so on the issue
   and close it rather than forcing a change.
5. **`make check` green before every commit** (ruff + mypy + pytest), plus `make docgen` when
   metrics, config or endpoints change. Evidence, not assertion.
6. **Decisions D1–D18 below are FROZEN.** Do not re-litigate them. If you have new evidence one is
   wrong, say so on this tracker before acting.

# Decisions already made — do not re-open

Taken 2026-08-12 during triage, each answering a question the audit raised.

## D1 — Control-POST authentication: fail closed, no escape hatch
`/api/collectors/trigger` and `/api/clients/clear-dns-cache` return **401 unless
`server.api_token` is set**. **No** `insecure_allow_unauthenticated_control` flag — rejected because
a permanently-supported insecure mode gets set in a Helm values file and forgotten, returning the
BLOCKER to the field. The web UI **omits or disables** the trigger and DNS-clear buttons, with an
explanatory tooltip, when no token is configured. This **overturns #558 / F-167**, which knowingly
left POST auth optional. Breaking change for v1.0.x users of those buttons; needs a
`docs/upgrading.md` entry.

## D2 — Fleet fixtures: one generator, SEVEN named presets, tiered in CI
A single generator parameterised by `(networks, per-family device counts, ports/switch,
SSIDs/network, clients)`.

| Preset | Shape | Stresses |
|---|---|---|
| `HOMELAB` | 1 net / 19 dev (1 MR56, MS120-8LP, MS250-24P, 16 MT) | the measured baseline — must reproduce live numbers |
| `BRANCH-RETAIL` | 750 nets × (2 MX + 1 MS24 + 3 MR) ≈ 4,500 dev | **network-count-driven API budget** — the dominant real shape |
| `CAMPUS` | 20 nets, ~4,000 MR + 1,200 MS48 ≈ 5,200 dev | dense wireless, per-AP fan-out |
| `DENSE-SWITCH` | 50 nets, 2,000 MS @ 48 ports ≈ 96k ports | **cardinality / series explosion** |
| `XL-MULTI-SITE` | 3,500 nets / ~20,000 dev | pagination depth, org ceiling |
| `MULTI-ORG-SHARD` | N instances × N orgs from one source IP | the 100 req/s per-source-IP limit |
| `CAMERA-HEAVY` | 30 nets × 800 MV | MV, the least-verified family |

**CI tiering:** every PR → `HOMELAB` + `BRANCH-RETAIL`. Scheduled → `CAMPUS`, `DENSE-SWITCH`,
`XL-MULTI-SITE`. On demand → `MULTI-ORG-SHARD`, `CAMERA-HEAVY`.

**Binding honesty rule:** `CAMERA-HEAVY`, and every absent-family element in any other preset, is
marked `SHAPE-ASSUMED` in the fixture, so a green test can never read as having verified a family
nobody owns.

### Vendor limits the presets must respect (researched 2026-08-12, authoritative)
- **50,000** devices/org recommended max; **5,000** devices/network combined.
- Hard **per-network** caps: **MX = 2**, **MG = 4**, MV = 1,000, MT = 1,700, APs = 5,000,
  switches = 5,000. This makes "1,000 devices per family bucket, evenly distributed" **structurally
  impossible** — a 500-network org cannot hold more than 1,000 MX or 2,000 MG.
- \>700 orgs → Meraki asks you to contact your account team. Meraki names **20,000+ devices** as
  where API monitoring beats SNMP.
- Real published estates are **branch-shaped, not campus-shaped**: SPAR ICS 3,500 stores,
  Visionworks 740 locations, a 500-store retailer; community operators run 1,000+ networks in one org
  and hit the 10 req/s ceiling daily. **The audit modelled no such shape**, and it is the one most
  likely to break this exporter because most of its cost scales with network count.

## D3 — Client collection: supported at LARGE, with every unbounded dimension bounded
Rejected moving per-client signals to data-logs-only (breaking on a released 1.x, reverses #533's
approved ID-only join) and rejected declaring it small/medium-only (a warning that still lets you
enable it merely documents the failure). The defect is **unboundedness, not volume** — ~275k series
is only ~13% of the LARGE projection, but applications-per-client has no cap an operator can set.
`clients.enabled` defaults to **`False`** (`config_models.py:928`), so the default path carries none
of this risk.

## D4 — Pacing: project AIMD owns it, smart flow OFF, one instrumented facade
Set `smart_flow_enabled=False` explicitly; `OrgRateLimiter` becomes the sole pacer. Every SDK call
routes through **one facade** that acquires a token, records the attempt and owns retries.
Verified in the pinned SDK (`meraki/config.py`): `SMART_FLOW_ENABLED = True`,
`SMART_FLOW_ORG_RATE = 9`, **`SMART_FLOW_GLOBAL_RATE = 100`** (the SDK already implements the
per-source-IP limit, so disabling smart flow removes that protection — see D5), and
**`SMART_FLOW_CACHE_PATH = ~/.meraki/.cache/rate_limit_cache.json`** with a 7-day TTL, which writes
rate-limit state into `$HOME` and breaks or misplaces itself on a read-only root filesystem.
Measured scope: **141 raw `asyncio.to_thread` call sites**.

## D5 — The 100 req/s per-source-IP limit: documentation only, no code
A single process cannot know how many siblings share its NAT IP, so enforcement would be guessing.
Document the limit and its arithmetic in `docs/scaling-guide.md`, cap recommended **shards per egress
IP at ~8** at the default `shared_fraction`, and state that larger fleets must spread across egress
IPs or lower `shared_fraction`.

## D6 — Over-budget: explicit profile selection above a computed threshold
Above a threshold **computed from the solved plan versus budget** (not a raw network count, so it is
shape-aware), startup **fails unless `collectors.profile` is set explicitly**, naming the measured
demand and the options. Profiles: `availability` = priority 1 only, `standard` = priorities 1–3,
`full` = everything. **Inside** a chosen profile, if demand still exceeds budget, priority 1 and 2
keep their floors and priority 3/4 shed — the scheduler must **stop stretching priority 1/2**, which
is the actual defect (availability degrading to 480s, MT to 240s). `over_budget` and per-group skip
counters are exposed so it is alertable.

## D7 — `/ready` stays a startup gate; staleness becomes metrics
Document `/ready` as "initial collection completed". `/health` keeps the dead-man staleness check.
Add **per-collector and per-endpoint-group last-success age as Prometheus metrics** so alerting lives
in Prometheus, not a probe. Rationale for not making `/ready` freshness-based: a NotReady pod is
dropped from Service endpoints, so **Prometheus stops scraping and you lose the metrics that explain
the failure**, and a transient Meraki outage would stall or roll back deployments.

## D8 — Backoff scoped by domain; org-wide only on org-wide evidence
Each domain / endpoint group tracks its own failure streak and backs off independently. Org-wide
suppression fires only on **401/403 on any call, or connectivity failure spanning multiple domains**.
A **404 or 402 on an optional license-gated endpoint never counts toward any streak** — it means "not
licensed", which is permanent state, not a failure.

## D9 — `api_base_url`: HTTPS-only, allowlist by default, unconditional redirect credential strip
Reject plain `http`. Accept the five origins already in `KNOWN_REGION_BASE_URLS` silently; anything
else requires explicit `meraki.allow_custom_api_base_url: true`. **Independently and
unconditionally, never carry the `Authorization` header across an origin change on redirect** — that
path is attacker-influenced rather than operator-chosen. Narrows #590 without reversing it.

## D10 — Bad config: fail fast on provably-wrong, warn on merely-suboptimal
The real bug is the blanket `except` in `_startup_collections`: continuing is **correct for a
transient Meraki outage and wrong for a deterministic config error**. **Refuse to start:** zero-match
NetworkFilter; empty effective collector set; `collector_timeout` < `per_fetch_deadline_seconds`.
**Warn and run:** executor under-provisioned against admission; workable-but-unusual pacing.

## D11 — Helm resources: raise defaults to cover MEDIUM, document LARGE separately
Decoupled from D6's profiles deliberately. **The new default must come from the `MEDIUM` preset's
MEASURED RSS once D2's fixture runs, not from a judgement call** — otherwise 512Mi is replaced by
another number with nothing behind it.

## D12 — Client identifiers: never substitute a MAC, and scrub bodies
Delete the `client.id or client.mac` fallback. With no ID, emit the row with the identifier field
**omitted, not the row dropped**. When `include_identifiers=false`, **scrub MAC-shaped strings from
the message body too** — key-only filtering is the underlying bug.

## D13 — Webhooks: freshness window + TTL dedupe on alertId, and split the metrics
Reject payloads whose `sentAt` is outside a bounded, configurable window (sane floor for clock skew,
clear log on rejection). Bounded TTL cache keyed on `alertId` or body fingerprint; apply device state
**once per alert**. Emit `delivery_attempts_total` and `unique_alerts_total` **separately**, so
Meraki's legitimate retries stay visible while state transitions are idempotent.

## D14 — Scanner gating: split by determinism
**Merge gates** on change-scoped, stable scanners: `zizmor`, `actionlint`, `dependency-review`.
**Publish gates** on HIGH/CRITICAL from Trivy and CodeQL, with **the scan moved BEFORE
push/sign/attest**, plus a committed exception file carrying a reason and an **expiry date** per
accepted CVE. Gating everything on merge would stall the repo on third-party CVE disclosures and, on
a solo repo, predictably ends with the gate bypassed.

## D15 — A disposable instance, recorded corpus and fault-injection proxy
A throwaway containerised exporter against a **recorded Meraki response corpus**, with a proxy
injecting 429s, timeouts, TLS failures, HTML bodies, slow responses and connection resets on demand.
**Pinned by digest, never `:main`, watchtower-excluded.** No live org involvement — you cannot revoke
a working key to test revocation, but a proxy returns 401 all day. **Response shapes in the corpus
must come from real captures, never invented**, or the corpus encodes the same wrong assumption as
the code.

## D16 — Publish verification level per device family
Rewrite `docs/support-matrix.md` so each family carries **live-verified / spec-verified /
community-reported**, with the date and what was checked. Add an issue template soliciting sanitised
real responses — one response is all a fixture needs, and a user with an MX is likelier to paste JSON
into an issue than to grant org access.

## D17 — Doc generators: fail loudly instead of under-reporting
Parse failures **exit non-zero**. Delete the dead `CircuitBreaker` and `async_utils.py` exclusions.
Convert the "Found N…" eyeball check into **assertions**, and fail if `config.md`'s hardcoded
`nested_models` list diverges from the settings tree `.env.example` walks.

## D18 — "New device family" means a new product type
Six seams applies to a genuinely new Meraki **product type**. A new **model subtype of an existing
product** costs nothing structural — Catalyst/CS already routes through the MS collector. No fix
required.

# Corrections carried forward — do not re-derive these

- **The 60 HTTP 400s were NOT the exporter.** The Dashboard request audit log showed 59 were external
  `createOrganizationActionBatch` POSTs from a different consumer; the exporter issues no POSTs at
  all. The 60th was the audit's own deliberate malformed GET.
- **`meraki_org_api_requests_count` is a trailing-hour, ALL-CLIENT gauge**, not exporter lifetime
  volume. It cannot validate a calls-per-cycle model. This is what produced the finding that the
  exporter's own counter only increments in `OrganizationInventory._make_api_call`.
- **`scripts/CLAUDE.md` falsely denies the CI docs-drift gate exists.** It does exist and it was red
  for 20 consecutive runs (2026-08-10 → 2026-08-12) before being fixed in `ce03473`. Treat every
  in-repo `CLAUDE.md` as a claim to verify, not ground truth.
- **`CircuitBreaker` does not exist anywhere in this codebase.** `rg` returns zero hits, yet
  `scripts/generate_metrics_docs.py` still excludes it and excludes all of `async_utils.py` for a
  reason that evaporated with it.
- **Pushing to `main` redeploys the <soak-host> soak.** The host runs watchtower
  (`<watchtower-container>`), so a push rebuilds `ghcr.io/…:main`, watchtower pulls it, and the
  container restarts — which destroyed the 15-hour counters the audit was handed. Any future work
  depending on soak counters must pin a digest or snapshot first.
- **The audit's 2026-07-02 `evidence/` pack is <net-name-4>LE** (baseline `f08cd69`, spec 1.72.0, SDK 3.3.0;
  HEAD is 168 commits, spec 1.73.0, SDK 4.4.0 later). Use it to see what was already assessed, never
  as current truth.

# Phase plan

- [x] **P0 · Release boundary (security)** — fail-closed control plane, credential boundary,
      identifier leakage. Gates any customer release.
- [x] **P1 · API ownership** — one instrumented pacing facade, call-construction correctness, budget
      truth.
- [x] **P2 · Scheduler & resilience** — collection profiles, over-budget policy, domain-scoped
      backoff, error classification.
- [ ] **P3 · Fixtures & scale** — fixture generator with 7 presets, cardinality and concurrency
      bounds, measured sizing.
- [ ] **P4 · Lifecycle & failure harness** — disposable instance with fault injection, shutdown
      drain, config validation, anomaly investigation.
- [ ] **P5 · Truth & docs** — support-matrix honesty, generator strictness, docs corrections, scanner
      gating.

Post a **phase-completion comment** after each phase: issues closed with SHAs, anything re-scoped or
closed stale, deviations, anything parked. If context runs out mid-programme, the successor resumes
from this tracker plus its phase comments alone.

# Cross-phase dependencies

- **P3 fixture generator blocks the Helm resource default** — the new value must be the `MEDIUM`
  preset's measured RSS (D11), not a guess.
- **P4 disposable harness blocks the histogram-contradiction investigation** — source reading has
  already reached a dead end there, so only runtime observation resolves it.
- **P1's facade should land before P2's over-budget work** — the profile threshold is computed from
  demand, and until the facade instruments every call nobody can measure actual wire rate.

# The unresolved arithmetic worth restating

The audit filed the duration-histogram anomaly as "unexplained provenance". It is stronger than
that. Duration is observed **exactly once** per successful `collect()` (`core/collector.py:195-201`)
and `run_collector_once` **skips** when the per-collector lock is held (`manager.py:711`). Under both
facts, 1,560 runs × 69.5 s mean = **108,468 s of execution cannot fit 55,200 s of wall clock**. It is
provably impossible, so one of those three read facts is false — and each candidate (multiple
observations per run, a lock that does not serialise, a duration that includes queue wait) is its own
bug.

## Issue index — 28 deliverables, all 46 items mapped

Filed 2026-08-12. Milestones `V1.1-P0` … `V1.1-P5` (numbers 25–30) are the authoritative per-phase
worklist: `gh issue list --milestone "V1.1-P0 · Release boundary (security)" --state open`.

| Issue | Deliverable | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| **P0 · Release boundary** | | |
| #695 | Control POSTs fail closed; atomic forced-task admission; UI gates buttons | F-L8-01 |
| #697 | `api_base_url` HTTPS-only + allowlist + redirect credential strip | F-L8-02 |
| #696 | Never substitute MAC as `client.id`; scrub bodies | F-L8-03 |
| **P1 · API ownership** | | |
| #698 | One instrumented API facade; smart flow off; AST/lint gate | F-L1-01, F-L1-02, F-L1-03, F-L6-01, F-L5-03 |
| #699 | Call construction: `perPage`, page-aware cost, drop serial filters | F-L6-02, F-L6-03 |
| #700 | Budget truth: per-source-IP docs; verify burst default | N1, N2 |
| **P2 · Scheduler & resilience** | | |
| #701 | Collection profiles + over-budget policy protecting priority 1/2 | F-L2-01 |
| #702 | Scheduler/staleness metrics; `/ready` documented as startup gate | F-L2-03, F-L5-02 |
| #703 | Client child groups registered and costed only when enabled | F-L2-02 |
| #704 | Domain-scoped backoff; 404/402 never counts | F-L5-01 |
| #705 | Preserve error categories instead of erasing to `unknown` | F-L5-04 |
| #706 | Apply `validate_response_format` to the four bypassing fetches | F-L5-05 |
| **P3 · Fixtures & scale** | | |
| #707 | Fleet fixture generator + 7 presets + CI tiering | F-L9-07, F-L9-08 |
| #708 | Bound client application cardinality (top-N + `other`) | F-L4-02 |
| #709 | Bound DNS fan-out; disclose reverse DNS | F-L3-02, F-L8-05 |
| #710 | Concurrency admission: back-pressure, executor alignment, queue visibility | F-L3-01, F-L3-04 |
| #711 | Cardinality-endpoint honesty; client-store map eviction | F-L4-03, F-L4-04 |
| #712 | Helm resource defaults from a measured MEDIUM fleet | F-L7-01, F-L4-01 |
| **P4 · Lifecycle & failure harness** | | |
| #713 | Disposable instance + recorded corpus + fault-injection proxy | (D15) |
| #714 | Deterministic shutdown drain; Helm grace cross-check | F-L3-03, F-L7-02 |
| #715 | Webhook freshness window, replay dedupe, split metrics | F-L8-04 |
| #716 | Startup validation: fail fast on provably-wrong config | F-L7-03, F-L7-06 |
| #717 | Investigate the duration-histogram arithmetic | ANOM-1 |
| **P5 · Truth & docs** | | |
| #718 | Support matrix states a verification level per family | (D16) |
| #719 | Doc generators fail loudly rather than under-report | F-L9-06, F-L9-05 |
| #720 | Docs corrections batch | F-L9-01, F-L9-02, F-L9-03, F-L9-04, F-L7-04, F-L7-05 |
| #721 | Merge gates on change-scoped scanners; publish gates on severity | F-L8-06 |
| #722 | Record the extension-cost measurement (documentation only) | F-L7-07 |

**Coverage check:** 43 audit findings + N1 + N2 + ANOM-1 = **46 items**, every one named in exactly one
row above. Nothing was dropped, merged away silently, or left unfiled.

## Hard sequencing

- **#698 before #701** — the profile threshold is computed from demand, and until every call is metered the demand figure is an estimate.
- **#707 before #712** — the Helm default must be the `MEDIUM` preset's measured RSS, not a judgement call. Otherwise 512Mi is replaced by another number with nothing behind it.
- **#713 before #717** — source reading has already reached a dead end on the histogram contradiction, and the original 15-hour container no longer exists.
- **#713 before the failure-injection acceptance criteria in #714, #715 and #716.**

Everything else is independent and may be worked in any order within its phase.

## Wave 1 completion

All twelve scoped issues are closed on `main`: #695 `40e24f8`, #696 `2d73c8d`, #697 `ca8b938`, #698 `1997aec`, #700 `d5adf5b`, #707 `fa76729`, #711 `349e8ed`, #715 `26813ed`, #718 `15da33c`, #719 `0410fc2`, #720 `61e49fe`, #722 `6d03473`. Final formatting-only head: `83836565a9f12d8e88ab12891453020d83751131`.

Exact-head CI run `31643561709` is green. Local integration passed Ruff, mypy across 121 source files, and 2,626 tests; docgen reproduced zero diff. The AST gate was proven negative by deliberately adding a raw SDK call and observing `test_698_no_raw_sdk_thread_calls_outside_facade` fail at `collectors/config.py:278`, then restoring it green.

Deviations/findings: generated seam docs landed in the pre-fan-out seam commit to keep Helm drift checks coherent; #715 retains its #713-harness checkbox because #713 is deliberately deferred, while its focused duplicate-delivery test proves two attempts and one state application; initial exact-head CI `31643397135` exposed two unformatted fixture files, repaired by formatting-only commit `8383656`. L9 found and this wave fixed an empty-token auth bypass, MAC-shaped allowed-attribute/dotted-form leakage, and default-port origin normalization. One LOW remains: configured-token native UI buttons issue POSTs without an Authorization header, so the server safely returns 401 but the buttons are not directly usable without external header injection.

P0 is complete and ticked. P1 remains unticked because #699 is intentionally deferred even though #698 and #700 landed. Nothing was parked. No Meraki API calls or <soak-host> operations were performed.

# Wave 2 plan, and four decisions frozen on top of D1–D18

Wave 1 closed twelve issues (#695–#698, #700, #707, #711, #715, #718–#720, #722) at
`83836565a9f12d8e88ab12891453020d83751131`, CI green. Its report is reviewed; every load-bearing
claim spot-checked held up.

## Four issues filed from the wave-1 review

| Issue | Severity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| #723 | Real gap | `core/discovery.py` makes four SDK calls via raw `asyncio.to_thread`, outside the #698 facade **and outside its AST gate's `_OWNED_ROOTS`** — so startup traffic is unmetered, unpaced, and AIMD never sees a discovery 429 |
| #724 | Real gap | `make check` is `lint typecheck test` and `lint` is `ruff check` only — **no `ruff format --check`**, so the local gate can pass where CI fails. This is not theoretical: it caused wave 1's red CI run `31643397135` and the repair commit `8383656` |
| #725 | LOW → decided | Wave 1's own open question: with a token configured the control buttons render **enabled** but the page sends no `Authorization` header, so they always 401 |
| #726 | LOW | `product_series` counts exporter self-instrumentation as product data. Verified live: `product_series 4829` + `self_series 6` = `exposed_series 4835`, reconciling exactly with the scrape — but **891** of those samples are `meraki_exporter_*`, so ~885 (~18%) are attributed as product data. The reconciliation #711 delivered is correct; only the naming is wrong |

## Decisions frozen for wave 2

**W2-1 — the control UI hides its buttons entirely when a token is configured; controls are
API-only.** Extends D1 to the configured-token case. Rejected, and not to be re-litigated: a browser
unlock field holding the token in JS memory (any XSS exfiltrates an operator secret), and a login
with HttpOnly cookie plus CSRF (disproportionate security surface for a convenience button). Docs
carry the authenticated `curl` instead.

**W2-2 — wave 2 is two-phase, and the P4 cluster is wave 3.** Forced by measured contention, not by
priority. Joining any two issues that must edit the same file collapses **ten of the twelve remaining
code issues into one connected component** via `scheduler.py` → `app.py` → `clients.py` →
`organization.py` → `device.py` → `error_handling.py`. Wave 1's one-issue-per-lane model cannot fan
out here, so wave 2's lanes own **file territories** and the two genuinely cross-territory issues
(#703, #710) are sequenced into a Phase B that inherits those files. #713 builds the harness #714,
#716 and #717 consume, so including them would idle three lanes behind it.

title: Tracker: v1.1 production-hardening programme (adversarial audit burndown)

body:
## Problem

The daily lane is noisy in a way that trains us to ignore it. #686 is the worked example: opened
2026-08-06, then a comment every single day (08-07, 08-08, 08-09, 08-10, 08-11) — five near-identical
69-row tables — for drift that needed no action at all.

Three distinct causes.

### 1. There is no acknowledge path for apidrift findings

`spec/oasdiff-ignore.txt` lets us accept a known oasdiff change. **apidrift has no equivalent.** Any
`WARNING`/`BREAKING` finding we have consciously decided not to act on gates the build (exit 3) and
holds the tracking issue open forever, with no way to say "known, accepted, stop telling me".

Re-vendoring the baseline is the only lever, and it is too blunt — it silences *everything*,
including drift we have not looked at yet.

### 2. The report is re-posted verbatim every day

`.github/actions/report-drift/action.yml` runs `gh issue comment` unconditionally whenever an issue
is already open. Nothing compares the new report against the last one, so an unchanged drift state
produces a new comment every 24h and the real signal (something *changed*) is buried in repetition.

### 3. The report leads with boilerplate

Of the 69 findings in the current report, 33 are `INFO derived` ("computed model, not API-mapped") —
one per derived model, on every run, forever. They are a coverage-accounting artefact, not news.
Anything actionable is below the fold.

## Approach

**Acknowledge file.** Add `spec/apidrift-ignore.txt`, same conventions as the oasdiff one
(one substring per line, `#` comments, case-insensitive). Wire it as `--ignore PATH`. A matched
finding is not deleted — it is downgraded to `INFO` with `-acknowledged` appended to its kind, so it
stays visible in the report but stops gating. Deleting it outright would make an accepted risk
invisible, which is how accepted risks get forgotten.

Match against a normalized `kind|op|detail` line so an entry can be as coarse as a kind
(`op-deprecated`) or as precise as one operation.

**Fingerprint the report.** Have `report-drift` embed `<!-- drift-fingerprint: <sha256> -->` in the
issue body and, on each run, compare the incoming report's fingerprint against the open issue's:

- unchanged → **update nothing, post no comment** (the issue body already states current reality)
- changed → rewrite the body with the current report and post a comment saying it changed

Net effect: the issue body is always the current state, and a comment means something actually moved.

**Lead with what matters.** In `render_markdown`, emit actionable findings in their own table first,
then collapse routine INFO into a `<details>` block with per-kind counts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `spec/apidrift-ignore.txt` exists (documented, empty apart from comments)
- [ ] `--ignore` wired into `__main__.py`; matched findings become `INFO <kind>-acknowledged` and do
      not gate; unit-tested incl. comment/blank-line handling and case-insensitivity
- [ ] An acknowledged `WARNING` yields exit 0; an unacknowledged one still yields exit 3
- [ ] `report-drift` posts no comment when the fingerprint is unchanged, updates body + comments when
      it changes
- [ ] `resolve-drift` still auto-closes on a fully clean run
- [ ] `render_markdown` puts actionable findings first, routine INFO in a collapsed block
- [ ] `tools/apidrift/CLAUDE.md` documents the ignore file and the fingerprint behaviour
- [ ] `make check` green

## Related

- #686 — the tracker whose comment spam prompted this
- #690 — added `op-deprecated`, the first finding kind likely to want acknowledging

body:
## Context

Spec 1.73.0 added two properties to the `getNetworkWirelessSsids` response (found while assessing
the #686 drift report). Assessed both for exporter value. **Decision: consume neither.** Recorded so
it is not re-litigated when the fields resurface in a future drift diff.

## How the endpoint is used today

`getNetworkWirelessSsids` is consumed in exactly one place — `collectors/devices/mr/firewall.py:163`
— purely to enumerate SSIDs so L3/L7 firewall rules can be fetched for the enabled ones. The
`WirelessSsid` model (`core/domain_models.py:1096`) pins only `number`, `name`, `enabled`. The
exporter exports **no SSID configuration metrics at all**, so either field would mean opening a new
config-info metric surface, not extending an existing one.

## `wlanIdentifier` (integer)

> "WLAN identifier for the SSID. Only present for Meraki admin users."

Rejected. "Meraki admin users" means Cisco-internal accounts, not customer org admins. The field
will be absent for every API key this exporter will ever run under, so a metric built on it would be
empty for 100% of users. Nothing to gain even in principle — it is an internal identifier, not
telemetry.

## `campusGateway` (object)

> "Campus gateway settings. Only present when ipAssignmentMode is 'Campus Gateway'."
> Sole content: `cluster.id` — "The campus gateway cluster ID used when the ipAssignmentMode is
> 'Campus Gateway'."

Rejected. Three reasons:

1. **No operational signal.** The object carries one opaque cluster identifier. No state, no health,
   no counter — nothing that changes at scrape cadence. It is config identity, which per the repo's
   boundary rule belongs nowhere near a Prometheus gauge unless it is joining something we already
   export. We export no SSID config series for it to join.
2. **Present only for a niche deployment mode.** Conditional on `ipAssignmentMode == 'Campus
   Gateway'`, absent for every other SSID. Adding a metric that is empty for most orgs and carries
   one label value for the rest is not worth the surface.
3. **It would be the thin end of an SSID-config metric wedge.** If we ever want SSID configuration
   exported, that is its own design (which fields, what cardinality, info-metric vs gauges) — not
   something to backdoor via one conditional field.

## Reversal conditions

Revisit `campusGateway` only if the exporter grows a deliberate SSID-configuration metric surface,
**and** campus gateway state (not just the cluster ID) becomes available. `wlanIdentifier` should
not be revisited at all while the "Meraki admin users" restriction stands.

## Related

- #686 — drift report where both fields surfaced

comments.body: Closing as the decision itself — no work to do. Both fields assessed and rejected; rationale and reversal conditions are in the body.

body:
## Problem

All five `/devices/{serial}/camera/analytics/*` operations are marked `deprecated: true` in the
Meraki OpenAPI spec (1.72.0 and 1.73.0 — pre-existing, not new drift). The exporter consumes two of
them in `collectors/devices/mv.py`:

| consumed op | used for | metric |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` | zone config + names | `meraki_mv_analytics_zones`, `meraki_mv_zone_info` |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` | per-zone person count | `meraki_mv_people_count` |

Deprecated operations page: <https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api-v1/deprecated-operations/>

No removal date is published, and the spec carries no `x-sunset` or replacement pointer — only a
generic `x-deprecation-notice`. So this is not urgent, but it is a known future `BREAKING
missing-op` and should be planned rather than discovered.

## Replacement surface

The org-level boundaries + detections API is the successor. None of it is deprecated:

| deprecated | replacement | params |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` | `getOrganizationCameraBoundariesAreasByDevice` | `organizationId` (req), `serials` (opt) |
| | `getOrganizationCameraBoundariesLinesByDevice` | `organizationId` (req), `serials` (opt) |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` | `getOrganizationCameraDetectionsHistoryByBoundaryByInterval` | `organizationId`, `boundaryIds`, `ranges` (all req); `duration`, `perPage`, `boundaryTypes` (opt) |

Two things make this attractive beyond just clearing the deprecation:

1. **It is org-wide bulk, replacing per-device loops.** Today `_collect_analytics_zones` and
   `_collect_analytics_recent` each fire once per camera. Boundaries collapse to one (or two) calls
   per org. That is the direction the roadmap workflow explicitly prefers for rate-limit budget.
2. Boundaries come back already keyed by `networkId` + `serial`, so the existing zone-info join
   carrier maps over cleanly.

## The blocker: this is not a drop-in, the metric semantics change

`getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` returns `averageCount` per zone — an **occupancy gauge**
("how many people are in this zone now"), which is what `meraki_mv_people_count` exposes
(`mv.py:531`).

`getOrganizationCameraDetectionsHistoryByBoundaryByInterval` returns, per boundary per interval,
`{startTime, endTime, objectType, in, out}` — **directional crossing counts over a window**. That is
flow, not occupancy. There is no field that reproduces `averageCount`.

So the migration cannot preserve `meraki_mv_people_count` as-is. Options, needs a decision:

- **A.** Replace the gauge with in/out counters (`meraki_mv_boundary_detections_in_total` /
  `_out_total`). Honest to the new data, but a breaking metric change for anyone with a dashboard or
  alert on `meraki_mv_people_count`, and net occupancy would have to be derived (cumulative in-out,
  which drifts).
- **B.** Keep `meraki_mv_people_count` alive on the deprecated endpoint until Cisco removes it, and
  add the boundary counters alongside as the forward path. Costs a period of dual collection.
- **C.** Migrate only the zones/config half now (`getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` →
  boundaries/areas+lines, a genuine like-for-like with a bulk-call win) and defer the
  `recent` → `detections` decision until a sunset date is announced.

**C is the recommendation** — it takes the free win, removes one of the two deprecated
dependencies, and does not force a metric-semantics decision before it is needed.

Two further unknowns to verify live before implementing the detections half (a working homelab key
is in the gitignored `.env`):

- `boundaryIds` is **required**, so detections needs a two-phase fetch (boundaries first, then
  detections keyed by the IDs returned). Confirm the practical cap — `perPage` maxes at 1000, but
  the limit on `boundaryIds` per request is not documented.
- `ranges` is required and its item shape is not described in the spec beyond "a list of time
  ranges with intervals". Confirm against the live API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded on A / B / C
- [ ] Live-verify boundaries + detections response shapes against the homelab org
- [ ] `ranges` item shape and any `boundaryIds` cap documented in `evidence/`
- [ ] If C: `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` replaced by the boundaries ops, per-camera loop removed,
      `meraki_mv_analytics_zones` / `meraki_mv_zone_info` preserved
- [ ] Pydantic models carry `__meraki_op__` for whichever new ops land
- [ ] `make check` green; docs regenerated if metrics changed

## Related

- #686 — drift tracker where the deprecation surfaced
- #690 — apidrift will start reporting these as `INFO op-deprecated` once merged

comments.body:
## Decision: option A — migrate both halves now, accept the metric-semantics break

Rob, 2026-08-11:

> I think for 691 we can break the network semantics as unless meraki announces the sunset with
> many weeks notice we will likely miss it and things will break?

Correct, and that reasoning holds up: there is no `x-sunset` field in the spec, no removal date on
the deprecated-operations page, and the only notification channel is the daily drift lane — which
tells us the op is **gone** (`BREAKING missing-op`), not that it is *going*. By then
`meraki_mv_people_count` is already broken in production. Taking the break on our own schedule is
strictly better than taking it on Cisco's.

This supersedes the option-C recommendation in the body.

### Scope

- Replace `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` with `getOrganizationCameraBoundariesAreasByDevice` +
  `getOrganizationCameraBoundariesLinesByDevice` (org-wide bulk; removes the per-camera loop).
- Replace `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` with
  `getOrganizationCameraDetectionsHistoryByBoundaryByInterval`.
- **`meraki_mv_people_count` is removed**, not reinterpreted. Its occupancy semantics cannot be
  reproduced from in/out crossing counts, and silently rebinding the name to different maths would
  be worse than deleting it — existing dashboards and alerts would keep working while quietly
  meaning something else.
- New counters carry crossing semantics honestly. Zone→boundary is a rename of the concept, so
  `meraki_mv_zone_info` / `meraki_mv_analytics_zones` are renamed to boundary equivalents rather
  than kept as aliases.
- Removal + renames documented as a breaking change in the release notes.

### Still to verify live before implementing (homelab key in the gitignored `.env`)

- `ranges` item shape — required, and the spec describes it only as "a list of time ranges with
  intervals".
- Practical cap on `boundaryIds` per request (undocumented; `perPage` maxes at 1000).
- Whether area and line boundaries share an ID namespace, which decides whether detections needs
  one call or two.

## Blocked: implementation needs a working API key

Decision is settled (option A above), but the code cannot be written yet.

**The `.env` key is dead.** `getOrganizations` returns `401 Unauthorized — No valid authentication
method found`. So none of the live verification in the checklist can be done, and this repo's own
rule (root `CLAUDE.md`: the OpenAPI spec is wrong for some endpoints, verify live before coding)
applies squarely here.

**`ranges` cannot be safely inferred.** Sources disagree on how to encode it:

| source | says |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAPI 1.73.0 | `ranges` (array), required, described only as "A list of time ranges with intervals" |
| SDK 4.4.0 signature | `ranges: list`, docstring repeats the spec verbatim |
| developer.cisco.com MV Sense REST API page | `boundaryIds` comma-separated, plus separate `interval` / `startTime` / `endTime` query params — **no `ranges` at all** |
| developer.cisco.com whats-new v1.43.0 | confirms the response shape (`boundaryId`, `type`, `results{startTime,endTime,objectType,in,out}`) but not the request |

The MV Sense page appears to predate the `ranges` form. Guessing between "array of
`{startTime,endTime,resolution}` objects" and the older flat triple is exactly the kind of thing that
either 400s or silently returns an empty array — the latter being worse, since it would look like a
working collector reporting zero detections.

Also noted while reading: a `counterMode` parameter was added to this endpoint (whats-new v1.62.0)
and is **not** in the vendored 1.73.0 spec's parameter list. Worth checking what it does when the
key works — it may be directly relevant to whether we can recover an occupancy-like signal.

### To unblock

A working API key for an org that has at least one MV camera with a configured boundary. Then, in
one session: confirm the `ranges` encoding, the `boundaryIds` cap, whether area and line boundaries
share an ID namespace, and what `counterMode` accepts.

Everything else on this issue is ready to go the moment that lands.

## 2026-08-14 capability-gate refresh — still blocked at authentication

The bounded read-only gate made exactly one Meraki GET: `getOrganizations` (no organization is configured locally). It returned `401 Unauthorized`. Per the stop rule, the run made zero network, device, boundary, detection, or raw `counterMode` requests. No key or Meraki identifier was printed or retained.

Several earlier documentation premises are now stale or contradictory, which makes live verification more important rather than less:

- Current OpenAPI 1.73 and Cisco's current MV Sense page document `ranges` items with `startTime`, `endTime`, and `interval`: https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/mv-sense/rest-api/
- Cisco's current example uses nested `ranges[][startTime]`/`[endTime]`/`[interval]`, but SDK 4.4.0's installed array-of-objects encoder produces `ranges[]startTime`. A real request is required before trusting that encoding.
- Cisco's v1.62/current whats-new material says optional `counterMode` was added, while current OpenAPI 1.73, the current operation page, and SDK 4.4.0 omit it: https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/whats-new/v1-62-0/
- Cisco examples show list-shaped boundary and result collections where current OpenAPI response schemas say object. The live envelope must drive the models.
- `boundaryIds` limits remain undocumented. An organization with N configured boundaries can prove only that at least N work, not the server maximum.

The option-A product decision remains binding. Implementation is parked because the required live facts are still unavailable: boundary response envelopes, mixed area/line behavior, usable `ranges` encoding, practical ID batching, and `counterMode` behavior.

Resume boundary: provide a working read-only key for an organization with at least one configured MV boundary, then rerun the bounded gate: auth -> filtered inventory -> area/line boundary GETs -> one 15-minute SDK detection GET -> baseline/true/false raw `counterMode` GETs. Only sanitized type/key/count evidence should be retained.

2026-08-14 capability re-check: the configured read-only credential is valid, but the available organisation has 0 camera devices, 0 area boundaries and 0 line boundaries. No identifier or payload was retained.

Current documentation/spec research now resolves one old unknown: `ranges` items are `{startTime, endTime, interval}`. The remaining wire contract is still not safe to implement without a capable org: SDK 4.4.0 appears to encode the nested keys differently from the current documented bracket form; `counterMode` is mentioned in a v1.62 whats-new entry but is absent from the current 1.73 spec and SDK; boundary-ID namespace/cap and the detections response still need live proof.

The blocker is therefore narrower than the 2026-08-11 comment: provide read-only access to any organisation with at least one MV camera and a configured area or line boundary. Then one bounded session can verify the exact SDK wire form, boundary IDs/cap, `counterMode`, and response shape before implementation. No code change is being guessed from an empty organisation.

title: MV: plan migration off the deprecated camera analytics endpoints

body:
## Problem

Two gaps in `tools/apidrift/conformance.py`, both found while assessing #686.

### 1. The `deprecated` flag is never read

The spec marks 13 operations `deprecated: true`. Two of them are consumed by this exporter:

| operationId | path | deprecated in 1.72.0 | deprecated in 1.73.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` | `GET /devices/{serial}/camera/analytics/recent` | yes | yes |
| `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` | `GET /devices/{serial}/camera/analytics/zones` | yes | yes |

apidrift never looks at `deprecated`, so neither has ever appeared in a drift report. The exporter
will keep calling them until Cisco removes the endpoints, at which point the daily lane fires a
`BREAKING missing-op` with no prior warning. Deprecated ops also carry `x-deprecation-notice`
(the only `x-` extension in the whole spec) pointing at
<https://developer.cisco.com/meraki/api-v1/deprecated-operations/>.

A model-scoped check would be insufficient: `CameraAnalyticsRecentZone` is defined in
`collectors/devices/mv.py:77`, and `models.conformance_models()` only collects models declared in
`core/api_models.py` + `core/domain_models.py`. So `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` has no
registered model and would be missed. The check must run over the **scanner's consumed-op set**,
which `__main__.py:main()` already computes.

### 2. Untyped responses produce misleading `model-extra` findings

`getOrganizationApplianceSecurityEvents` has a 2xx schema of `{type: object, additionalProperties:
...}` — the spec describes no properties at all. `response_properties()` returns that schema,
`_union_properties()` finds an empty `properties` map, and `check_models()` then reports every
model field as `INFO model-extra` "not in any mapped op response". Currently three findings
(`ApplianceSecurityEvent.ts`, `.eventType`, `.networkId`) that read as "our model is stale" when
the truth is "the spec does not describe this response".

This is the only consumed op affected today (verified across all 109), but the noise is
actively misleading and will recur for any future free-form endpoint.

## Approach

### Deprecation

Add `check_deprecated_operations(consumed, baseline, live)` to `conformance.py`, called from
`main()` where the consumed set and both specs are already in hand. Split severity along the
tool's existing baseline-vs-live axis:

- `INFO op-deprecated` — deprecated in **both** baseline and live. Pre-existing backlog, visible
  in the report, non-gating.
- `WARNING op-newly-deprecated` — deprecated in live but **not** in the baseline. This is real
  drift and the moment a human should act, so it gates (exit 3) and opens the tracking issue.

This deliberately mirrors how the rest of the tool works: re-vendoring the baseline is the
acknowledge path, and it naturally downgrades a `WARNING op-newly-deprecated` to `INFO
op-deprecated` on the next run.

Rationale for not making all deprecations WARNING: the two camera ops have been deprecated for at
least two spec versions, so a permanent WARNING would hold the tracker open forever and train us to
ignore it. Rationale for not making them all INFO: the daily workflow only posts a report when exit
is 3 or oasdiff is 1 (`.github/workflows/api-drift.yml:89-95`), so an INFO-only deprecation would
never be surfaced at all.

Filter the consumed set through the live spec's operationIds before checking, the same way
`missing-op` is filtered against `baseline_ops`, so scanner false positives (`api`, `serial`) can
never produce a finding.

### Untyped responses

In `_union_properties()` / `check_models()`, detect an op whose response schema has no
`properties` but is a free-form object (`additionalProperties` present, or bare `type: object`).
Emit a single `INFO spec-untyped` finding for that op and suppress the per-field `model-extra`
findings sourced from it. A model whose ops are *all* untyped gets exactly one finding instead of
one per field.

Keep type-checking behaviour unchanged — there are no spec types to check against.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check_deprecated_operations()` added, unit-tested for: deprecated in both (INFO), newly
      deprecated (WARNING), not deprecated (no finding), consumed-but-absent-from-spec (no finding)
- [ ] Wired into `main()`; findings appear in both md and json output
- [ ] `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsRecent` + `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` report `INFO op-deprecated`
      against the current vendored 1.73.0 baseline (exit stays 0)
- [ ] `spec-untyped` collapses the three `ApplianceSecurityEvent` `model-extra` findings to one
- [ ] `x-deprecation-notice` / the deprecated-operations URL surfaced in the finding detail
- [ ] `tools/apidrift/CLAUDE.md` documents both new finding kinds and the severity split
- [ ] `make api-conformance` exit 0; `uv run pytest tools/apidrift/tests` green

## Related

- #686 — the drift tracker this was found under

title: Meraki OpenAPI drift on consumed operations

body:
The metric should return one line per AP, but only returns a single line. The root cause is the missing serial label in the device_lookup dictionary (line 859 in device.py). Without serial, all APs have identical label sets, so Prometheus deduplicates them into a single aggregated value. You have 3 APs with 5+3+7 clients, but see only one line.

Solution: Add "serial": serial, to the device_lookup dictionary (line 860), so each AP gets unique labels and returns as a separate metric line.

Impact: You're measuring the SUM of all APs in the network instead of per-AP granularity—critical for monitoring individual AP health.

comments.body:
This same issue affects other device-level MR metrics that use create_device_labels() - To check

Probably affected metrics:

- meraki_mr_clients_connected 
- meraki_mr_connection_stats_count 
- meraki_mr_packet_loss_* 
- meraki_mr_packets_* 
- meraki_mr_cpu_load 
- meraki_mr_power_* 
- meraki_mr_radio_* 
- meraki_mr_port_* 
- meraki_mr_signal_rssi_dbm 
- meraki_mr_signal_snr_db 
- meraki_mr_ssid_*

Fixed in afe2562 (pushed to `main`).

## Root cause

The reported line number was close but the mechanism was slightly different from the issue body. `create_device_labels()` already reads `serial` from `device.get("serial", "")` — the problem was upstream: the shared `device_lookup` dict built in `DeviceCollector._collect_org_devices` (`collectors/device.py`) never included a `"serial"` key (only `name`, `model`, `network_id`, `network_name`, `device_type`).

Consumers feed each lookup entry straight into `create_device_labels()`, so every lookup-matched device got `serial=""`. Identical label sets → Prometheus collapsed all APs in a network into a single aggregated series.

## Scope (confirming @DarkPsionix)

The suspicion in the comment was correct — this was never `meraki_mr_clients_connected`-specific. Every consumer of this shared lookup that fed it to `create_device_labels()` **without locally stamping serial** was affected:

- `meraki_mr_clients_connected` (`mr/clients.py`)
- `meraki_mr_connection_stats_*` (`mr/clients.py`)
- `meraki_mr_power_*` / `meraki_mr_port_*` / PoE / link-aggregation (`mr/performance.py` ethernet status)

Interestingly, four *other* sites had already worked around this locally (`mr/wireless.py`, `mr/performance.py` power-mode, `mr/performance.py` packet-loss, `ms.py` STP — the last with an explicit F-174 comment documenting the exact missing-`serial` behaviour), which is why the radio/SSID/STP metrics were fine.

## Fix

Add `"serial": serial` to the lookup dict at the source (one place fixes every consumer). The pre-existing per-consumer workarounds are now redundant but harmless, so left in place as defence for the lookup-miss fallback. Updated the stale F-174 comment in `ms.py`.

## Why the tests missed it

The MR sub-collector unit tests hand-built `device_lookup` entries that already carried `serial`, masking the coordinator bug. Added a regression test that exercises the **real** `_collect_org_devices` lookup-building path with 3 APs (client counts 5/3/7) and asserts three distinct per-serial series.

`make check` green: 2544 passed, ruff + mypy clean.

**Thank you so much for this fix!** 🎉

Following this correction, **the new version is working wonderfully**. The meraki_mr_clients_connected metrics now correctly return one line per AP, which finally allows us to monitor each access point individually with the necessary granularity.

A **huge thanks** for the quick correction and for the **fantastic work** you continue to do on this Meraki exporter. It is truly appreciated!

body:
## Summary

`service.version` is set on the **OTLP metrics resource** (the MeterProvider's `Resource`), so it is promoted to a `service_version` **label on every emitted metric series**. Per the OpenTelemetry → Prometheus compatibility spec this is a deviation: version belongs on an **info metric** (`target_info` from the resource, or a `*_build_info` gauge), never as a label on ordinary series.

## The standard

Only `service.name` (+ `service.namespace`) → `job` and `service.instance.id` → `instance` are meant to become labels. **Every other resource attribute — including `service.version` — goes to a `target_info` metric** (OpenMetrics 1.0 convention). Promoting a resource attribute to per-series labels is a documented, non-default opt-in.

Consequence of putting version on every series: **each new build mints a whole new series set.** After a redeploy, the old-version and new-version series coexist for the query-lookback window, so any `sum`-style panel adds both → a transient multiplier; and active-series cardinality grows with the number of versions ever seen. This was found loudly on `graph2otel` (which runs a per-commit `:main` image) — see rknightion/graph2otel#104 for the full spec analysis. Repos on stable release tags hit the cardinality growth but rarely see the doubling.

## Change

- Keep `service.version` on the OTel **resource** (semconv-correct → flows to `target_info`).
- Stop it becoming a per-series label: rely on the existing `*_build_info{version=...}` gauge (and/or `target_info`) for version, joined via `group_left` where a panel needs it.
- Audit dashboards/alerts for any query that aggregates over or filters on `service_version` and repoint them at the info metric.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `service_version` no longer appears as a label on ordinary metric series (only on `target_info` / `*_build_info`)
- [x] Version stays queryable via the build-info gauge (+ a documented `group_left` example)
- [x] Dashboards/alerts updated if any referenced `service_version`
- [x] Note the OTLP→Prometheus resource-attribute convention in the telemetry setup docs

Cross-repo consistency pass with rknightion/graph2otel#104 (detailed spec citations there). Sibling issues: tailscale2otel#187, opnsense-exporter#270.

comments.body:
Completed by ae4ea9a.

The exporter-side premise was stale: `build_otel_resource()` correctly retains `service.version` on the OTLP Resource, `_number_point()` builds ordinary data-point attributes only from the source Prometheus sample labels, and `MetricsData` keeps the Resource separate from those points. No exporter-side resource-to-series promotion exists. `meraki_exporter_build_info{version,commit}` is already registered and queryable.

Current primary documentation confirms the boundary:

- OpenTelemetry Prometheus compatibility maps Resource attributes to `target_info`, with service name/namespace and instance ID becoming `job`/`instance`: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/compatibility/prometheus_and_openmetrics.md
- The Collector documents `target_info` and the standard `on(job, instance) group_left(...) target_info` join; `resource_to_telemetry_conversion.enabled` is the explicit promotion path: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/exporter/prometheusexporter/README.md
- Prometheus defaults `promote_resource_attributes` to `[]` and `promote_all_resource_attributes` to `false`: https://prometheus.io/docs/operating/configuration/

The documentation now contains literal `target_info` and `meraki_exporter_build_info` joins and explains that an ordinary `service_version` label is downstream receiver translation, not exporter payload behavior. Consumer audit found no alert or query filtering/aggregating on `service_version`; three dashboard occurrences only hide that column on scrape-path tables.

Verification: `make check` passed Ruff, Ruff format, mypy over 121 source files, and 2,684 tests with the one pre-existing Starlette/httpx warning.

title: Don't promote service.version to a per-series metric label (OTLP→Prometheus: version belongs on target_info/build_info)

body:
## Problem

Every Renovate uv bump breaks CI. Most recent: PR #651 (`0.11.26` → `0.11.28`), [run 29320434696](https://github.com/rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter/actions/runs/29320434696) — `docker-build-test` failed at the uv install step's `sha256sum -c -` gate.

The cause is structural, not a one-off. The Dockerfile pins uv two ways that Renovate cannot keep in sync:

- `ARG UV_VERSION` — tracked by Renovate's `github-releases` datasource, so it bumps.
- `ARG UV_CHECKSUM_AMD64` / `ARG UV_CHECKSUM_ARM64` — hand-pinned tarball hashes. Renovate has no way to compute these, so they go stale the moment the version bumps.

The Dockerfile comment already acknowledges this and points at `make docker-uv-checksums` as the manual refresh step. That works (it fails loudly rather than silently installing an unverified uv, which is the #562 property we want), but it means **every uv bump PR is red until a human intervenes**, and Renovate automerge can never carry one through.

## Proposal

Use the official uv image with a digest pin — [uv's own documented](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/) supply-chain-hardened install method:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.28@sha256:0f36cb9361a3346885ca3677e3767016687b5a170c1a6b88465ec14aefec90aa /uv /uvx /bin/
```

This is strictly better on both axes:

- **Security (#562 preserved, arguably strengthened).** The `@sha256:` digest is an immutable content address for the entire image, committed in the repo rather than fetched at build time alongside the artefact it would be checking. Same guarantee the two `FROM python:...@sha256:` pins already rely on.
- **Automation.** Renovate's built-in `dockerfile` manager natively tracks `COPY --from` image refs and updates **tag and digest atomically in one commit**. Bumps land green, unattended. This is the same mechanism the `FROM` lines already use — the Dockerfile comment on the `FROM` line notes it works there; the uv `ARG` only missed out because it lives outside a `FROM` line.
- **Simplification.** `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` is a multi-arch index (verified: `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`, matching exactly the arches we support), so the whole `TARGETARCH` case block disappears along with the `curl`/`sha256sum`/`tar`/`install` chain and the `UV_VERSION=latest` guard. Roughly 30 lines become 1.

## Scope

- `Dockerfile` — replace the uv install block.
- `Makefile` — remove the now-dead `docker-uv-checksums` target (#562's manual helper).
- Check whether `builder` still needs `curl` in its apt install list once the tarball fetch is gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dockerfile installs uv via `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:<ver>@sha256:<digest>`
- [ ] `UV_VERSION`, `UV_CHECKSUM_AMD64`, `UV_CHECKSUM_ARM64` ARGs and the `TARGETARCH` case block are gone
- [ ] `make docker-uv-checksums` removed; no dangling references to it (Dockerfile comments, docs)
- [ ] `docker-build-test` green on both the amd64 CI build and a local arm64 build
- [ ] `uv --version` in the built image reports the pinned version
- [ ] A subsequent Renovate uv bump updates tag + digest together and goes green with no manual step

comments.body:
Done in 8bacd50.

uv is now installed via `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.28@sha256:0f36cb93...` — uv's own documented hardened install method. The `UV_VERSION`/`UV_CHECKSUM_*` ARGs, the `TARGETARCH` case block, the curl/sha256sum/tar chain, the `latest` guard, the `make docker-uv-checksums` target, and the custom regex manager in `renovate.json` are all gone. `curl` also dropped out of the builder's apt list along with its only caller.

Verified:

- Full image builds locally (arm64); `Docker Security` built it green on amd64 in CI.
- `uv --version` in the image reports `0.11.28`.
- Container serves `GET /health` and `GET /metrics` (both 200) under CI's smoke-test env (pinned `ORG_ID` so startup skips the `getOrganizations` call).
- Image index verified multi-arch: `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`, exactly the arches we build.

The immediate breakage on PR #651 was unblocked separately by refreshing the checksums by hand (f7b8475), so that bump merged. This change means the next uv bump won't need it — Renovate updates tag and digest atomically in one commit, and automerge can carry it through unattended. That's the last acceptance box, and it'll confirm itself on the next uv release.

title: Dockerfile: replace manual uv tarball checksums with digest-pinned ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv

body:
## Mechanism
`manager.py::_run_collector_with_timeout` (~727-739) catches `TimeoutError`/`Exception` from `await collector.collect()`, logs + increments `_collection_errors`, and deliberately does NOT re-raise (correct resilience — lets other collectors continue). But `collector.collect()` itself (`core/collector.py`) DOES re-raise after setting its own span to `<net-name-4>TUS_CODE_ERROR`.

## Effect (live-verified)
Trace `5170be4c89f7ed0a756e458f67a63f6`: `collect.NetworkHealthCollector` → `<net-name-4>TUS_CODE_ERROR` with a full `NothingCollectedError` exception event, while its parent `collect.collector` in the SAME trace → `<net-name-4>TUS_CODE_OK`. Any panel built as `{ name="collect.collector" && status=error }` or a rootServiceName-scoped error-rate metric systematically reads **zero** during real, logged failures.

## Fix (either)
(a) also set `collect.collector`s span status to ERROR when the wrapped `collect()` raised, or (b) document in `docs/observability/otel.md` that error-rate TraceQL must target `name =~ "collect\\..*Collector"`, never the shared root name.

## Acceptance
Root-level error-rate reflects real collector failures, or the docs explicitly steer authors to the child-span selector. _v1 soak/sink assessment._

comments.body: Fixed in a9f075b (option a). The swallow-and-continue error paths in `_run_collector_with_timeout` now mark the `collect.collector` root span ERROR + `record_exception`, and the `trace_method` wrapper no longer overwrites an ERROR status back to OK on the normal-return path (OTel `set_status` only makes OK final, not ERROR — so the wrapper explicitly skips the OK set when the body already set ERROR). Root-level `{ name="collect.collector" && status=error }` panels now fire on real failures. Verified with a manager-level test that a swallowed `NothingCollectedError` leaves the root span ERROR.

body:
## Mechanism
`core/otel_tracing.py::_extract_span_attributes` (~line 448) only reads **kwargs** when auto-extracting `org_id`/`network_id`/etc via `_AUTO_EXTRACT_ATTRS`. Every real `@trace_method` call site passes these **positionally** — e.g. `device.py:698` `self._collect_org_devices(org_id, org.get("name", org_id))` — so the mechanism has never fired in production despite its docstring claiming auto-extraction.

## Evidence (live)
`process.organization` span in trace `d55896290bc68095dccb88d4383ad41e` carries only `{"class":"DeviceCollector"}`; TraceQL `span."org.id" != ""` matches **zero** spans across either service.name in a 6h sweep. Same for `collect.mr_*`, `collect.mx_metrics`, `collect.ms_metrics`.

## Fix direction
Bind args in the decorator via `inspect.signature(func).bind(*args, **kwargs)` so positional args are extracted, rather than requiring every call site to switch to kwargs. Add a regression test asserting span attributes on a `trace_method`-decorated call.

## Acceptance
`process.organization` and other trace_method-decorated collector-org methods carry `org.id` (and `org.name` where available) as span attributes. _v1 soak/sink assessment._

comments.body: Fixed in a9f075b. `_extract_span_attributes` now binds positional args via `inspect.signature(func).bind_partial(*args, **kwargs)`, so `org_id`/`network_id`/`serial`/... auto-extract even when passed positionally (which every real call site does). Regression test asserts `process.organization` carries `org.id`/`org.name` via an in-memory span exporter.

body:
## Surfaced by the DevNet org during the soak
The DevNet org (MX100) emits, at ~2/min steadily, `"Collect MX performance score failed"` with `DataValidationError: getDeviceAppliancePerformance: Expected dict, got NoneType`. The MX performance fetcher assumes a dict response but the endpoint returns `None`/empty for this appliance/state (likely no performance score available for the device model/license), and the validation layer rejects `None`.

## Evidence
`gcx logs query {service_name="meraki-dashboard-exporter-devnet"} | logfmt | level="error"` — dominant error on that shard; `error="getDeviceAppliancePerformance: Expected dict, got NoneType"`.

## Fix direction
Treat a `None`/empty `getDeviceAppliancePerformance` response as "no score available" (skip/emit-nothing gracefully) rather than raising `DataValidationError`; wrap via `validate_response_format` with a nullable expectation. Confirm against the OpenAPI spec / live call which MX models/states return null.

## Acceptance
An MX with no performance score produces no error-level log (graceful skip), and MX performance metrics still emit where a score exists.

_This is an application bug (not a telemetry-sink defect); surfaced by adding the DevNet MX during the soak. Not fixed this session._

comments.body: Fixed in ab5ab6f. `MXCollector._collect_performance_score` now guards a `None` response BEFORE `validate_response_format`: marks the serial collected (so it is not retry-hammered) and skips with a DEBUG line, instead of raising `DataValidationError`. Genuine error-shaped dicts still fall through to `validate_response_format`. Regression test added with `getDeviceAppliancePerformance` returning `None`.

body:
## Mechanism
`core/logging.py::_select_renderer` defaults to `structlog.processors.LogfmtRenderer()` (`LoggingSettings.log_format` defaults to `"logfmt"`, `core/config_models.py:1169-1172`). Loki `| json` fails 100% on these lines (`JSONParserErr: "Value looks like object, but cant find closing } symbol"`) since the payload is logfmt, not JSON.

## Not blocking (works today)
`| logfmt` parses every field (`level`, `event`, `org_id`, `trace_id`, `span_id`) cleanly, and Lokis auto `detected_level` label gives level-based filtering with **zero** parse stage. So dashboards/alerts are buildable today.

## Recommended fix (config-only, no code change)
Set `MERAKI_EXPORTER_LOGGING__LOG_FORMAT=json` on <soak-host> (both shards). Optionally flip the packaged default `LoggingSettings.log_format` `"logfmt"`→`"json"` for new deployments (Loki/ELK/CloudWatch are the primary sinks; `| json` is Lokis cheaper parse path, and the `exception` field — currently a ~2.4KB single-line Python-repr blob under logfmt — becomes valid nested JSON under the JSON renderer, which is drill-into-able).

## Acceptance
`{service_name=~"meraki-dashboard-exporter.*"} | json` returns zero `__error__` labels; `exception` on error lines is valid nested JSON. _v1 soak/sink assessment._

comments.body: Fixed in 1e4ee31. `LoggingSettings.log_format` now defaults to `"json"` (was `"logfmt"`): Loki `| json` returns zero `__error__` labels and the exception field becomes valid nested JSON. `logfmt` remains available for console output. Regenerated .env.example/values.yaml/config.md.

body:
## Context
OTLP traces and the OTLP metrics-bridge from both exporter instances reach Grafana Cloud (verified via `gcx traces query` and `{job="meraki-dashboard-exporter"}` in prom), but OTLP **data-logs** (`core/otel_data_logs.py` → collector <lan-ip>:4417 → Loki) have never been exercised because the exporter emitted zero records (see the signal_quality/packet-loss coupling bug). Traces arriving does **not** prove the logs pipeline works — a collector can forward traces+metrics but drop OTLP logs.

## Evidence
- `gcx logs query {service_name=~"meraki.*"} |= "signal_quality"` = 0 lines; the ~230 lines/min under `service_name=~"meraki-dashboard-exporter.*"` are the **docker-stdout** app logs (`job="integrations/docker"`), NOT OTLP data-logs.
- Collector host <lan-ip> not inspectable from <soak-host> — external, unverified suspect for the OTLP-logs→Loki path specifically.

## Confirming diagnostic
Once emission is fixed, re-query Loki for `event.name="meraki.wireless.client.signal_quality"` (scope `meraki_dashboard_exporter.data_logs`) across all jobs/service_names. If absent while the exporter emitted counter > 0, the fault is the collectors OTLP-logs pipeline (external config).

## Acceptance
An exporter-produced data-log record is queryable in Loki with a documented selector.

_v1 soak/sink assessment; not fixed this session._

comments.body: Resolved — the OTLP-logs→Loki path is **proven working**. `meraki.org.webhook.delivery` data-log records flow end-to-end into Grafana Cloud Loki today (verified 2026-07-03: real rows ~1/min, `status_code=200`, `url_host=hooks.slack.com`). The key detail the original assessment missed: OTel data-log attributes land in Loki as **structured metadata** (dot→underscore), so the correct selector is a pipeline filter `{service_name=~"meraki-dashboard-exporter.*"} | event_name=\`meraki.org.webhook.delivery\`` — filtering inside `{}` (as stream labels) returns nothing, which is what made it look absent. The surviving data-log gap is #637 (signal_quality/packet_loss never emit), not the pipeline.

body:
## Mechanism
`MRClientLogsCollector.collect_client_logs` (`collectors/devices/mr/client_logs.py:171-206`) early-returns when `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPacketLossByClient` returns no rows, and `_collect_signal_quality` (client_logs.py:301-342) derives its client universe from that **same** packet-loss response. So `WIRELESS_CLIENT_SIGNAL_QUALITY` (#622, RSSI/SNR) can only ever emit for clients that also appear in the packet-loss response — i.e. clients with *measured loss*. A healthy client (zero loss) never gets a signal-quality record though its signal data exists. The feature is broken for exactly the common (healthy-fleet) case.

## Evidence (<soak-host> soak, both shards, current HEAD 4514bf9)
- `meraki_exporter_data_log_records_emitted_total` has **zero child series** on both `:9099` and `:9100` after 58 DeviceCollector cycles → `DataLogEmitter.emit()` has never run. `_dropped_total` also zero (never threw).
- MR AP up on homelab (`meraki_device_up{device_type="MR",model="MR56"}`=1); producer path runs every cycle (not gated behind `MR_SSID_USAGE`).
- `gcx logs query {service_name=~"meraki.*"} |= "signal_quality"` → 0 lines over 30m.

## Confirming diagnostic
`GET /organizations/<maintainer-org-id>/wireless/devices/packetLoss/byClient?timespan=300` returns `[]` (run read-only with the homelab key).

## Fix direction
Decouple signal-quality client enumeration from the packet-loss response (enumerate active wireless clients independently, e.g. via the clients-overview / connection path) so it emits for all active clients; or explicitly gate signal_quality on its own source.

## Acceptance
With an up AP + active clients, ≥1 `signal_quality` record emitted per cycle (`meraki_exporter_data_log_records_emitted_total{event=...}` > 0) regardless of packet-loss presence.

_Filed from the v1 soak/sink assessment; not fixed in that session._

comments.body: Clarification after further live verification (2026-07-03): the original evidence said `meraki_exporter_data_log_records_emitted_total` has zero series 'so emit() never runs for any event' — that over-generalized. The **webhook.delivery** data-log event DOES emit and reaches Loki fine (see #638, now closed). The confirmed-broken path is specifically the two **wireless-client** events: `meraki.wireless.client.signal_quality` and `meraki.wireless.client.packet_loss` both return **zero** records in Loki over 24h, consistent with this issue's root cause (signal_quality enumeration coupled to the empty `packetLoss/byClient` response). So this issue stands as-is for the wireless-client coupling; the pipeline itself is fine.

Minor field note for the fixer: during the soak, two independent agents observed `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPacketLossByClient` returning `401 Unauthorized, {'errors': ['Invalid API key']}` at times (early boot), even though the same key succeeds on other endpoints. It was NOT persistent (0 occurrences in a later 25-min window on both shards; the call is interval-gated so it runs infrequently). So when implementing, confirm the endpoint's actual live behaviour on this key — whether it **401s** (a scope/permission gap on the DevNet demo key) vs **returns an empty list** (the healthy-client case this issue describes). The fix (decouple signal_quality enumeration from the packet-loss response) holds either way, but the 401 possibility means packet-loss data itself may also be unavailable in this specific environment.

Fixed in d6a8b8c. Signal-quality now enumerates its client universe INDEPENDENTLY of packet loss — `getNetworkClients` per allowed wireless network, filtered to `recentDeviceConnection == "Wireless"` — so a healthy zero-loss client (absent from the packet-loss response) still emits. Packet-loss and signal-quality are now independent producers.

Live-verified root cause on <soak-host>: `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPacketLossByClient` returns `OK rows=0` (empty, NOT 401) for BOTH orgs — the earlier 401s were transient early-boot blips, so the coupling (not a scope gap) was the bug.

Caveat: the end-to-end emit could NOT be observed live because the <soak-host> lab currently has ZERO associated wireless clients (`getNetworkClients`=79, all `recentDeviceConnection="Wired"`; connectionStats/overviewByDevice both empty). The decoupling is unit-tested (incl. a regression asserting signal-quality emits when packet loss is empty, and that wired clients are skipped), but a soak-observed emit needs an env with active wireless clients.

## Context / observation

Watching the <soak-host> soak, `"Starting parallel organization processing"` logs `concurrency_limit=5` (`settings.api.concurrency_limit`, env `MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__CONCURRENCY_LIMIT`, default 5, at `collectors/organization.py:518`). The same knob bounds the `ManagedTaskGroup` fan-out inside `device.py`/`network_health.py`/`organization.py` (per-org, per-device-type, per-network sub-work).

## The question (from Rob)

The adaptive scheduler + client-side AIMD rate limiter (`core/rate_limiter.py`, `core/scheduler.py`) exist to auto-adjust to the Meraki API's available rate budget. So why *also* statically cap parallel sub-work within a run via `api.concurrency_limit`? What's the benefit of limiting sub-work breadth when the rate limiter already governs request rate?

To work through / document (or change):

- [ ] **What `api.concurrency_limit` tunes** vs `collectors.max_concurrent_collectors` (also default 5, bounds how many collector loops run at once *globally*). The two are easily confused — one caps breadth *inside* a collector, the other caps how many collectors run concurrently. Are both needed?
- [ ] **Interaction with the rate limiter:** the token bucket already paces outbound requests. Is the concurrency cap redundant, or distinct (bounding in-flight memory / SDK executor-thread pressure independent of request rate)?
- [ ] **Derive it adaptively?** Could effective concurrency come from the solved budget like intervals do, giving one adaptive control surface instead of a static knob users must reason about?
- [ ] **Sharding awareness:** Rob floated passing a concurrency/awareness value into each sharded collector "to let them know other things are happening" (cross-collector coordination of in-flight work). Evaluate worthwhile vs over-engineering.
- [ ] **Docs clarity regardless:** if both knobs stay, config docs / `.env.example` must make the distinction + rate-limiter relationship unambiguous. Today it reads as "just another concurrency number."

## Acceptance

Either (a) a documented rationale for keeping both knobs with clearer descriptions, or (b) a proposal to derive concurrency adaptively / collapse the knobs. No code change required to close — clarity+design decision.

_Filed from the v1 soak session; not to be fixed in that session._

comments.body: Resolved (option a) in 1e4ee31 — keep both knobs, clarify the descriptions. Decision: `api.concurrency_limit` caps fan-out BREADTH inside one collector (in-flight memory + SDK executor-thread pressure), which is a distinct concern from the client-side AIMD rate limiter that caps request RATE (how fast requests leave the bucket). `collectors.max_concurrent_collectors` caps how many collector loops run globally. Deriving concurrency adaptively from the solved budget would conflate rate and breadth, so both stay; the field descriptions (regenerated into .env.example/values.yaml/config.md) now spell out the distinction + the rate-limiter relationship. No functional change.

title: Clarify (and reconsider) api.concurrency_limit vs the adaptive rate limiter — do we need per-run sub-work caps?

## Summary

`Settings()` is constructed **twice** on a normal server start, so every `@model_validator` side effect — including the "unrecognized env var" startup warnings — runs twice. Observed as each unrecognized-var warning appearing twice at startup, but the underlying issue is redundant `Settings` construction on the hot startup path.

## Observed (soak run, 2026-07-03)

The `MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT` / `MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION` "unrecognized env var" warnings (see companion issue) each print **twice** during a single startup — one pair before collector registration, one pair after.

## Root cause

Two independent `Settings()` instances are built and the second is never threaded from the first:

1. `main()` builds a throwaway `settings = Settings()` for early validation / friendly error messaging — `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/__main__.py:147`.
2. `main()` then calls `create_app()` with **no arguments** — `__main__.py:186`.
3. Module-level `create_app()` constructs `ExporterApp()` with no settings — `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/app.py:1345-1359` (`ExporterApp()` at ~1356).
4. `ExporterApp.__init__` does `self.settings = settings or Settings()` — `app.py:145-147` — building a **second** `Settings()`.

Each construction runs the `warn_unrecognized_env_vars` `@model_validator(mode="after")` (`core/config.py:136-150`), hence the duplicated warnings. (`create_app`'s `_app_instance` memoization at `app.py:1342-1359` is fine and only runs once — this is not a memoization bug. In `--check` mode only the `__main__` construction happens, so the doubling is specific to the real server-start path.)

## Impact

- Every startup `Settings`-validator warning is emitted twice (confusing).
- Redundant `Settings()` construction (minor; re-reads env, re-runs all validators).

## Fix sketch (do not implement yet)

Thread `main()`'s already-built `settings` into `create_app()` → `ExporterApp(settings=...)` so a single instance is reused, or drop the early `main()` construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Settings()` is constructed once on a normal server start.
- [ ] Each startup validator warning appears exactly once.

Found during the post-v1-readiness soak. Deferred (`v1-sink`) — will be addressed as part of the poller-model rearchitecture.
