## Summary

The exporter's **own Docker image** bakes `MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION` and `MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT` as build metadata (`Dockerfile:115-128`), but the app's config-diagnostics layer doesn't know about them, so at startup it (a) warns they are **unrecognized** ("check for a typo") and (b) prints them as `***REDACTED***` in the config summary. The `meraki_exporter_build_info` metric itself works — this is purely a diagnostics wart, but it means every containerised deployment logs spurious "typo" warnings about vars the image itself set.

## Observed (soak run, 2026-07-03)

```
[warning] Ignoring unrecognized MERAKI_EXPORTER_* environment variable (check for a typo; value not logged) env_var=MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT
[warning] Ignoring unrecognized MERAKI_EXPORTER_* environment variable (check for a typo; value not logged) env_var=MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION
...
event="  MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT=***REDACTED***"
event="  MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION=***REDACTED***"
```

(Container env confirmed: both set to the git SHA via `ARG APP_VERSION`/`ARG GIT_COMMIT` → `ENV` in `Dockerfile:127-128`.)

## Root cause

These two vars are consumed **directly via `os.environ`**, bypassing pydantic `Settings`:
- `get_version()` → `os.environ.get("MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION")` (`src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/__version__.py:47`)
- `get_commit()` → `os.environ.get("MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT")` (`__version__.py:71`)
- Both feed `meraki_exporter_build_info` (`core/build_info.py:38-48`, registered at `app.py:185`) and OTel `service.version`.

Because they are **not** `Settings` fields, two diagnostics helpers misjudge them:

**(a) False "unrecognized" warning.** `Settings.warn_unrecognized_env_vars` (`core/config.py:136-150`, the feature added in #515) calls `find_unrecognized_env_vars` (`core/config_models.py:1280-1309`), which flags any `MERAKI_EXPORTER_*` env key not in `known_env_var_names(model_cls)` (built from pydantic fields, `config_models.py:1252-1277`). There is no `version`/`commit` field, so both are flagged. The checker already carves out a `_FILE` exception (`config_models.py:1305-1307`) but has no allowlist for known non-pydantic vars.

**(b) Over-redaction.** `mask_sensitive_value` (`core/config_logger.py:94-131`) is redact-by-default with a **safe-substring allowlist** (`_SAFE_KEY_SUB<net-name-6>INGS`, lines 24-65). `version`/`commit` are in neither the sensitive nor the safe list, so they hit the catch-all `REDACTED` at line 131. Non-secret build metadata is masked purely for being absent from the allowlist.

## Fix sketch (do not implement yet)

1. Add a known-but-non-pydantic allowlist (`MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION`, `MERAKI_EXPORTER_COMMIT`) to `find_unrecognized_env_vars` / `known_env_var_names` so they don't warn.
2. Add `"version"` and `"commit"` to `_SAFE_KEY_SUB<net-name-6>INGS` (`config_logger.py`) so build metadata prints in clear.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No "unrecognized env var" warning for `MERAKI_EXPORTER_VERSION`/`_COMMIT`.
- [ ] Both shown unredacted in the startup config summary.
- [ ] `meraki_exporter_build_info` unchanged (still populated).

Related: #515 (added the unrecognized-var warning). Found during the post-v1-readiness soak. Deferred (`v1-sink`) — will be addressed as part of the poller-model rearchitecture.

labels.name: v1-sink
labels.description: Deferred: verified bug parked until the poller-model rearchitecture

body:
## Summary

A benign `404 "No MR repeaters found on this network"` from `getNetworkWirelessMeshStatuses` is logged **twice at ERROR level** on every MEDIUM cycle for any wireless network without mesh repeaters. Collection is unaffected (the collector already treats it as expected and emits no series) — this is pure log noise / false alarm.

## Observed (soak run, 2026-07-03)

```
event="wireless, getNetworkWirelessMeshStatuses - 404 Not Found, {'errors': ['No MR repeaters found on this network']}" level=error
operation=getNetworkWirelessMeshStatuses error_type=APIError event="API call failed: getNetworkWirelessMeshStatuses" level=error
```

## Root cause — two ERROR emitters fire before the collector downgrades to debug

`MeshCollector._fetch_mesh_statuses` (`src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/network_health_collectors/mesh.py:91-117`) is decorated **only** with `@log_api_call` — it does **not** use `@with_error_handling` (unlike the newer `latency_stats.py` / `air_marshal.py`, and as flagged by `network_health_collectors/CLAUDE.md`: "error handling is not uniform across all 7").

1. **SDK-side ERROR** (first line). The Meraki SDK client is built with `suppress_logging=False`, `inherit_logging_config=True`, `retry_4xx_error=False` (`src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/api/client.py:179-209`). Its `RestSession` logs every non-retried API error at `logger.error(...)` in the `"{tags}, {operation} - {status} {reason}, {message}"` format. This is independent of the decorator choice and would affect **any** benign 4xx across collectors.
2. **`@log_api_call` decorator ERROR** (second line). `core/logging_decorators.py:92-103`: the `except` block resolves `log_method = logger.warning if _is_rate_limit_error(e) else logger.error`, then re-raises. `_is_rate_limit_error` (lines 475-481) only matches 429/rate-limit, so a 404 → `logger.error`. There is no 404/not-available branch.

After the re-raise, `MeshCollector.collect`'s `except` (`mesh.py:134-161`) correctly matches `"404"` in `str(e)`, logs at **debug**, and returns without emitting a metric. So the design intent (no repeaters = no series, benign) is already correct — only the two upstream ERROR logs are wrong.

The sibling pattern that avoids this is `@with_error_handling`, whose generic branch special-cases `getattr(e, "status", None) == 404` to `logger.debug` (`core/error_handling.py:420-435`).

## Impact

- 2× ERROR log lines per no-mesh wireless network per MEDIUM cycle. No functional/metrics impact.
- Note the SDK-logger mechanism (emitter 1) is general — the rearchitecture should decide how benign 4xx are logged fleet-wide, not just for mesh.

## Fix sketch (do not implement yet)

Migrate `MeshCollector` to `@with_error_handling` (or add a 404 branch), **and** decide the SDK-logger policy in `client.py` (e.g. raise the SDK logger level, or `suppress_logging`) so benign 4xx don't emit an ERROR from the SDK.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A "No MR repeaters" 404 produces at most a `debug` log, no ERROR.
- [ ] Decision recorded on the general SDK-side benign-4xx logging policy.
- [ ] Collection still emits no mesh series for no-repeater networks (unchanged).

Found during the post-v1-readiness soak. Deferred (`v1-sink`) — will be addressed as part of the poller-model rearchitecture.

## Summary

`DataRatesCollector.collect` crashes with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'NoneType' and 'int'` whenever the most-recent wireless data-rate bucket has `null` throughput fields. On a quiet network this is essentially **every** MEDIUM cycle, so the network-wide download/upload kbps metrics are never emitted and an ERROR-level traceback is logged each run.

## Observed (soak run, 2026-07-03)

```
network_id=<net-id-8> network_name="<net-name-site>"
event="Failed to collect network data rates" level=error
exception="... TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'NoneType' and 'int'
  .../collectors/network_health_collectors/data_rates.py, lineno 102 ..."
```

## Root cause

`src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/network_health_collectors/data_rates.py:102-103`:

```python
download_bytes_per_second = latest_data.get("downloadKbps", 0) * 1000
upload_bytes_per_second   = latest_data.get("uploadKbps", 0) * 1000
```

`dict.get(key, 0)` returns the default `0` **only when the key is absent**. The Meraki API returns the keys **present but `null`** for buckets with no traffic, so `.get(...)` returns `None`, and `None * 1000` raises `TypeError`.

**Verified against the live API** (`GET /networks/{id}/wireless/dataRateHistory?timespan=300&resolution=300`):

```json
[{"startTs":"2026-07-03T13:35:00Z","endTs":"2026-07-03T13:40:00Z",
  "averageKbps":null,"downloadKbps":null,"uploadKbps":null}]
```

The `TypeError` is not a `400`/`404`/`Bad Request`/`rate limit`, so it falls through the `except` block's string-inspection guard (`data_rates.py:130-151`) to the `logger.exception(...)` branch — hence the ERROR traceback and no metric.

## Impact

- `meraki_network_wireless_download_kbps` / `_upload_kbps` never set for any wireless network whose latest 5-minute bucket is idle (the common case).
- ERROR-level traceback logged every MEDIUM cycle (log noise + false alarm).

## Fix sketch (do not implement yet — deferred to poller rearchitecture)

Coalesce null to `0` (or skip emitting) before the multiply, e.g. `(latest_data.get("downloadKbps") or 0) * 1000`. Consider whether an all-null latest bucket should emit `0` or be skipped like the empty-response path (`data_rates.py:83-88`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `null` `downloadKbps`/`uploadKbps` in the latest bucket does not raise; collection completes without an ERROR log.
- [ ] Behaviour for all-null latest bucket is deliberate and documented (emit 0 vs skip).
- [ ] Regression test with a factory response whose latest bucket has `null` throughput fields.

Found during the post-v1-readiness soak. Deferred (`v1-sink`) — will be addressed as part of the poller-model rearchitecture.

body:
**Parent epic:** #617 (read its description IN FULL first — it holds the program summary; its two long 2026-07-03 comments hold the original design doc + the frozen Option A build spec whose execution model this issue replaces). **Area:** `core` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** V1-P3.

## Why (Rob's decision, 2026-07-03 — binding, do not re-litigate)

The #617 build spec deliberately kept the three FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW tier loops as *heartbeats*: endpoint groups gate inside them and can never run faster than their owning collector's tier interval. That shipped (commits `3e20f34`/`3071792`/`2cb500d`) and works — but Rob has rejected the heartbeat compromise: **FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW must disappear as constructs entirely.** Consequences of the compromise being removed:

1. **Interval quantization.** `interval_for(g) = max(floor, tier_heartbeat)` means `device_availability` (floor 120s, `device.py:71-77`) actually runs at 300s. The epic's "device up-ness fresh at ≤120s" success criterion is silently unmet (the spec's optional "Lane X" workaround was never built — this issue makes it unnecessary).
2. **Two scheduling vocabularies.** Operators see tiers (config, logs, `tier` label on self-metrics, /status) *and* endpoint groups (scheduler gauges, /status).
3. **Vestigial surface.** `UPDATE_INTERVALS__*`, three per-tier concurrency knobs, tier-keyed TTL fallback, tier-gated readiness, tier-derived liveness — all superseded by the solver.

v1 is the only breaking-change moment (no interim releases): removing tiers now means v1's operator surface, self-metric contract, and Helm values are final.

## Target execution model (frozen design)

**Collector-clocked, group-driven dispatch.** Collectors remain the execution vessels (error boundary, 240s timeout, health bookkeeping, `ManagedTaskGroup` fan-out) — but each collector gets its **own loop clocked by its endpoint groups**:

```
wake_at = min over g in collector's enabled, gated groups of next_due(g)
sleep until min(wake_at, now + scheduler.resolve_interval_seconds)   # cap: re-solves/AIMD/re-enabled groups picked up within one resolve period
run collector once (existing collect() path; gates open exactly for due groups)
repeat
```

Because the loop wakes at the *earliest due group's* time, every group runs at **exactly its solved interval** — per-group scheduling with collector-level batching when due-times coincide. Spurious wakes (interval stretched mid-sleep) are cheap no-ops: gates say "not due", the loop recomputes and sleeps again.

**Considered and rejected:** a single global dispatcher executing per-group closures. Rejected because (a) fetch sites share per-run fan-out context and error/timeout boundaries at collector granularity, (b) it needs per-group timeout/health/status plumbing for ~80 groups, (c) it delivers identical cadence to the model above. Do not re-open this fork.

### Frozen gate-semantics change: attempt tracking (prevents a failure hot-loop)

Under tier heartbeats, a group whose fetch failed (gate left open) retried at the next heartbeat — the heartbeat itself spaced retries. Under group clocks that spacing disappears: an open gate ⇒ `next_due` is already past ⇒ immediate re-wake ⇒ **hot retry loop on persistent failure**. Fix, frozen into `EndpointScheduler`:

- Scheduler tracks `last_attempt[g]` alongside `last_ran[g]`. `should_run(g)` returning `True` records the attempt.
- `should_run(g)` is `True` when: never attempted, OR (`now - last_ran[g] >= interval_for(g) × 0.9` AND `now - last_attempt[g] >= failure_retry_seconds`).
- `next_due(g)` = `last_ran[g] + interval_for(g) × 0.9`, floored at `last_attempt[g] + failure_retry_seconds`.
- New setting `SchedulerSettings.failure_retry_seconds: int = 300` (ge=30, le=3600) — reproduces today's ~300s failed-fetch retry cadence for every group regardless of floor.
- `mark_ran(g)` semantics (canonical, resolving the build-spec §1a-vs-§2 tension the 2026-07-03 audit flagged): **mark iff the cycle achieved ≥1 successful fetch for the group** (partial fan-out success counts; total failure leaves the gate open → bounded retry via `failure_retry_seconds`). The per-site mark_ran fixes land in #629 first; this issue only adds the attempt layer.

## What is removed (complete inventory — from the 2026-07-03 audit; verify each with grep before closing)

**A. Registry/tier mapping:** `core/registry.py:20-146` tier-keyed registry + `@register_collector(tier)` (→ no-arg decorator, flat list); `core/collector.py:48` `update_tier` default; `collectors/devices/mt.py:43` override; `collectors/manager.py:96-99,268-306,1014-1016` tier-keyed `self.collectors`.
**B. Tier loops:** `app.py:571-593` per-tier task creation; `app.py:614-699` `_tiered_collection_loop`; `collectors/manager.py:547-558` sequential-by-tier `collect_initial` (→ ordered by best group priority class, then name); `manager.py:673-745` `collect_tier`. Also the two derived delays: `app.py:701-710` `_wait_for_first_collection` sleeps `SLOW+5` (→ explicit completion event with fixed 1800s timeout) and `app.py:739-740` cardinality initial delay `MEDIUM+30` (→ fixed 330s).
**C. Per-tier concurrency:** `manager.py:196-216` + `config_models.py:114-130` `concurrency_limit_fast/medium/slow` → ONE `collectors.max_concurrent_collectors` global semaphore around collector runs (default = today's medium limit, 5).
**D. Tier-keyed TTL fallback:** `core/metric_expiration.py:222-243` `_get_ttl_for_tier`, `:296-320` fallback chain, `:29-39,129-177` `_TrackedSeries.tier`/`tier=` param; `core/collector.py` `tier=self.update_tier` passing. Explicit `ttl_seconds` (already threaded at every gated site) stays primary; fallback for stragglers = owning collector's min-enabled-group interval × `metric_ttl_multiplier`, via a resolver the manager installs on the expiration manager.
**E. Readiness:** `manager.py:128-136` `_tier_initial_complete`, `:456-493` `is_ready` (FAST+MEDIUM gated) → ready when every collector owning ≥1 enabled **priority ≤3** group has ≥1 successful run (ConfigCollector — all priority-4 — stays excluded, exactly like SLOW today). Keep F-105 semantics: no success ⇒ readiness withheld.
**F. Liveness:** `app.py:278-319` fastest-tier derivation → `3 × scheduler.fastest_effective_interval_seconds()` (exists at `core/scheduler.py:569`, currently diagnostics-only — becomes load-bearing; re-read each health check so AIMD stretching widens the threshold). Update `config_models.py:396-401` help text + chart values comment.
**G. Config + the scheduler's own tier coupling (the load-bearing removal):** `config_models.py:322-356` `UpdateIntervals` model deleted; `core/scheduler.py:239,273-304,398-404,525-534` solver drops `tier_intervals` — pre-solve `interval_for(g)` becomes the group's **floor** (this is what un-quantizes `device_availability` to 120s); `EndpointGroup.tier` field (`scheduler.py:208-221`) deleted; **all ~79 `EndpointGroup(tier=…)` declarations** across `collectors/{alerts,clients,config,device,insight,mt_alerts,mt_sensor,network_health,organization}.py` (mechanical); `scheduler.py:422-446` `_collect_overrides` clamp changes from "≥ tier heartbeat" to "honour below-floor pins with a WARNING" (build-spec step-2 rule, now floor-relative).
**H. Smoothing:** `core/collector.py:619-679` + `manager.py:189-243` tier-interval-based windows/offsets → one-time deterministic per-collector phase offset (keep the sha256 logic) applied to the FIRST steady-state wake only, bounded by `min(0.5 × collector_cadence, 120s)`; steady state then self-schedules. `manager.py:893-906` utilization gauge denominator → collector cadence.
**I. Status/diagnostics:** `services/status.py:28-60` `_compute_staleness` thresholds → per-collector cadence; `:96` `CollectorStatus.tier`; `:362-395` tier_intervals dict; `manager.py:932-1003` `get_tier_interval` + per-tier `tier_info` diagnostics; `core/config_logger.py:262-297` startup tier log; `templates/status.html` + `templates/index.html` tier sections → per-group interval/next-due table + per-collector cadence.
**J. Labels (contract change, rename-now policy #531, no dual-emit):** `core/metrics.py:102` `LabelName.TIER`; the `tier` label on ALL self-metrics — `core/collector.py:877-917` (duration/errors/success-timestamp/api-calls/smoothing gauges), `manager.py:148-185`, `metric_expiration.py:104-108,330-334` `expired_metrics_total{tier}`; OTel span attribute `collector.tier` + `tier=` structured-log fields. ADD `meraki_exporter_collector_cadence_seconds{collector}` gauge (derived min enabled-group interval) so staleness alerts can be expressed as `time() - success_timestamp > 3 × cadence`.
**K. Dead code:** `services/inventory.py:40-42,60-63,101-103` `TTL_FAST/SLOW` constants (already dead); `core/constants/device_constants.py:46-51` `UpdateTier` enum itself (last).

## Behavioural invariants to preserve (regression-test these)

- Restart ⇒ refetch-everything-once (never-attempted groups gate open; sequential initial collection unchanged in spirit).
- Solver, AIMD, resolve loop, cost model, floors, pins, `scheduler.mode=fixed` unchanged — `fixed` now means "floors/pins only, no stretching" with NO tier fallback (update docstrings/docs).
- `enabled_fn` auto-disable (#623): `wake_at` skips disabled groups; all-disabled or zero-group collectors (e.g. `ClientsCollector` with `clients.enabled=false`) are never scheduled beyond a resolve-period re-check — log once at startup.
- Manual trigger (`POST /api/collectors/trigger`, `app.py:1182`) gains `force=True` through `run_collector_once` → gate helpers, so a trigger actually fetches every group (today it silently no-ops in-window groups — fix here).

Test this.

## Files to touch (single lane, one owner — seams too entangled to fan out)

`core/scheduler.py` · `core/constants/device_constants.py` · `core/registry.py` · `core/collector.py` · `core/metric_expiration.py` · `core/config_models.py` · `core/config_logger.py` · `core/metrics.py` · `collectors/manager.py` · `app.py` · `services/status.py` · `services/inventory.py` (dead constants) · `templates/status.html` + `templates/index.html` · all `@register_collector`/`EndpointGroup(tier=…)` call sites (mechanical, ~10 files) · `charts/meraki-dashboard-exporter/` · `docs/` + CLAUDE.md sweep · tests throughout.

body:
**Parent epic:** #617. **Area:** `api` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** V1-P3. **Requires the live homelab API key** (gitignored `.env`, org `<maintainer-org-id>`, MR/MS/MT + 2×MV, no MX/MG — some items below are unverifiable in the homelab and must be verified against the OpenAPI spec + documented as such).

## Why this issue exists

The #617 build spec marked ~14 scheduler inputs **⚠ "needs Phase-6 live verification before being frozen as constants"**. The 2026-07-03 audit confirmed **every one of them shipped ASSUMED — none was live-verified.** The closing comments on #271, #331 and #549 each claim these are "tracked on the Phase-6 checklist (#619)", but #619's checklist never actually listed them — this issue is that missing list. #619 now references this issue as a release-gate item.

This matters because these values are the solver's ground truth: a wrong floor either wastes budget (floor too low ⇒ redundant fetches of an unchanged window) or silently serves stale data (floor too high). And the #271 rewrite currently **drops 6GHz data** on an assumption.

## The verification list (from build spec §2 legend + Phase-6 list; shipped values per audit)

| # | Item | Shipped value / behaviour | Where | What to verify live |

| 8 | **#271 byBand/6GHz shape** | org-wide ByDevice/ByNetwork landed; **6GHz rows dropped**; band strings assumed (`"5"`) | `network_health_collectors/rf_health.py:13-21,100,132,149-159` | Actual `byBand` array band values on live response (2.4/5/6). If 6GHz present, STOP DROPPING it — emit it (band label exists). Homelab has WiFi-6E-capable APs? if not, verify against OpenAPI + a 6GHz-capable org if available, else document the assumption in code |

## Method

- Use the homelab key from the gitignored `.env` (never log/commit it). Prefer small standalone scripts under the scratch dir or `uv run python -c`; nothing lands in the repo except corrected constants/fields + tests + code comments recording verification date/org.
- Remember `evidence/live-api-verification.md`: **the OpenAPI spec is wrong for some endpoints** — live beats spec; spec is the fallback only where the homelab lacks hardware.
- Window verification technique: two fetches N minutes apart inside the presumed window; identical aggregate payloads ⇒ window ≥ gap. Also check response `timespan`/`startTs` fields where present.

title: Live-verify the frozen scheduler assumptions: volatility floors, #271 byBand/6GHz, #549 MV fields, #331 conn-stats dedup, perPage maxima

body:
**Parent epic:** #617. **Area:** `core` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** V1-P3. **Sequence: do this BEFORE the de-tiering sub-issue** — its gate-semantics decision here is a prerequisite for the attempt-tracking layer there.

Findings from the 2026-07-03 read-only audit of the landed #617 implementation (commits `3e20f34`/`3071792`/`2cb500d` + Phase-4 follow-ups) against the frozen build spec (long comment on #617, 2026-07-03 06:09). The implementation is structurally spec-conformant; these are the surviving defects. Each item below is self-contained — file:line refs verified against `main` @ 2026-07-03; re-verify before editing (code moves).

## Binding semantic decision (resolves a build-spec self-contradiction)

Build spec §1a says *"`mark_ran` is called after a successful fetch **only** … so failures retry on the next heartbeat"*; spec §2 (NH gate placement) says *"`mark_ran` per group **after the fan-out completes**"*. The implementation followed §2, so a fan-out whose every item failed still advances the gate. **Canonical rule, decided at review: `mark_ran(g)` iff the cycle achieved ≥1 successful fetch for that group.** Partial fan-out success counts (don't re-fetch a whole org because one network 500'd); total failure leaves the gate open so the next heartbeat retries. Apply it to every site below.

## Gap 1 — mark_ran fires after fan-outs that swallowed every failure (MEDIUM-HIGH)

On a total outage the gate still advances, suppressing retry for the full solved interval instead of the next heartbeat (a freshness-recovery regression vs pre-#617 behaviour; worst at high floors):

- `collectors/devices/mr/clients.py:186` — `MR_CONNECTION_<net-name-4>TS` (floor **1800s**) marked ran unconditionally after the per-network loop whose exceptions are swallowed at `:178`. Total outage ⇒ no retry for ~1620s.
- `collectors/device.py:833-834` — `DEVICE_AVAILABILITY` (priority 1, up-ness!) marked ran even when `_fetch_device_availabilities` returned `None` (error path via `with_error_handling`, `device.py:1830-1860`).
- `collectors/network_health.py:475-476` + `network_health_collectors/rf_health.py:450` — all NH groups marked after fan-outs that swallow failures (`continue_on_error`); worst at `NH_FAILED_CONNECTIONS`/`NH_LATENCY_<net-name-4>TS`/`NH_AIR_MARSHAL` (floor **3600s**).
- `collectors/devices/mr/performance.py:1084` — `MR_CPU_LOAD` (same pattern; low impact, floor 300).
- `collectors/devices/mv.py:342-353` — `MV_ANALYTICS` marked even when a `continue_on_error` sub-fetch was swallowed (floor 900).
- `collectors/clients.py:422` — `CLIENTS_LIST` via `_process_network_batch`/org-backoff skips.

Fix pattern: thread a "≥1 success" flag out of the fan-out (or count successes) and call `_mark_group_ran` only when true. Note the org-wide single-fetch groups already do this correctly (e.g. `clients.py:228`, `mx.py:496`) — make the multi-fetch sites consistent with them. TDD: per site, a test where every sub-fetch fails must leave `should_run(group)` True.

## Gap 2 — `MS_PORT_OVERVIEW` emissions bypass `_set_metric`/TTL tracking (MEDIUM)

`collectors/devices/ms.py:2064-2114` emit via raw `gauge.labels(...).set(...)`: this floor-**3600s** group's series are not expiration-tracked at all and the solved `ttl_seconds` is never threaded — violates the build-spec table invariant (every emission of a gated group passes `ttl_seconds=self._group_ttl_seconds(group)`). Stale media/link-speed label combos linger forever after ports change. Convert to the standard `_set_metric`/`_set_metric_value` path with the group TTL.

## Gap 3 — empty-but-successful responses never mark_ran ⇒ pointless refetch every heartbeat (LOW)

- `collectors/devices/mr/performance.py:740` — `MR_PACKET_LOSS`
- `collectors/devices/mx.py:441-442` — `MX_UPLINK_<net-name-4>TUS`

# Scoping: #623 auto-detect in-use features/hardware, auto-disable unused collectors/endpoints

## 1. Problem restatement

Cut wasted Meraki API calls by detecting which device families/features an org actually uses, disabling the corresponding endpoint fetches inline when absent, and re-discovering periodically so they re-enable when hardware appears. Key question posed by the issue: does the #617 scheduler's zero-cost-for-absent-family already achieve most of this, so the epic only needs to target residual probe-when-absent calls?

## 2. What ALREADY exists (quantified — this is most of the epic)

The distinction that matters is **"gated but still probes once per cycle"** (fetch runs, returns empty, costs 1+ call) vs **"never fetched"**. Audit result: almost every family-dependent fetch is already **never fetched** when the family is absent, via explicit presence checks in the collectors — not via the scheduler.

**(a) Family-level presence gates (never fetched when absent) — already built:**

| Family | Gate | Cite |
|---|---|---|
| MX (uplink status/health/usage, HA, VPN×2, security events, firewall fan-out) | whole `_collect_mx_specific_metrics` block runs only if any device has model `MX*` or `productType=="appliance"` | `collectors/device.py:917-924` → block at `device.py:1143-1250` |
| MG (uplink statuses) | only if any `MG*` model present | `device.py:926-928` |
| MS (port status/usage/packets, STP, stacks, PSU) | only if `MS*` model or `productType=="switch"` | `device.py:749-750, 909-915` |
| MR (clients, conn stats, ethernet, packet loss, CPU, SSID) | only if any `MR*` model present | `device.py:899-902` |
| MV (analytics ×3) | per-device path only; zero cameras ⇒ zero calls | `device.py:852-875` |
| Network-health (all 7 NH groups incl. air marshal) | early return when no wireless networks (from cached inventory, 0 API calls) | `collectors/network_health.py:420-427` |
| MT readings | readings fetched only `if sensor_serials` | `collectors/devices/mt.py:391-394` |
| MT sensor alerts | early return when no sensor-capable networks | `collectors/mt_alerts.py:201-205` |
| Alerts sensor overview | fans out only to `get_networks_with_device_types(org_id, ["sensor"])` | `collectors/alerts.py:284-308` |
| Client signal quality | opt-in (#533) + wireless-clients-present check | `collectors/clients.py:1272-1307` |
| Whole org | `if not devices: return` before any per-family work | `device.py:653-655` |

So the issue's motivating example — `getOrganizationApplianceUplinkStatuses` for a no-MX org — is **already never called**.

**(b) The #617 scheduler's role — demand accounting, not skipping.** `should_run()` (`core/scheduler.py:490-503`) checks only elapsed-time vs solved interval; it never consults `cost_fn`. A zero-device family contributes zero demand to the solver (`solve_intervals`, `scheduler.py:266-267`), so it exerts no stretching pressure — but a zero-cost group would still be "due" every heartbeat. The actual not-fetching comes from the collectors' presence checks in (a). The two mechanisms compose correctly; neither is redundant.

**(c) Periodic re-discovery — already exists at 15-min granularity.** `_scheduler_resolve_loop` (`app.py:721-787`) re-solves from a fresh `OrgShape` every `resolve_interval_seconds` (default 900s, matching the inventory TTL). `get_org_shape` (`services/inventory.py:1159-1220`) computes all 16 per-family counts from cached, `NetworkFilter`-enforced inventory reads (zero extra API calls). Presence checks in (a) also re-read the (900s-TTL) inventory each MEDIUM cycle, so a newly-added MX is picked up within ≤ TTL + one cycle (~20 min worst case). The issue's "re-run discovery every X hours" is already exceeded. (`core/discovery.py:181`'s productTypes count is startup-log-only and unfiltered by design; the live mechanism is `get_org_shape`, not `DiscoveryService`.)

## 3. Exact residual: probe-when-absent calls that still fire

**Family-level (the epic's true target) — only TWO sites found:**

1. **`getOrganizationSensorGatewaysConnectionsLatest`** — `devices/mt.py:456-468` (`_collect_org_gateway_connections`). Gated only on `_should_run_group(MT_SENSOR_READINGS)` (`mt.py:462-465`), NOT on MT presence — unlike its sibling `_collect_org_sensors` which skips the readings fetch when `sensor_serials` is empty (`mt.py:391`). Group floor is 60s on FAST tier (`mt_sensor.py:40-46`), so a **zero-MT org burns up to 1,440 calls/day** on this one endpoint. Its `cost_fn` also floors at 2 for zero sensors (`2 + pages(0,100) - 1 = 2`, `mt_sensor.py:44`).
2. **`getOrganizationSwitchPortsOverview`** — `devices/ms.py:1862-1888` (`collect_port_overview`), invoked unconditionally at `device.py:884-889`, *outside* the switch-presence gate. Floor 3600s ⇒ **24 calls/day** for a no-switch org.

**Feature-level (family present, feature unused — returns empty each cycle):** MX_VPN 2 calls/300s (576/day) for MX orgs without site-to-site VPN (`device.py:1196,1203`); MX_HA 1/300s (288/day) without warm spare (`device.py:1189`); MX_SECURITY_EVENTS 1/300s (288/day); MS_<net-name-4>CKS 1 per switch-network/900s; ORG_PACKET_CAPTURES 1/900s (96/day). Here the API call *is* the cheapest probe — you can't know VPN/HA is unused without asking. Auto-disabling these needs an empty-response back-off cache with a re-probe TTL (real state, real staleness risk: enable VPN → metrics silently absent until re-probe).

**Future collectors (#613 Insight / #326 Catalyst / #327 eSIM / #328 MG-HA):** all still OPEN/unimplemented (verified via `gh issue view`). There is nothing to disable yet; the right deliverable is a *convention in the scheduler seam* those specs adopt on day one.

## 4. Quantified rate-limit saving

Budget: 10 rps × 0.8 shared fraction = **8 rps = 691,200 calls/day** (`core/config_models.py:174-194`).

- **Family-level residual (worst case: org with zero MT and zero MS):** 1,440 + 24 = 1,464 calls/day ≈ 0.017 rps ≈ **0.21% of budget**.
- **Feature-level residual (MX org using no VPN/HA/stacks/captures/sec-events):** ~1,250-1,350 calls/day ≈ **0.19% of budget**.
- For Rob's homelab (single org, most families present), the residual is effectively just whichever families he lacks — likely **well under 0.2% of budget**.

Conclusion: the #617 gating + existing presence checks already deliver ≳99% of the epic's intended saving. The residual is dominated by one endpoint (`getOrganizationSensorGatewaysConnectionsLatest`) whose fix is a few lines.

## 5. Proposed design (if any of it is built)

**Mechanism — `enabled_fn` on `EndpointGroup`, folded into `should_run` exactly as the issue suggests:**

- Add `enabled_fn: Callable[[OrgShape], bool] | None = None` to the frozen `EndpointGroup` dataclass (`core/scheduler.py:170-180`).
- `EndpointScheduler.should_run` (`scheduler.py:490-503`) already has `self._last_shape` (`scheduler.py:336, 440`): return `False` when `declared.enabled_fn is not None and self._last_shape is not None and not enabled_fn(self._last_shape)`. Fail-open when no shape yet (pre-resolve) — matches the existing fail-open contract.
- `solve_intervals` treats disabled groups as zero demand (their cost_fn is already ~0 for absent families; optionally short-circuit).
- Re-enable is free: the 900s resolve loop refreshes the shape; next `should_run` flips true. No new TTL machinery — the "X-hour re-discovery" requirement is satisfied by the existing 15-min loop.
- Surfaced in `diagnostics()` (`scheduler.py:538-568`) as `"enabled": bool` per group → visible on `/status`.

**Which groups annotate:** `MT_SENSOR_READINGS` (`s.sensor_count > 0`) and `MS_PORT_OVERVIEW` (`s.switch_count > 0`) — both fetch sites already check `_should_run_group` first (`mt.py:462`, `ms.py:1875`), so **the two residual probes are fixed automatically by the seam with zero collector edits**. Optionally annotate the whole MX/MG/MV/MR/NH group set for defence-in-depth (behaviour today is already correct via presence checks, so this is documentation-grade). Feature-gated future collectors (#613/#326/#327/#328) declare `enabled_fn` + (for license-gated Insight) a one-time probe convention in their own specs.

**#585 / NetworkFilter interaction — clean.** `OrgShape` is computed from the filtered inventory views (`inventory.py:1162-1168, 1187-1188`), and presence checks use the same filtered `get_devices`. So "filter excludes every sensor network ⇒ `sensor_count == 0` ⇒ MT probes off" falls out for free and is the correct semantic. Single-org means one shape and one resolve loop — no per-org enablement map needed.

**Explicitly NOT proposed pre-v1:** the feature-probe cache (empty-response back-off for MX_VPN/MX_HA/MS_<net-name-4>CKS/etc.). Saving ≈0.2% of budget; costs new persistent state, a staleness window on feature enablement, and docs/tests. Defer; revisit only if a real deployment shows these dominate.

## 6. Build plan (recommended slice)

Single lane, disjoint from other v1 work:

1. `core/scheduler.py` — `enabled_fn` field + `should_run` check + diagnostics key (~20 lines). Seam file: orchestrator-owned per CLAUDE.md.
2. `collectors/mt_sensor.py`, and `device.py` group declarations — `enabled_fn` on `MT_SENSOR_READINGS`, `MS_PORT_OVERVIEW` (2 lines). Optionally fix `cost_fn` for zero sensors (`mt_sensor.py:44`).
3. Tests: solver/gate unit tests (disabled group not due; re-enables after resolve with new shape; fail-open pre-resolve) + one MT integration test asserting zero gateway-connections calls for a sensor-less org.
4. Doc touch: scheduler docs note the enablement gate.

Effort: **~half a day**. Alternative minimal fix (no seam): mirror `mt.py:391`'s presence check inside `_collect_org_gateway_connections` and move `collect_port_overview` inside the switch gate — ~1-2h, but leaves no convention for #613/#326/#327/#328.

## 7. Risks

- `enabled_fn=False` means `mark_ran` never advances — on re-enable the group fires immediately (desirable; no thundering herd since it's per-group).
- A filter/API blip that transiently zeroes a family would pause its probes for ≤15 min — acceptable, and inventory error paths keep stale cache rather than returning empty.
- Adjacent bug found (not this epic, worth its own issue): the MR presence gate at `device.py:900` checks model prefix `"MR"` only, unlike MS (`device.py:909-913`) and MX (`device.py:918-923`) which also check `productType` — an org with only Catalyst APs (`CW*` models, `productType=="wireless"`) silently skips all MR org-wide metrics. Directly relevant to #326.

## 8. RECOMMENDATION

**Already-mostly-covered-by-#617 + existing presence gates.** Do **not** build the full epic (per-endpoint enablement registry + feature-probe cache + X-hour re-discovery) pre-v1 — periodic re-discovery already runs every 15 min, family-level auto-disable already exists in the collectors, and the total addressable residual is ~0.2-0.4% of the default API budget. **Do** build the half-day slice pre-v1: the `enabled_fn` seam on `EndpointGroup` + annotations for `MT_SENSOR_READINGS` and `MS_PORT_OVERVIEW`, which eliminates the only two real probe-when-absent sites (≈1,464 calls/day worst case, dominated by the 1,440/day MT gateway probe) and gives #613/#326/#327/#328 their auto-disable convention for free when they land post-v1. Defer the feature-probe cache indefinitely. File the MR/Catalyst presence-gate bug separately.

comments.body:
# Scoping: #622 — OTel log emitter for high-cardinality per-entity data

## 1. Problem restatement

Per-entity signals (per-client wireless packet loss #323, per-client signal detail, and similar) are valuable for troubleshooting but must never become labeled Prometheus series — client populations are unbounded and violate the project's cardinality rules (CLAUDE.md fatal rules; `roadmap_workflow` §3). #622 proposes a dedicated OTel **log** emitter: structured OTLP log records carrying the per-entity detail, so operators with a log backend (Loki, Elastic, any OTLP sink) get per-client visibility with zero metric-cardinality cost. This scope covers routing rules, SDK wiring, schema, config, build plan, and a v1-worthiness recommendation.

## 2. What already exists (verified against current code)

- **Tracing-only OTel.** `core/otel_tracing.py:95-107` builds an `OTLPSpanExporter` (gRPC, `endpoint` + `insecure` from settings) behind `BatchSpanProcessor`; `docs/observability/otel.md:12-13` states "tracing only... metrics are not exported through OTEL."
- **`core/otel_logging.py` is NOT a log exporter.** Despite the name, it only injects trace context into structlog output (`otel_logging.py:42-43`: "Direct OTEL log export requires additional packages. For now, we just ensure trace context is added to logs"). The name collision is a naming hazard for the new module.
- **`OTelSettings`** (`core/config_models.py:532-573`): `enabled` (default False), `endpoint` (OTLP gRPC), `insecure` (TLS toggle, F-110), `service_name`, `sampling_rate`, `resource_attributes`; validator requires endpoint when enabled.
- **Wiring points:** `app.py:145-146` (`TracingConfig.setup_tracing()`), `app.py:149-151` (`OTELLoggingConfig`), `app.py:495-496` (shutdown).
- **Logs SDK is already installed — no new dependency.** Verified live against the venv (opentelemetry-sdk 1.43.0 / opentelemetry-exporter-otlp 1.43.0, both already in `pyproject.toml:22-29` as `>=1.29`): `opentelemetry._logs` API (`LogRecord`, `Logger.emit`, `SeverityNumber`, `set/get_logger_provider`), `opentelemetry.sdk._logs.LoggerProvider`, `opentelemetry.sdk._logs.export.{BatchLogRecordProcessor, InMemoryLogExporter}` (in-memory exporter = clean test seam), and `opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc._log_exporter.OTLPLogExporter` all import successfully. Caveat: the module paths are still underscore-prefixed (`_logs`) in 1.43 — see Risks.
- **A grandfathered per-client metric surface already exists.** `collectors/clients.py` (MEDIUM tier, `clients.py:38`) emits per-client metrics — status, usage, `WIRELESS_CLIENT_RSSI/SNR` (`metrics_constants.py:395-427`) — **opt-in** (`ClientSettings.enabled=False`, `config_models.py:684-687`) and **ID-only** per #533 (`metrics_constants.py:401-405`: numeric series carry only `client_id`, PII-ish labels live on `meraki_client_info` join carrier, capped by `max_clients_per_network`, `config_models.py:717-721`). Any boundary rule must acknowledge this existing exception rather than pretend the surface is purely aggregate.

## 3. The boundary rule (proposed, for docs + future issue triage)

> **Metrics** carry bounded, fleet-shaped aggregates: label sets drawn from stable inventory (org / network / device serial / SSID number / port / band) or top-N endpoints bounded by construction (#299). **OTel logs** carry per-entity detail where the entity population is unbounded or churny (client ID/MAC, per-event, per-connection rows). No NEW client-keyed labeled metric may be added — new per-client signals route to the log emitter. The existing opt-in `clients.py` surface is grandfathered under the #533 ID-only + `_info`-join regime and is unchanged by this epic (migrating it to logs is explicitly out of scope for v1).

### Data-class routing (scan of open deferred/roadmap issues)

| Signal | Route | Why |
|---|---|---|
| #323 per-client wireless packet loss (`getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPacketLossByClient`, org-wide bulk) | **Log emitter — first producer; #622 absorbs #323** | Unbounded client keys; the issue itself says "do NOT label by MAC". One bulk call/org → N records. |
| #324 per-**AP** signal quality (SNR/RSSI) | **Metric** (stays as designed) | Bounded by AP fleet. The per-**client** variant of `signalQualityHistory` (mandatory `clientId` filter) would be per-client fan-out → if ever built, it's a log-emitter data class, not a metric. |
| #299 top-N clients/SSIDs/manufacturers by usage | **Metric** | Bounded top-N by construction. |
| #282/#280 per-AP radio status / health scores | **Metric** | Bounded per-AP. |
| #300 webhook delivery log | **Log emitter — natural fast-follow** (it is literally a log) | Per-delivery-attempt rows, unbounded. |
| #296 CDP/LLDP topology | Metric (`_info`-style) for v1 thinking; log emitter is a fallback if port×neighbor cardinality proves hostile | Bounded by physical ports, but churny values. Decide at that issue, not here. |
| Existing `clients.py` RSSI/SNR/usage | Metric (grandfathered, opt-in, ID-only) | Shipped surface; #533 rename just landed; don't churn pre-v1. |

## 4. Proposed design

**New module `core/otel_data_logs.py`** (avoid `otel_logs.py` — too confusable with the existing `otel_logging.py`): class `DataLogEmitter`.

- Builds its **own private `LoggerProvider`** (shared `Resource` definition with `otel_tracing.py:73-80` — extract the resource construction into one helper so service.name/instance/environment are identical across traces and logs) + `BatchLogRecordProcessor(OTLPLogExporter(endpoint, insecure))`.
- **Deliberately NOT set as the global logger provider and no `LoggingHandler` attached to stdlib/structlog** — this is a *data channel*, not app-log export. App logs stay on stdout exactly as today; the tracing-only stance for self-observability is preserved. This also keeps a clean seam for #339's two-plane design: this emitter is unambiguously "product-line emissions" plane.
- Public API: `emit(event_name: str, attributes: Mapping[str, str|int|float|bool], severity=INFO, body: str | None)` — wraps `opentelemetry._logs.LogRecord` + `Logger.emit()`. All `_logs` imports confined to this one module (rename-proofing).
- No-op when disabled: collectors call unconditionally; the emitter short-circuits (cheap boolean) so producer code has no config branching.
- Lifecycle: constructed in `ExporterApp.__init__` next to `app.py:145-151`; `shutdown()` (flush) next to `app.py:495-496`. Handed to collectors the same way `inventory`/`rate_limiter` are (`core/collector.py:79-88` — add one optional `data_log_emitter` kwarg; funnelled seam, orchestrator-owned per the wave rules).

**Config** (mirrors #339's proposed `otel.metrics` sub-block shape so the two epics converge on one `OTelSettings` structure):

```
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__LOGS__ENABLED=false                # off by default (hard requirement)
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__LOGS__ENDPOINT=...                 # optional; defaults to otel.endpoint
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__LOGS__INSECURE=<inherit otel.insecure>
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__LOGS__INCLUDE_IDENTIFIERS=false    # PII opt-in: mac/hostname/description attrs
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__LOGS__EVENTS=["wireless.client.packet_loss", ...]  # per-data-class allowlist, default = all built
```

New `OTelLogsSettings` nested under `OTelSettings` (`config_models.py:532`). Validator: `logs.enabled` requires an endpoint (own or inherited). Note: `otel.enabled` gates *tracing*; `otel.logs.enabled` is independent — an operator may want per-client logs without traces. Docgen picks this up via `make docgen`.

**Record schema** (bounded attribute keys, dot-namespaced per OTel conventions, matching the existing span-attr style in `otel_tracing.py:349-356`):

- Common: `event.name` (e.g. `meraki.wireless.client.packet_loss`), `org.id`, `network.id`, `network.name`, `device.serial` (when applicable), `client.id`, `data.window_seconds`, exporter resource attrs.
- Identifier attrs (`client.mac`, `client.hostname`, `client.description`) **only when `include_identifiers=true`** — consistent with the #533 ID-only stance and feeds the #559 GDPR doc.
- Per-class numeric payload as attributes, e.g. packet_loss: `downstream.loss_percent`, `upstream.loss_percent`, `total.loss_percent`, `downstream.total_packets`, etc. Body = compact human summary.
- Severity: INFO always (this is data, not alerting); no dynamic severity games.

**First producer (#323):** new fetch in `collectors/devices/mr/performance.py` (alongside the existing per-network packet loss fetch at `performance.py:569-617`) or a small sibling module — `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPacketLossByClient`, one bulk call per org, SLOW tier, wrapped in `validate_response_format`, Pydantic model for rows, then `emitter.emit(...)` per client row. Skipped entirely (no API call) when the emitter/event is disabled — zero rate-limit cost for non-users.

## 5. Coexistence with the tracing-only stance and #339

- Prometheus `/metrics` remains the **sole metrics surface**; this epic adds no metrics and touches no registry code. Docs change from "tracing only" to "traces (self-observability) + optional structured data logs (per-entity product data)" — `docs/observability/otel.md:12-13` rewritten accordingly.
- #339 (OTLP *metrics* bridge) is a sibling with the same two-plane doctrine; this emitter is purely the product plane. Shared seams to coordinate: the `Resource` helper and the `OTelSettings` sub-block shape (`otel.logs` now, `otel.metrics` later). No ordering dependency — either can land first; landing #622's sub-block first actually establishes the pattern #339 wants.

## 6. Build plan

- **Lane 0 (seam, orchestrator):** `OTelLogsSettings` in `core/config_models.py`; `data_log_emitter` kwarg on `MetricCollector.__init__` (`core/collector.py:79`); resource-helper extraction from `otel_tracing.py`. Small.
- **Lane 1 (core):** `core/otel_data_logs.py` (`DataLogEmitter`, no-op path, batch processor, shutdown/flush) + `app.py` wiring + unit tests using `InMemoryLogExporter` (verified importable). ~1 agent-day.
- **Lane 2 (first producer, #323):** MR per-client packet-loss fetcher + Pydantic model + emit + tests (factory rows → asserted log records via in-memory exporter; assert NO new Prometheus series). ~1 agent-day.
- **Lane 3 (docs):** rewrite `docs/observability/otel.md`, add the boundary rule to `docs/metrics/overview.md` + CLAUDE.md cardinality rules, `make docgen` for config, cross-link from #559's privacy doc. ~0.5 day.
- Total: **M (~2.5–3 agent-days)**, no new dependencies, no changes to existing metric surface, fully off by default. Gate: `make check` green + docgen.

## 7. Risks

1. **`_logs` namespace instability** — OTel Python still ships logs under `opentelemetry._logs` / `opentelemetry.sdk._logs` at 1.43.0 (verified; no public `sdk.logs` module exists yet). The Logs *Bridge* API is spec-stable but a future package rename would break imports. Mitigation: all imports confined to `core/otel_data_logs.py`; Renovate bump would fail loudly in CI, one-file fix.
2. **Volume** — a 10k-client network at MEDIUM cadence is ~10k records/5min. Mitigation: SLOW tier default for #323, `BatchLogRecordProcessor` queue caps (drop-oldest is acceptable for sampled telemetry), and document the volume math.
3. **Silent drop when misconfigured** — no backend ⇒ exporter retries then drops, invisibly. Mitigation: emit a `meraki_exporter_*` counter for records emitted/dropped (self-obs plane, bounded labels) so the feature is observable.
4. **Scope creep toward migrating `clients.py`** — explicitly out of scope; grandfathered surface stays.
5. **New surface days before v1** — mitigated by off-by-default + an explicit "experimental, schema may change until v1.x" marker under the new stability policy (GAP-01), which the log-record schema should be excluded from until proven.

## RECOMMENDATION

**Build for v1 — minimal scope: core emitter + one producer (#323) + docs; everything else fast-follow.** Reasoning: the marginal cost is unusually low (SDK + OTLP log exporter already pinned and verified importable — zero new dependencies; ~3 agent-days), it permanently closes #323 the *right* way (the issue itself warns against the metric form), and it lets v1 documentation state the metric-vs-log boundary rule as established policy rather than an IOU — which is exactly the kind of cardinality-doctrine clarity a v1 of a Prometheus exporter should ship with. Off-by-default + experimental-schema marking makes the launch risk negligible. Defer to fast-follow: per-client signal-quality records (#324's client half), webhook delivery log (#300), and any thought of migrating the grandfathered `clients.py` surface. If the v1 timeline is under acute pressure, the fallback is to land Lanes 0+1 (emitter + config, no producer) and hold #323 for v1.0.x — but the full minimal scope is preferred since a producer-less emitter is untestable in anger.

body:
Follow-up found while landing #511.

`core/batch_processing.py::process_in_batches_with_errors` catches per-item exceptions via `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` and only `logger.error(...)`s them — it never calls `_track_error`, so per-item batch failures (MS device batches, network-health bundles, etc., which run through this helper from `device.py`/`network_health.py`) do NOT surface in `meraki_exporter_collector_errors_total`. #511 instrumented the manual `except…continue` swallow sites but could not touch this file (out of its owned set, and the helper is a bare module function with no access to the counter).

**Fix:** give `process_in_batches_with_errors` a way to report per-item failures to the owning collectors error counter — e.g. an optional `on_error: Callable[[ErrorCategory], None]` / `error_sink` param that callers wire to `self._track_error`, incremented once per swallowed per-item exception. Keep control flow (return partial results) unchanged.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] A per-item exception inside `process_in_batches_with_errors` increments `meraki_exporter_collector_errors_total` for the calling collector.
- [ ] Existing callers in `device.py` / `network_health.py` pass the sink.
- [ ] Unit test: batch with one failing item → counter +1, partial results still returned.
- [ ] `core/batch_processing.py` is a funnelled seam — single owner.

body:
**Area:** `ops` · **Type:** `ops` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** V1-P6 · Release readiness & v1.0.0 cut

### Goal
The final gate before v1.0.0: verify the whole program end-to-end, then cut the release. This is the only issue in phase P6; it closes when v1.0.0 is published.

### Verification checklist (all must hold, with evidence)
- [x] `make check` green and `ci-success` green on main (no skips, no flaky reruns)
- [x] Docs site builds; `make docgen` produces no diff (generated docs current)
- [x] Golden /metrics exposition tests (#594) pass with the FINAL post-#531 metric names
- [x] Live soak against the homelab (key in gitignored `.env`, org <maintainer-org-id>): exporter runs ≥30 min, /metrics serves all expected families, zero 429 storms, rate-limiter metrics show budget headroom
- [x] #630 closed — scheduler live-verification (volatility floors, #271 byBand/6GHz shape, #549 MV field names, #331 conn-stats dedup verdict, perPage maxima). This is the itemised Phase-6 list the #271/#331/#549 closing comments deferred here; added 2026-07-03 when #617 was reopened.
- [x] #617 fully closed — #629 (gate-semantics gaps) and #631 (tier removal) landed; no FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW constructs remain in code/config/metrics/docs
- [x] Honest-health regression: run with an INVALID key → /ready stays 503, failure_streak > 0, /health flips after the staleness threshold (the #509 contract)
- [x] Fresh-install walkthrough: README quickstart (compose) and Helm install both work exactly as written against a clean environment
- [x] Support matrix (#566), upgrade guide (#571), and stability policy (#535) accurately reflect what actually shipped — spot-check every claim
- [x] Every breaking change is in the upgrade guide: metric renames + unit changes (#531), single-org contract (#585), client label contract (#533), any config renames
- [x] All phase P0–P5 issues closed (or explicitly moved to P7/post-v1 with Rob's sign-off recorded on the issue)

### Cutting the release (mechanics — do not improvise)
release-please derives versions from conventional commits; nothing in the phases above will naturally trigger a 0.x → 1.0.0 major bump. To cut exactly v1.0.0, land an empty-change commit on main with a `Release-As` footer:

```
chore: release 1.0.0

Release-As: 1.0.0
```

(Alternatively a `feat!:` commit would major-bump, but pre-1.0 release-please treats breaking bumps as minor unless `bump-minor-pre-major` config says otherwise — the `Release-As` footer is deterministic; use it.) Then: release-please opens the release PR (authored via the PAT so CI runs) → verify CI green on that PR → **Rob personally approves and merges it** (⚖ human gate — the agent must stop and ask). Merge triggers: tag, GHCR image (semver + latest, signed, SBOM), OCI Helm chart, GitHub Release with artifacts.

### Post-cut sanity
- [x] `docker pull ghcr.io/rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter:1.0.0` works; container serves /health + /metrics
- [x] `helm install` from `oci://ghcr.io/rknightion/charts/meraki-dashboard-exporter --version 1.0.0` renders and deploys
- [x] Release notes readable and complete; cosign signature verifies

### Notes / risks
Master tracker: #618 (phase P6). Evidence pack: `evidence/`. Do not start this issue until P0–P5 are complete. P7 (dashboards/alerting, M16 issues) intentionally follows the v1 cut unless Rob decides otherwise at this gate — ask him at the ⚖ point.

<sub>Created 2026-07-02 as part of the v1 launch master plan (#618).</sub>

comments.body:
**Execution routing (for #618 orchestration):** agent model: `opus` · thinking effort: `high`.

The orchestrator spawns one dedicated subagent per issue with these settings and implements nothing itself. Implementer: if this issue turns out materially harder than scoped (cross-seam impact, unclear design, contradicting evidence), STOP and report back for escalation to a stronger model — do not improvise architecture.

## 📋 Phase-6 live-API verification checklist (accumulating)

Per Rob's decision (build spec-only, verify at Phase 6), these items were coded against the OpenAPI spec + SDK introspection and MUST be confirmed against the live homelab org (and, where noted, other fleets) before the v1.0.0 cut. Most are **cost-model accuracy** (affect the scheduler's demand math, not correctness); a few are **response-shape** (affect emitted data).

### #617 scheduler cost/floor freezes (perPage maxima + data windows)
- `device_availability` / `org_availabilities` — `pages(device_count, 500)` perPage assumption; floor 120.
- `mr_wireless_clients` `pages(MR,1000)`; `mr_ethernet_status` `pages(MR,1000)`; `mr_packet_loss` `2×pages(MR,1000)`; `mr_ssid_status` `pages(MR,500)`; `mr_ssid_usage` floor 900 (daily-summary window).
- `ms_port_overview` floor 3600 (43200s data window); `ms_power` `pages(MS,1000)`.
- `mx_uplink_status` `pages(MX,1000)`; confirm `getOrganizationApplianceSecurityEvents` timespan and the 900s `mx_performance`/`mx_firewall_config` windows.
- `mt_sensor_readings` perPage=100 divisor for `getOrganizationSensorReadingsLatest`.
- `mv_analytics` floor 900 — confirm the analytics data window supports it.

### #271 — org-wide channel-utilization response shape (correctness)
- `byBand[].band` values assumed `"2.4"`/`"5"`/`"6"` (spec sample only showed `"5"`).
- `byBand[].{wifi,nonWifi,total}.percentage` camelCase key names (legacy per-network used snake_case `non_wifi`).
- **6GHz decision:** `band=="6"` rows are currently dropped (no 6GHz gauge). Decide whether to add a series.

### #331 — connection-stats dedup (investigation)
- Live field-diff `mr_connection_stats` (getNetworkWirelessDevicesConnectionStats) vs `nh_connection_stats` (connection_stats.py). If redundant, delete one group. Both fetchers currently kept.

### #549 — MV analytics (note)
- `getDeviceCameraAnalyticsZones` was **kept** (still functional in SDK 3.3.0; sole source of `mv_zone_info` #534 zone labels, no label-preserving successor). Confirm live; verify the analytics-live/quality endpoints still return the expected shapes.

## 🔬 Phase-6 live-verification checklist — Phase-4 wave 4A additions (commit 13bf859)

All wave-4A area metrics shipped **spec-only** where live hardware/config was unavailable (homelab = MR/MS/MT + 2×MV; **no MX, no MG**). Pydantic models are lenient (`extra="allow"`, uncertain fields Optional) so schema drift degrades to "metric not emitted", never a crash. Verify each below against a live capture (working key in gitignored `.env`) or the vendored OpenAPI spec before v1.

### MX — ALL spec-only (no MX hardware) 🔴
- `getNetworkApplianceContentFiltering` / `getNetworkApplianceSecurityMalware` / `getNetworkApplianceSecurityIntrusion` (#285) — field names (`blockedUrlCategories` shape, `idsRulesets`, mode enums); malware/intrusion 400/404 without Advanced Security license.
- `getDeviceApplianceDhcpSubnets` (#286) — row shape `subnet,vlanId,usedCount,freeCount`.
- `getNetworkApplianceVpnSiteToSiteVpn` (#287) — `mode`, `hubs[].hubId`, subnet `useVpn` flag.
- `getNetworkApplianceFirewallPortForwardingRules` / `OneToOneNatRules` / `OneToManyNatRules` (#288).
- `getNetworkApplianceVlans` (HTTP 400 when VLANs disabled) / `getNetworkApplianceStaticRoutes` (#289).

### MG — ALL spec-only (no MG hardware) 🔴
- `getOrganizationDevicesCellularUplinksBandsByDevice` (#304) — bands nesting/field names (`connectionType` vs `type` vs `rat`; slot→RAT→status structure). Handles 2 shapes defensively.
- `getOrganizationDevicesCellularUplinksTowersByDevice` (#304) — serving-cell field names (`cellId`/`id`/`cid`, `tac`/`trackingAreaCode`); "one serving cell per MG" assumption.

### MR — live-verifiable (homelab MR) 🟡
- `getNetworkWirelessSsidFirewallL3FirewallRules` (#290) — top-level `allowLanAccess` bool presence; `comment=="Default rule"` heuristic for excluding the trailing default row.
- `getOrganizationWirelessRfProfilesAssignmentsByDevice` (#291) — row shape; **`isIndoorDefault`/`isOutdoorDefault` flags are a guess** (documented on a different endpoint) — if absent, `is_default` always reads "false" (under-reports, never false-positive).

### MS — live-verifiable (homelab MS) 🟡
- `getNetworkSwitchDhcpV4ServersSeen` (#292) — `isAllowed` field name (missing→"not allowed").
- `getNetworkSwitchDhcpServerPolicyArpInspectionWarningsByDevice` (#293) — **REAL DISCREPANCY flagged**: SDK docstring implies a `warnings: [...]` array (non-compliant devices only), not the `supportsInspection`/`hasTrustedPort` boolean-coverage row in the spec. Implemented per frozen spec defensively; may need remapping from `warnings` after live check.
- `getOrganizationSummarySwitchPowerHistory` (#294) — datapoint field (`draw` vs `usage`) + ordering/lag for HELP.
- `getNetworkSwitchLinkAggregations` (#295) — row shape `id, switchPorts[{serial,portId}]`.
- `getOrganizationSwitchPortsStatusesBySwitch` (#296) — confirm `cdp`/`lldp` objects present on the **org-wide** payload (only the per-device endpoint was spec'd); if absent, coverage degrades to the per-device fallback path.

### Org — mostly live-verifiable 🟡
- Top-N usage (#299) — **usage UNITS** (assumed decimal kB→bytes ×1000 per `client_overview.py` precedent; do not trust until confirmed), the `usage`/`total` container + client-`id` field names, allowed `timespan`.
- Webhook logs (#300) — `responseCode` field name (→ status_code; missing→"0").
- Adaptive policy (#298) — `counts.{groups,customAcls,policies}`; 404 unless licensed (homelab likely unlicensed → may stay spec-only).
- Firmware compliance (#611) — by-device `upgrade.status`/top-level `status` + value vocabulary; confirm device dicts carry `firmware`.

### Sensor/Camera — hardware-dependent 🟡
- MT20/MT30 button (#303) — `button.pressType` + reading `ts`; needs an MT20/MT30 (absent → no rows, documented normal).
- MV Sense (#305) — `senseEnabled`, `mqttBrokerId`; needs a Sense-capable camera.
- Camera onboarding (#306) — response shape (network id field) + bounded `status` vocab (unknown→"other" keeps cardinality safe).
- Sensor relationships (#308) — `device.serial` + `relationships.livestream.relatedDevices[{serial,productType}]`; needs an MT↔MV pairing.

### Network-health 🟡
- Wireless mesh (#307) — shape (`serial`, `latestMeshPerformance.{mbps,metric,usagePercentage}`), `usagePercentage` string-vs-number, null-on-fresh-repeater; needs mesh repeaters (absent in homelab → emits nothing).
- **Air Marshal threat_type (#612) — GATING 🔴**: the `type`/`threatType` field is **confirmed ABSENT from the current cached OpenAPI spec**. Gauge emits all-zero buckets today. **Mandatory live homelab MR check**: if the live API returns no such field, DROP `meraki_mr_air_marshal_bssids_by_threat_type_count` and treat #612 as docstring-refresh-only (docstring already refreshed).

## 🔬 Phase-6 verification — Phase-4B additions (commit ae13759)

Deferred-set metrics shipped, each `enabled_fn`-gated (absent family = zero cost). Lenient local Pydantic models throughout.

### Live-verifiable (homelab MR present) 🟡
- **#324** per-AP signal quality — confirm `getNetworkWirelessSignalQualityHistory` `snr`/`rssi` newest-non-null-bucket selection + null behaviour; verify AP-tag scoping against real tagged devices.
- **#325** power mode — confirm the actual `powerMode` string vocabulary (e.g. `full`/`low`) on `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesPowerModeHistory`.

### Spec-only (no hardware/license) 🔴
- **#326** Catalyst controllers — no CW* APs in homelab: verify `joinedAt` format (ISO-8601 parse) + `mode`/`countryCode` vocabularies on `getOrganizationWirelessDevicesWirelessControllersByDevice`.
- **#327** eSIM — no MG: verify `getOrganizationCellularGatewayEsimsInventory` shape, esp. the "active profile" discriminator (`profiles[].status=="active"` vs the eSIM-level `active` bool).
- **#328** MG HA — no MG: verify `highAvailability.role` vocabulary is `{primary,spare}` and MG rows are reliably `model`-prefix-identifiable in `getOrganizationUplinksStatuses`.
- **#330** MX uplink overview — no MX: verify `getOrganizationApplianceUplinksStatusesOverview` nests as `counts.byStatus.{...}` and whether all five status keys are always present vs sparse.
- **#613** Insight — no Insight license + no MX: verify `getOrganizationInsightApplications` shape; `getNetworkInsightApplicationHealthByTime` "complete bucket" semantics + null-field behaviour; exact 400-vs-404 error shape for a non-Insight org; `wanGoodput`/`lanGoodput` units (kept excluded until verified).

## ⚠ Phase-6 live-verification items — Wave 4D (beta early-access + OTLP metrics bridge)

Added by Wave 4D (commits cd76d8d #278/#279, 2b9400c #313/#314/#339). These shipped spec-only / cannot be verified in CI; verify against the homelab (and a real OTLP backend) before the v1.0.0 cut.

### Early-access collector (cd76d8d, #278/#279)
- [ ] Confirm the homelab org returns rows from `getOrganizationEarlyAccessFeaturesOptIns` and that field names match the lenient model (`shortName`, `id`, `createdAt`, `limitScopeToNetworks`). The model degrades gracefully on drift (rows skipped, no run failure), but eyeball the `has_beta_api` shortName match and the `limitScopeToNetworks` list shape against live data. (Stable + SDK-native, so this should just work.)

### OTLP metrics bridge (2b9400c, #339/#313/#314) — needs a real exporter → OTel Collector → Prometheus/Mimir round-trip
This is the parity oracle; none of it is testable in CI.

body:
## Mission

Implement **every open issue in this repository** and ship **v1.0.0**. When the phases below are complete, GitHub Project #2 is 100% done and the project graduates from pre-release to its first stable release. There are **no interim releases** — everything lands on `main` continuously and ships together at v1, so sequence for build-coherence, never for "relief".

**This issue is the parent tracker.** The orchestrating agent works from it directly — no scratch files. Progress lives here (see *Tracker protocol*) and on the individual issues, so any future session can resume from GitHub alone.

**Milestones ARE the phases.** Every open issue sits in exactly one `V1-P0`…`V1-P7` milestone matching the phases below — `gh issue list --milestone "V1-P2 · Correctness & platform fan-out" --state open` is always the authoritative worklist for a phase. (The old thematic M1–M16 milestones are closed history.)

## Operating rules (binding)

1. **Read every issue IN FULL: the description AND every comment.** Enrichment comments carry binding contract rules (naming, budget, single-org), evidence-pack pointers, dedupe verdicts, and decisions — an issue's comments frequently override or extend its body. Skipping comments is how work gets done twice or wrong.
2. **The orchestrator is a PURE SCHEDULER — it implements nothing, ever.** Recommended setup: a Fable session at LOW thinking effort. Its only jobs: dispatch one dedicated subagent per issue, sequence phases/lanes per this plan, run the mechanical gate commands, commit/push/close on green evidence, and keep this tracker current. It never writes code, never authors docs, never debugs a failure — a red `make check` or merge conflict spawns a **fixer subagent (`opus`/high)** scoped to that failure. All planning intelligence is already front-loaded into this issue; the orchestrator follows it.
3. **Respect each issue's execution routing — it is binding.** Every open issue carries `model:{fable|opus|sonnet}` + `thinking:{high|medium}` labels AND an "Execution routing" comment. Spawn the subagent with exactly that model and thinking effort. Implementer subagents own one lane each (disjoint file sets, one file = one owner), never commit, never run `gh`, and return self-contained final-message briefs. If an implementer reports the issue is materially harder than scoped, escalate one model tier (sonnet→opus→fable) — never let it improvise architecture.
4. **`fable-candidate` issues (#617 #531 #509 #533 #540 #545 #534 #614 #339):** spawn a dedicated **Fable/high subagent** whose FIRST deliverable is the design/spec posted on the issue; implementation is then delegated per that spec (which states the implementer routing). This keeps the low-effort orchestrator viable — the deep thinking happens in the subagent, not the scheduler. If Fable subagents are unavailable in the session, post a comment here naming the blocked issue and ask Rob to run it in a Fable session; do NOT downgrade these nine.
5. **Consult `evidence/` before coding any issue** — verified research (capacity math, per-fetcher conformance tables, live-API samples, live failure-run evidence). Treat its facts as solved data; re-confirm only file:line refs that may have drifted. Start with `evidence/README.md`.
6. **Validate-before-implement.** Re-confirm each mechanism in current code; confirm SDK methods/response shapes against the installed SDK and OpenAPI spec — and remember **the spec is wrong for some endpoints** (`evidence/live-api-verification.md`): when an issue flags live verification, do it first (working homelab key in the gitignored `.env`; org `<maintainer-org-id>`, MR/MS/MT + 2×MV, co-term licensing, no MX/MG).
7. **Per issue:** TDD (failing test → minimal fix → green) → scoped tests green → full `make check` green (evidence, not assertion) → `make docgen` when metrics/config changed → one commit to `main` with `Closes #N` → push. Tightly-coupled issues that are literally one change to one file may share a commit with multiple `Closes` trailers.
8. **Seams are funnelled, never parallelised:** `core/metrics.py`, `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`, `core/collector.py`, `core/metric_expiration.py`, `manager.py`, `config_models.py`, and the coordinators (`device.py`, `organization.py`, `network_health.py`) get ONE owner per wave.
9. **Dashboards stay frozen** until Phase 7 (`dashboards/CLAUDE.md`): never edit `dashboards/*.json` in a code fix; never defer a fix fearing dashboard breakage.
10. **Stale issues are closed, not forced:** if re-verification shows an issue already fixed or its premise wrong, say so on the issue and close it — e.g. #272/#273 are suspected already-done.
11. **Ask Rob only at genuine product forks** (⚖ below, and rule 3's deferrals). Everything else: proceed.

### Decisions already made — do NOT re-litigate
- Metric names: **rename now, pre-1.0, no dual-emit** (#531).
- Client metrics: **ID-only numeric series + `meraki_client_info` join** (#533).
- Distribution: **container + Helm only**, no PyPI (#602).
- **1 poller = 1 organisation** (breaking; fail-fast on multi-org keys) (#585).
- No interim releases; v1 is the next release.
- Mutable name labels: **dropped from numeric series; join via `_info` metrics** (#534, decided 2026-07-02 — analysis deliverable skipped, straight to spec+implementation).

### Model guidance
Routing is per-issue via `model:*`/`thinking:*` labels + the "Execution routing" comment (rule 3) — do not re-derive it. Distribution: 9× fable/high (design), ~31× opus/high, ~36× opus/medium, ~52× sonnet/high, ~47× sonnet/medium. Fixer/escalation subagents default to opus/high. The P6 gate issue (#619) runs opus/high with the ⚖ human release approval.

## Tracker protocol

- The orchestrator **edits this issue's body** to tick the phase checkboxes below and posts a **phase-completion comment** after each phase: issues closed (with commit SHAs), issues re-scoped/closed-stale, deviations, fable-candidate deferrals pending, and anything queued for Rob.
- Individual issues get a closing comment stating what was done. Parked items get a comment stating exactly what blocks them.
- If context runs out mid-phase, the successor session resumes from this issue + the phase comments alone.

## Phase plan (milestone = worklist; lanes inside a phase run in parallel over disjoint files)

### ☑ Phase 0 — `V1-P0 · Unblock CI` (serial, first)
#508. Nothing else commits cleanly until `ci-success` is green.

### ☑ Phase 1 — `V1-P1 · Metric contract seam` (ONE lane, serial; blocks all collector edits)
#531 ⚡fable (the sweep — rename table in body + `evidence/metric-contract-audit.md`), then #532 #538 #539 #536 #537 #535.
⚖ #534 ⚡fable (mutable name-label policy) — analyse, recommend to Rob, implement his call.
Everything after this phase uses final metric names.

### ☑ Phase 2 — `V1-P2 · Correctness & platform fan-out` (parallel lanes)
- **core-resilience (seam owner):** #509 ⚡fable #510 #511 #528 #547
- **network-health:** #512 #524 #555
- **org/config/licensing:** #513 #516 #519 #522 #523 #551
- **device-collectors:** #517 #521 #526 #527 #520 #525 #530
- **clients:** #533 ⚡fable #543
- **config-surface:** #514 #515 #518 #529 #585 #586 #587 #588 #589 #590 #598 #599 #312 #310
- **web-ui/status:** #311 #317 #319
- **security/webhook:** #558 #561 #564
- **chart/docker:** #560 #562 #563 #600 #601 #603 #606 #318
- **CI/tests:** #592 #593 #594 #595 #605 #607 #608 #609 #283
- **docs (part 1):** #565 #571 #572 #573 #574 #575 #576 #577 #602 #604 #610 #281 #284

### ☑ Phase 3 — `V1-P3 · Rate-limit & scale program` (the centrepiece)
- **3a pre-work (parallel):** #270 #545 ⚡fable #548 #550 #553 #544 #546 #556 #557 #554 #274 #276 #277 #540 ⚡fable #309 #597
- **3b scheduler:** write the **#617 ⚡fable design doc first** (`evidence/scale-and-capacity.md` is the cost model). ⚖ Present to Rob: adaptive scheduler in v1, or fixed tiers + hand gates? The design decides the fate of #541 #549 #552 #591 #596 (absorbed as solver floors vs simple gates), resolves #275, evaluates #320, and settles #271 #331 (verify live field names first; #272 #273 suspected already-done — verify & close).
- **3c guidance:** #542 (sizing formula) + #568 (sharding/HA guide) + comment-and-close #218 with the concrete answer.

### ☑ Phase 4 — `V1-P4 · Signal expansion (new metrics)` (post-contract, post-scheduler; parallel area lanes)
All new metrics follow the post-#531 contract + budget rules (each issue's enrichment comment binds).
- **beta-api:** #278 first (plumbing), then #279 #280 #282
- **by area:** MX #285 #286 #287 #288 #289 · wireless #290 #291 #307 · switch #292 #293 #295 #296 · org #294 #297 #298 #299 #300 #301 · sensor/camera #302 #303 #304 #305 #306 #308 · plus #611 #612
- **deferred/optional (⚖ propose descoping to Rob where cost/value is poor):** #321 #322 #323 #324 #325 #326 #327 #328 #330 #613 #614 ⚡fable #615
- **OTLP:** #339 ⚡fable (epic) + #313 + #314

### ☑ Phase 5 — `V1-P5 · Final docs & onboarding` (needs Phase 3/4 outcomes)
#566 (support matrix — final coverage) · #567 (freshness — final scheduler) · #569 (alert rules — final names) · #570 (runbook) · #559 (privacy) · #616 (positioning).

### ☐ Phase 6 — `V1-P6 · Release readiness & v1.0.0 cut`
Work #619 — the full verification checklist AND the release mechanics (v1.0.0 requires a `Release-As: 1.0.0` commit; release-please will not major-bump on its own). ⚖ Ends with Rob personally approving and merging the release PR → **v1.0.0**.

### ☐ Phase 7 — `V1-P7 · Dashboard & alerting rebuild` (dedicated specialist session)
#578–#584 + full rebuild using post-sweep metric names (worklist: `dashboards/CLAUDE.md`), then #315 (provisioning example ships the NEW dashboards) and #316 (dashboard-vs-metrics CI check). Run as its own Grafana-specialist session; this issue tracks completion. Grafana alerting rides with this phase.

## Out of scope
#170 (Renovate bot housekeeping — leave alone). Nothing else: every other open issue appears above.

<sub>Created 2026-07-02 as the master tracker for the v1 launch; restructured same day so milestones V1-P0…P7 mirror these phases exactly. Deliberately not in Project #2 or any milestone. Evidence pack: `evidence/` (commit 8f3168a). ⚡fable = `fable-candidate` label (rule 3).</sub>

**Orchestration note (binding for future sessions) — how to actually set subagent thinking effort:**

The plain `Agent` tool in Claude Code **inherits the orchestrator session's reasoning effort** and only exposes a `model` override — so a low-effort orchestrator session silently dispatches low-effort subagents regardless of the issue's `thinking:high` label.

To honour the per-issue `model:*` + `thinking:*` routing labels, dispatch implementer/design subagents via the **Workflow tool**, whose `agent(prompt, {model, effort})` call supports an explicit per-agent `effort` override ('low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max'). Example: a `model:opus thinking:high` issue → `agent(prompt, {model: 'opus', effort: 'high'})`. Alternatively run the orchestrator itself at an effort ≥ the highest routed tier, but the Workflow route is the correct one for a low-effort scheduler session (which remains the recommended setup per rule 2).

(Noted 2026-07-02 after #508 was dispatched effort-inherited-low; Rob approved letting that one and the in-flight #531 design run as-is.)

**Area:** `core` · **Type:** `feature/epic` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Milestone:** V1-P3 · **Status: REOPENED 2026-07-03** — phase 2 (full de-tiering) + audit follow-ups remain.

# Adaptive budget-aware API scheduler — epic status & remaining work

## TL;DR for a fresh agent

Phase 1 (the adaptive solver) is **built, merged, and green** — a 2026-07-03 read-only audit found it structurally conformant to its build spec. But that spec deliberately kept the FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW tier loops as heartbeats, and Rob has rejected that compromise: **the tiers must be removed as constructs entirely.** The remaining work is the three sub-issues below; each embeds its full spec. Do NOT redesign the solver — it stays; only the dispatch layer, config surface, and observability surface change.

## Where to read what (the comments on this issue are the historical record)

1. **Design doc** (comment 2026-07-03 03:13): Option A vs B analysis, verified cost model, volatility floors, per-sibling-issue map. Rob chose Option A (adaptive solver in v1).
2. **Build spec** (comment 2026-07-03 06:09): the frozen-interface spec the implementation followed — the ~50-group endpoint table (priorities/floors/cost functions), seam signatures, AIMD semantics, wave plan. **Its §1a "tiers remain heartbeats" execution model is the part Rob overturned on 2026-07-03**; everything else in it accurately describes the code on `main`.
3. **This body**: current state + remaining work. Where this body conflicts with the older comments, this body wins.

## What landed (commits on `main`)

- `3e20f34` wave 0 — `core/scheduler.py` (pure `solve_intervals` + `EndpointScheduler`), `SchedulerSettings`, scheduler self-metrics + `LabelName.GROUP`, collector gate helpers, per-series `ttl_seconds` expiration override.
- `3071792` wave 1 — AIMD 429 feedback on `OrgRateLimiter` (wired from the single retry-owner in `error_handling.py`), `OrgShape` from inventory, manager wiring + startup demand-vs-budget log, `/status` + index scheduler sections, `_scheduler_resolve_loop`.
- `2cb500d` wave 2 — every fetch site gated by endpoint group; folded #541 (windowed NH floors), #549 (MV migration + own interval), #552 (MX perf gate), #271 (org-wide channel-util), #331 (1800s conn-stats gating). Closed this issue the first time.
- `ead1217`→`ae13759` — Phase-4/4B groups registered on the same scheduler (~80 groups now).
- `make check` green on `main` as of 2026-07-03. Adaptive mode is the shipped default (`scheduler.mode=adaptive`).

## Why reopened (Rob, 2026-07-03)

The exporter still runs three tier pollers — visible in any deployment's logs — because the build spec froze "tiers remain heartbeats; the solver only stretches". Structural consequences Rob rejects:

- **Quantization:** groups can never run faster than their tier heartbeat, so `device_availability` (floor 120s) really runs at 300s — the epic's own "up-ness ≤120s" criterion is silently unmet (the spec admitted this; its optional workaround lane was never built).
- **Two vocabularies:** operators see tiers (config, logs, `tier` self-metric label, /status) *and* endpoint groups.
- **Vestigial surface at v1:** `UPDATE_INTERVALS__*`, per-tier concurrency knobs, tier-keyed TTL fallback, tier-derived readiness/liveness — v1 is the only breaking-change moment; shipping them bakes them into the stable contract.
