# Design doc — #617 Adaptive budget-aware API scheduler (design-only, for Rob's decision)

## 0. TL;DR and the decision

**Decision for Rob:** ship the adaptive solver in v1, or ship fixed FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW tiers + hand-tuned per-endpoint interval gates (with the cost model as an advisory startup check)?

**Recommendation: Option B — fixed tiers + gates in v1, plus the *advisory* half of the solver (cost model, demand-vs-budget startup log, /status section, gauges), deferring the closed-loop interval-mutating solver to post-v1.** The key insight from reading the current code: the adaptive scheduler's execution mechanism *is* the gate pattern the codebase already has six instances of (`ms_port_usage_interval` etc., `config_models.py:218-240`; `_should_collect_static_config`, `mv.py:129-143`; `mx_firewall.py:55-75`) — the solver only changes *who computes the gate values* (a startup solver vs. hand-set defaults). So gates built for v1 are the substrate of the adaptive scheduler, not throwaway work, and the epic's phase-1 (cost model + transparency) still lands in v1 with near-zero soak risk. Full tradeoffs in §5.

---

## 1. Current mechanics (grounded, verified 2026-07-03)

- Three independent tier loops (`app.py:452-467` creates them; `_tiered_collection_loop` at `app.py:488+`), intervals from `UpdateIntervals` (`config_models.py:300-315`: fast=60, medium=300, slow=900). Each loop calls `CollectorManager.collect_tier(tier)` (`manager.py:534`), which fans collectors out under `ManagedTaskGroup` with per-tier concurrency (`manager.py:578-591`) and per-collector smoothing offsets (`manager.py:584`, deterministic hash of name, capped at 0.5×interval, `manager.py:38,213`).
- The scheduling unit is **collector × tier**; the cost unit is **endpoint group inside a collector**. `DeviceCollector` (MEDIUM) internally mixes 300s, 600s, and 900s cadences via self-managed timestamp gates. This unit mismatch is why "make MEDIUM slower" can't fix anything — and why any redesign must schedule endpoint groups, not collectors.
- Client-side limiter: `OrgRateLimiter` token bucket, `rate = 10 × rate_limit_shared_fraction`, burst 20 (`core/rate_limiter.py:42-46`); pure open-loop — no 429/Retry-After feedback path exists today.
- Per-collector timeout 240s (`collectors.collector_timeout`); collector lock prevents self-overlap (`manager.py:669-677`).
- Metric expiration TTL is **tier-keyed only**: `_set_metric` passes `tier=self.update_tier` (`core/collector.py:650`) and `_get_ttl_for_tier` maps tier→interval×2.0 (`metric_expiration.py:199-220`, multiplier default `config_models.py:353-358`). **Consequence (cross-cutting constraint, §7): any fetch gated slower than 2× its collector's tier interval has its series expired between fetches.** The existing 900s gates inside MEDIUM DeviceCollector (MX firewall, MV static config, MS STP) already sit past the 600s TTL — a latent flap that #541-style gating would multiply. Both options need a per-series TTL override on the `track_metric_update` seam.

## 2. Cost model (validated against current fetchers)

The issue's sketch `calls/cycle ≈ 8W + 20O + MS/2 + ⌈MR/20⌉ + MV + physMX + pagination` matches `evidence/scale-and-capacity.md` §2 and I re-verified the load-bearing terms in code:

| Group | Calls/cycle (current) | Verified at |
|---|---|---|
| NetworkHealth bundle | **8×W per 300s** — still no gating, incl. per-network channel-util | bundle `network_health.py:395-403`; `rf_health.py:125` still on per-network `getNetworkNetworkHealthChannelUtilization` (#271 NOT done) |
| Device | ~20/org + 1×W (MR conn-stats, `mr/clients.py:134`) + MS/2 @600s + ⌈MR/20⌉ CPU + 1×MV live @300s + 2MV/3 @900s + physMX (`mx.py:171`, ungated) + Sw + Sw/3 + 2A/3 | per evidence table + spot-checks |
| Org+Alerts+MT+Config | ~0.4 rps at LARGE | evidence §2 |
| Pagination | memory-usage 500 pages/org/cycle at 5k devices | `devices/base.py:106-112` |

Totals stand: **SMALL ~0.43 rps (4%); LARGE-1org ~17.8 rps (178% of the 10 rps org budget)**, NetworkHealth alone infeasible inside its own 240s timeout at 400 wireless nets (evidence §3). Treat these as solved data.

**Post-pre-work estimate** (#271 org-wide channel-util, #541 floors, #548 perPage, #552, #549, MR conn-stats gated to its 1800s window): NetworkHealth 10.7 → ~3.3 rps (data-rates + bluetooth stay at 300s: 2.7; windowed endpoints gated: ~0.6); Device 6.7 → ~4.2; total **≈ 8 rps ≈ 100% of the shared-fraction budget (0.8×10, #550)** at the university profile. i.e. gates alone get LARGE from "physically impossible" to "at budget, tight"; the adaptive solver's marginal value at that scale is auto-stretching the class-3/4 groups to create headroom without operator tuning.

## 3. Volatility floors (per endpoint group)

Floor = the endpoint's natural data window; polling faster is pure waste. From evidence + issue #541 (each to be live-verified per APIORG-01 before freezing values):

| Group | Floor | Priority class |
|---|---|---|
| Device/org up-ness, availabilities, alerts | 60–120s (availabilities TTL already 120s, `inventory.py`) | 1 |
| MT sensor readings | 60s | 2 |
| Channel-util (org-wide, post-#271), data-rates, bluetooth, MR CPU, MS ports | 300s | 3 |
| MS packet stats / port usage | 600s (existing) | 3 |
| Wireless connection-stats (both `connection_stats.py` and `mr/clients.py` — same 1800s window) | 1800s | 3 |
| Failed-connections, latency (client+device), air-marshal | 3600s | 3 |
| MX perf (#552), MV analytics (#549), MV/MX/MS static config | 900s | 3–4 |
| Config, licensing, login-security, inventory | 900–3600s | 4 |

## 4. Option A — the adaptive solver (design sketch)

1. **Registration:** each collector declares `EndpointGroup(name, priority: 1-4, floor_s, cost_fn(OrgShape) -> calls_per_cycle)` — a class-level registry on `MetricCollector` (`core/collector.py`), populated by coordinators/sub-collectors. `OrgShape` (W, Sw, A, Sn, per-type device counts) comes from `OrganizationInventory` post-warm.
2. **Solve** (startup + each inventory refresh, i.e. ~900s): start every group at its floor; `demand = Σ cost_i / interval_i`; while `demand > budget × target_utilization` (budget = `10 × rate_limit_shared_fraction`, target ~0.7): stretch the lowest-priority, least-stretched group ×1.5, capped at `min(4×floor, 3600s)`; recompute. Deterministic, ~trivial CPU. If still over budget at all caps → loud startup warning naming the collectors to disable (this is the #218 guidance moment).
3. **Execute:** do NOT invent per-group timers. Keep the three tier loops as heartbeats and make every fetch site consult `schedule.should_run(group_key)` — the identical shape to today's `_should_collect_*` gates, with the interval read from the solver instead of a setting. This is the de-risked execution model: tiers remain, the solver just writes gate values.
4. **Feedback (AIMD):** on observed 429/Retry-After (needs #545's single retry-owner first), multiply effective budget ×0.5, additively recover +0.1 rps per clean minute; re-solve only when effective budget moves >20% (hysteresis). Absorbs external consumers sharing the org budget.
5. **Restart semantics:** gate timestamps are in-memory; a restart refetches every group once — acceptable because startup is already sequential-by-tier (`manager.py:486-490`).
6. **Compatibility:** `UPDATE_INTERVALS__*` become overrides layered on the solver; `scheduler_mode = "fixed"` (setting, §6) bypasses the solver entirely and uses the gate defaults.

**Blast radius A:** `manager.py`, `core/collector.py` (registration), every coordinator's fetch sites (~15 gate consultations), `core/metric_expiration.py` (per-series TTL, §7), `app.py` (readiness + liveness must derive from *computed* fastest cadence, interacts with #596), `config_models.py`, `/status`, docs. Effort L–XL. Risk: transient scheduling behavior is exactly the kind of thing that only soak reveals, and v1 has no soak runway ("no interim releases" — this ships untested-in-anger to every user simultaneously).

## 5. Option B — fixed tiers + gates + advisory cost model (recommended)

- Implement #541/#549/#552 as settings-backed timestamp gates using the existing pattern (values = §3 floors). ~6 new `APISettings` fields + gate checks at the fetch sites; the pattern has 6 precedents.
- Implement the **cost model as a read-only advisor**: a new `core/schedule_advisor.py` (~200 lines) that computes demand from org shape at startup/inventory-refresh, emits the observability surface (§6), and logs `your org needs ~X req/s; budget is Y; consider: <specific knobs>`. No behavior change, no soak risk, and it IS the solver's phase-1 — post-v1, Option A becomes "wire the advisor's output into the gates + add AIMD".
- **Tradeoff stated honestly:** at the 500-net university profile Option B lands at ~100% of the shared budget — workable but with zero headroom; a customer at that scale may still need to turn the documented knobs (disable MV/clients, stretch data-rates/bluetooth) that the advisor now names explicitly. Option A would do that stretching automatically. Below ~200 wireless nets (the overwhelming majority of orgs) the two options are behaviorally identical because nothing needs stretching.
- **Blast radius B:** `config_models.py`, ~6 fetch sites, 1 new advisory module, `metric_expiration.py` TTL override (§7, needed under both options), `/status`. Effort M. Risk low.

**Why B:** rate-limiting pain is fixed ~80% by pre-work + gates; the solver's remaining 20% (auto-stretch, AIMD) is precisely the 20% with the highest soak risk; nothing in B is thrown away when A lands post-v1; and the customer-guidance half of #218 (the "discover saturation by hitting it" complaint) ships either way via the advisor.

## 6. Observability surface + fallback setting (both options)

- Gauges (new `CollectorMetricName` members, orchestrator seam): `SCHEDULER_ESTIMATED_DEMAND_RPS` (`meraki_exporter_scheduler_estimated_demand_rps{group}`), `SCHEDULER_BUDGET_RPS`, `SCHEDULER_BUDGET_UTILIZATION_RATIO`, `SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_SECONDS{group}` (+ `SCHEDULER_<net-name-6>ETCH_FACTOR{group}` and effective-budget under A). Label: new `LabelName.GROUP` (or reuse existing if orchestrator prefers).
- `/status`: "org shape → per-group demand → budget → chosen intervals (+ stretch under A)" — extend `get_scheduling_diagnostics()` (`manager.py:804-856`), which already surfaces tiers/offsets/limiter and is consumed by `services/status.py`.
- Startup log line: demand vs budget + per-group intervals + explicit advice when over budget.
- Fallback setting: `APISettings.scheduler_mode: Literal["fixed","adaptive"]`. Under B, ship `"fixed"` as the only implemented mode (the setting reserves the seam); under A, default `"adaptive"` with `"fixed"` retained until soaked. **Note: the "frozen CFG3 config seam" was referenced in my brief but its names were not included — the field names above (`scheduler_mode`, per-endpoint `*_interval` fields on `APISettings` following the `ms_port_usage_interval` precedent) are proposals the orchestrator must reconcile with CFG3 before implementation.**

## 7. Cross-cutting constraint (applies to BOTH options — surface to the implementing lanes)

`track_metric_update(tier=self.update_tier)` (`core/collector.py:650`) + tier-keyed TTL (`metric_expiration.py:199-220`, ×2.0 default) means any gate slower than 2× the owning collector's tier interval flaps its series (expire→gap→reappear). Already latent for the existing 900s gates inside MEDIUM DeviceCollector. Fix: allow `_set_metric`/`track_metric_update` to carry an explicit `ttl_seconds` (or effective-interval) override, set by gated fetchers to `gate_interval × multiplier`. This satisfies #541's "no metric goes stale beyond its natural window" acceptance criterion and is a prerequisite seam for either option.

## 1. FROZEN SEAMS

### 1a. New module `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/scheduler.py` (single owner: Lane S)

All types below live in this ONE new file. Wave-0 freezes the signatures; the solver body may iterate inside Lane S only.

```python
"""Adaptive budget-aware endpoint scheduler (#617)."""
from __future__ import annotations
import math, time
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Any, NamedTuple

from .constants import UpdateTier


class EndpointGroupName(StrEnum):
    """Wire names for scheduler groups (label values of LabelName.GROUP)."""
    # exact members listed in the §2 table's "group" column


def pages(n: int, per_page: int) -> int:
    """Pagination helper: max(1, ceil(n / per_page))."""
    return max(1, math.ceil(n / per_page)) if n > 0 else 1


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OrgShape:                      # see 1b for where it is computed
    org_id: str
    network_count: int
    wireless_network_count: int      # network productTypes contains "wireless"
    switch_network_count: int        # … "switch"
    appliance_network_count: int     # … "appliance"
    sensor_network_count: int        # … "sensor"
    camera_network_count: int        # … "camera"
    cellular_network_count: int      # … "cellularGateway"
    device_count: int
    ap_count: int                    # device productType == "wireless"
    switch_count: int                # … "switch"
    appliance_count: int             # … "appliance" (incl. vMX)
    physical_mx_count: int           # appliance devices whose model does NOT start with "VMX"
    camera_count: int                # … "camera"
    sensor_count: int                # … "sensor"
    cellular_count: int              # … "cellularGateway"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class EndpointGroup:
    name: EndpointGroupName
    priority: int                    # 1=up-ness/alerts, 2=sensor, 3=perf/health, 4=config/inventory (issue-fixed order)
    floor_seconds: float             # natural data window; never poll faster
    cost_fn: Callable[[OrgShape], float]   # estimated API calls per ONE execution, incl. pagination
    tier: UpdateTier                 # servicing heartbeat == owning collector's registered tier
    gated: bool = True               # False = demand-accounting only (inventory warm); should_run always True
    setting_pin: str | None = None   # name of a legacy APISettings field that PINS this group when
                                     # explicitly set by the operator (detected via
                                     # settings.api.model_fields_set), e.g. "ms_port_usage_interval"


class SolvedInterval(NamedTuple):
    interval_seconds: float
    stretch_factor: float            # interval / max(floor, tier_heartbeat)
    cost_per_cycle: float
    demand_rps: float                # cost_per_cycle / interval_seconds
    pinned: bool


def solve_intervals(
    groups: Iterable[EndpointGroup],
    shape: OrgShape,
    budget_rps: float,
    target_utilization: float,
    tier_intervals: dict[UpdateTier, int],
    overrides: dict[str, int],       # settings.scheduler.group_interval_overrides + setting_pin values
    max_stretch_factor: float,
    max_interval_seconds: float,
) -> dict[EndpointGroupName, SolvedInterval]:
    """Pure, deterministic solver (unit-test target — no I/O, no clock)."""


class EndpointScheduler:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, rate_limiter: OrgRateLimiter) -> None: ...
    def register_groups(self, groups: Iterable[EndpointGroup]) -> None: ...
    def resolve(self, shape: OrgShape) -> None:            # sync, pure CPU; recompute + emit gauges + log
    def interval_for(self, group: EndpointGroupName) -> float: ...   # pre-resolve: max(floor, tier heartbeat)
    def should_run(self, group: EndpointGroupName, now: float | None = None) -> bool: ...
    def mark_ran(self, group: EndpointGroupName, now: float | None = None) -> None: ...
    def ttl_seconds_for(self, group: EndpointGroupName) -> float: ...  # interval_for(g) × monitoring.metric_ttl_multiplier
    def fastest_effective_interval_seconds(self) -> float: ...
    def needs_resolve(self) -> bool: ...                   # AIMD hysteresis: effective budget moved >aimd_resolve_hysteresis since last resolve
    def diagnostics(self) -> dict[str, Any]: ...           # feeds get_scheduling_diagnostics()/status
```

**The deterministic algorithm (frozen semantics of `solve_intervals`):**

1. `interval[g] = max(g.floor_seconds, tier_intervals[g.tier])` for every enabled group. A group can never run FASTER than its heartbeat — tiers remain heartbeats; the solver only stretches.
2. Apply `overrides`: an overridden/pinned group's interval is set exactly (clamped to ≥ tier heartbeat; a pin below floor is honoured with a WARNING log) and marked `pinned=True` — excluded from stretching.
3. `demand = Σ g.cost_fn(shape) / interval[g]` (all groups incl. `gated=False` overhead groups).
4. While `demand > budget_rps × target_utilization`:
   - candidates = unpinned, gated groups with `interval[g] < cap(g)` where `cap(g) = min(floor_seconds × max_stretch_factor, max_interval_seconds)` (defaults: ×4 and 3600 — the "min(4×floor, 3600)" rule).
   - if no candidates: break and record `over_budget=True` (drives the loud startup warning naming the priority-3/4 collectors to disable — the #218 guidance moment).
   - pick by sort key `(-priority, current_stretch_factor, name)` — i.e. **lowest-priority class first (4 before 3), least-stretched first within a class, name as the deterministic tiebreak** — and set `interval[g] = min(interval[g] × 1.5, cap(g))`; recompute demand.
5. Return the full map. Given identical inputs the output is byte-identical (pure + total ordering).

**Fixed mode** (`scheduler.mode == "fixed"`): steps 1–2 only (floors + pins, no stretch loop), AIMD disabled. Gating still applies — this is how #541/#549/#552 behave identically in both modes; mode only changes who sets values above the floor.

**Gate semantics (frozen):** `should_run(g, now)` returns True when `now - last_ran[g] >= interval_for(g) × 0.9` (10% tolerance so heartbeat jitter/smoothing can't cause systematic skip-a-beat aliasing) OR when `g` has never run (restart ⇒ refetch-everything-once, matching today's startup; readiness unaffected). `mark_ran(g)` is called by the fetch site **after a successful fetch only** (matches the existing `_mark_*` convention, e.g. `ms.py:465,475`; `mv.py:147`; `mx_firewall.py:75`) so failures retry on the next heartbeat. Group-level gates cover a whole per-network/per-device fan-out for that cycle; existing per-serial gates (MS) keep their per-serial maps but read the interval from `scheduler.interval_for(group)` instead of the raw setting.

**AIMD feedback (frozen seam — lives on `OrgRateLimiter`, `core/rate_limiter.py`):**

```python
class OrgRateLimiter:
    def record_throttle_event(self, org_id: str | None, retry_after: float | None) -> None: ...
    def effective_rate_per_second(self) -> float: ...
    def configured_rate_per_second(self) -> float: ...   # rate_limit_requests_per_second × shared_fraction
```

- `record_throttle_event`: multiplicative decrease `effective ×= aimd_backoff_multiplier` (default 0.5), floored at `0.5 rps`, applied **at most once per 30s cooldown window** (so one 429 burst = one halving, not N).
- Recovery: additive `+aimd_recovery_rps_per_minute` (default 0.1) per clean minute, lazily computed on read, capped at configured rate.
- The token bucket refills at `effective_rate_per_second()` (change `rate_per_second` reads at `rate_limiter.py:106,118`) → immediate backpressure, independent of re-solve.
- **Caller:** `core/error_handling.py`, inside the single 429-retry owner — at the `_track_retry(operation, "http_429_rate_limit")` paths (`error_handling.py:336-364` and the `RetryableAPIError` branch at `:250-292`) — resolved via `getattr(instance, "rate_limiter", None)` / `getattr(instance.parent, ...)`, same resolution pattern as `_resolve_retry_after_cap` (`error_handling.py:494-502`). Pass the (already-extracted, capped) `retry_after`.
- The scheduler observes AIMD through `needs_resolve()`: re-solve when `|effective − budget_used_at_last_solve| / budget_used_at_last_solve > aimd_resolve_hysteresis` (default 0.2).

**`collectors/manager.py` (Lane M — single owner):**
- Construct `self.scheduler = EndpointScheduler(settings, self.rate_limiter)` right after the rate limiter (`manager.py:83`); pass `scheduler=self.scheduler` into every collector constructor (`manager.py:281-288`); after `_initialize_collectors`, call `self.scheduler.register_groups(g for c in all collectors for g in c.get_endpoint_groups())`.
- `collect_initial` (`manager.py:471-496`): after `warm_cache()` succeeds, `shape = await self.inventory.get_org_shape(settings.meraki.org_id)`; `self.scheduler.resolve(shape)`; then emit the **startup demand-vs-budget log line** (INFO, one line): `"Scheduler solved: org shape W=… D=…; estimated demand X.X rps; budget Y.Y rps (shared_fraction Z); target utilization U; stretched: <group> <interval>s (<n>x)…"` — plus a WARNING when `over_budget=True` naming the priority-3/4 collectors to disable (`MERAKI_EXPORTER_COLLECTORS__DISABLE_COLLECTORS=…`). - **Tier loops unchanged as heartbeats.** `collect_tier` (`manager.py:534`) keeps running every collector each cycle; gating happens inside `_collect_impl` at fetch sites. A fully-gated collector run is a cheap no-op that still records success — deliberate (see liveness).
- `get_scheduling_diagnostics` (`manager.py:814-866`): add a `"scheduler"` key = `self.scheduler.diagnostics()`: `{mode, org_shape, budget_rps, effective_budget_rps, target_utilization, over_budget, total_demand_rps, last_resolve_ts, groups: [{name, priority, tier, floor_seconds, interval_seconds, stretch_factor, pinned, cost_per_cycle, demand_rps, last_ran_ago_seconds}]}`. This flows to the index page (`app.py:860,875`) and `/status` automatically once StatusService/templates render it.
- Retire the `"endpoint_intervals"` diagnostics block (`manager.py:860-865`) into the scheduler section (same data, now per-group).

**`app.py` (Lane A — single owner):**
- Lifespan: in `_startup_collections` (`app.py:492`), after tier loops start, create a tracked `_scheduler_resolve_loop()` background task (same bookkeeping pattern as `app.py:531-536`): every 60s check `scheduler.needs_resolve()` (AIMD hysteresis ⇒ early re-solve); every `settings.scheduler.resolve_interval_seconds` (default 900) recompute `shape = await inventory.get_org_shape(org_id)` (cached reads; the TTL expiry makes this the "on-inventory-refresh" hook) and `scheduler.resolve(shape)`. Swallow-and-log exceptions; honour `_shutdown_event` with the 1s-increment wait pattern (`app.py:633-636`).
- **#596 liveness contract PRESERVED, no code change needed:** because groups never run faster than their heartbeat and gated collectors still complete successful heartbeat runs, collector success cadence remains the tier interval — so `_fastest_enabled_tier_interval_seconds` (`app.py:248-266`) and the 3× threshold (`app.py:268-281`) stay correct as-is. Lane A's only action: update that helper's docstring (it explicitly anticipated #617 swapping in "fastest computed group cadence" — record that under the gate model the tier derivation IS the computed fastest cadence) and add a regression test asserting the threshold is unchanged in adaptive mode. `EndpointScheduler.fastest_effective_interval_seconds()` exists for diagnostics, not for the threshold.
- Readiness (`/ready`, `app.py:899-913`) untouched.
- `/status`: `services/status.py` `StatusService.get_snapshot` (`status.py:352`) + `templates/status.html` gain a "Scheduler" section rendering the diagnostics dict as **org shape → per-group demand → budget (configured + effective) → chosen intervals/stretch**; `templates/index.html` gets the one-line summary (demand/budget/utilization). Templates are self-contained files (see `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/CLAUDE.md`) — edit each directly.

**`core/error_handling.py` + `core/rate_limiter.py` (Lane R):** AIMD per §1a — hook at the 429 paths (`error_handling.py:250-292, 336-364`), state on `OrgRateLimiter`, counter `SCHEDULER_THROTTLE_BACKOFFS_TOTAL`. In `fixed` mode or `aimd_enabled=False`, `record_throttle_event` is a no-op and `effective == configured`.

**Docs (final wave):** `make docgen`; `docs/scaling-guide.md` gets the sizing formula + solver explanation (#542 alignment); freshness doc (#567) documents per-group intervals as the freshness source of truth; MET-09-style HELP text on the new gauges.

---

## 4. WAVE PLAN (one file = one owner; transient red OK until each checkpoint)

**Wave 0 — seam freeze (sequential, before any fan-out):**
| lane | files (sole owner) | delivers |
|---|---|---|
| S | NEW `core/scheduler.py` + `tests/test_scheduler.py` | all §1a types, `EndpointGroupName` enum (every §2 name), pure solver + gate/AIMD-read logic, unit tests vs SMALL (1 org/10 nets/100 dev) and LARGE (500/5000, evidence header) shapes; determinism test; over-budget warning test |
| ORCH | `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`, `core/metrics.py` | §1e enum members + `LabelName.GROUP` (orchestrator funnels — these are the wave-method seam files) |
| CFG | `core/config_models.py`, `core/config.py` | `SchedulerSettings` + mount + `model_fields_set` pin detection + tests |
| C | `core/collector.py`, `core/metric_expiration.py` | §1c registration/injection/gate helpers + §1f `ttl_seconds` override + tests (incl. flap-regression: 900s-gated series with MEDIUM tier survives cleanup) |

**Wave 1 — infrastructure (parallel, disjoint):**
| lane | files | delivers |
|---|---|---|
| R | `core/rate_limiter.py`, `core/error_handling.py` | AIMD (§1a) + 429-feedback simulation tests |
| INV | `services/inventory.py` | `get_org_shape` (§1b) + tests (filtered networks, VMX exclusion) |
| M | `collectors/manager.py` | scheduler construction/injection/registration, resolve-in-collect_initial, startup log line, diagnostics section |
| A | `app.py`, `services/status.py`, `templates/status.html`, `templates/index.html` | resolve loop, /status + index sections, #596 docstring+regression test |

**Wave 2 — fetch-site gating + group declarations (parallel; each lane declares its coordinator's `endpoint_groups`, adds gates, threads `ttl_seconds`, updates that lane's tests):**
| lane | files | notes |
|---|---|---|
| NH | `collectors/network_health.py`, `network_health_collectors/**` | **includes prerequisite #271 org-wide channel-util rewrite (byBand/6GHz ⚠ Phase-6) + rf_health inventory fix + #541 floors**; biggest lane |
| DEV | `collectors/device.py`, `collectors/devices/base.py` | coordinator seam — group declarations for ALL device groups + `device_availability`/`device_memory` gates (device.py is a registry-like seam: exactly one owner) |
| MR | `collectors/devices/mr/**` | conn-stats 1800s gate (#331 fold), CPU/ethernet/packet-loss/ssid gates |
| MS | `collectors/devices/ms.py`, `ms_stack.py`, `ms_power.py` | existing per-serial gates read `_group_interval`; port-overview 3600 gate |
| MX | `collectors/devices/mx.py`, `mx_*.py` | #552 `mx_performance` 900s gate; vpn/ha/security/firewall groups |
| MV | `collectors/devices/mv.py` | #549: endpoint migration (⚠ Phase-6 replacement names) + 900s group + org-keying fix |
| MISC | `collectors/mt_sensor.py`, `devices/mt.py`, `devices/mg.py`, `mt_alerts.py` | MT/MG groups |
| ORG | `collectors/organization.py`, `organization_collectors/**` | 9 org groups |
| AC | `collectors/alerts.py`, `collectors/config.py`, `collectors/clients.py` | alerts/config/clients groups; clients groups behind `get_endpoint_groups()` override |

**Wave 3 — integration checkpoint (orchestrator):** full `make check` green (evidence, not assertion); e2e assertion that at a mocked LARGE shape the solver stretches priority-4-then-3 and total demand ≤ budget×target; `make docgen`; scaling-guide/freshness updates; commit(s) with `Closes #617` (+ `Closes #541, #549, #552` as folded floors, per their ACs being satisfied by the solver lanes).

**Phase-6 LIVE VERIFICATION list (blockers for freezing ⚠ values; homelab key in gitignored `.env`):** #271 org-wide channel-util response (`byBand` array field names, 6GHz presence, perPage max 1000); #331 conn-stats field diff (`getNetworkWirelessDevicesConnectionStats` vs `getNetworkWirelessConnectionStats`); #541 endpoint windows (conn-stats 1800, failed/latency/air-marshal 3600, port-overview 43200); #549 MV replacement endpoint names/shapes; perPage maxima marked ⚠ in §2 (coordinate with #548's constants).

**Risk register for the orchestrator:** (1) the `_metric_timestamps` value-shape change (§1f) touches every expiration test — Lane C runs `tests/test_metric_expiration*` scoped before wave 1 starts; (2) `EndpointGroupName` is append-only once wave 2 starts (lanes depend on it — any addition goes through the orchestrator); (3) working tree already has uncommitted changes in `api/client.py`, `config.py`, `mt_sensor.py`, `network_health.py`, `error_handling.py`, `config_models.py`, `metrics_constants.py`, `async_utils.py` + 4 test files — reconcile/commit those BEFORE wave 0 so lanes branch from a clean seam; (4) `/status` JSON is consumed by `?format=json` users — additive keys only.

**Review of the reopening (2026-07-03, Fable session)** — verdict and routing.

Ran a full read-only audit of the landed implementation (waves `3e20f34`/`3071792`/`2cb500d` + Phase-4 follow-ups) against the build spec above. Verdict: **structurally spec-conformant** — solver, AIMD, OrgShape, ~80 gated groups, per-series TTLs, /status surface all match the frozen seams; `make check` green. What Rob observed in the homelab (three tier pollers still running) is the build spec's §1a *working as designed* — the spec froze 'tiers remain heartbeats', and that design decision is what's now overturned, not an implementation shortfall.

**I agree with doing the full de-tiering now, pre-v1:** the heartbeat model quantizes groups up to their tier interval (device up-ness runs at 300s despite its 120s floor — the epic's own criterion unmet), leaves two scheduling vocabularies on the operator surface, and v1 is the only breaking-change moment for the config surface, the `tier` self-metric label, and the Helm alert rules. The solver/cost-model/AIMD investment is untouched — only dispatch, config, and observability layers change.

The audit also surfaced real gaps beyond the tier question: gate-advance on totally-failed fan-outs (worst at 1800/3600s floors and on up-ness), `MS_PORT_OVERVIEW` series bypassing TTL tracking, and the fact that **every ⚠ Phase-6 value shipped assumed, never live-verified** (incl. 6GHz rows silently dropped in the #271 rewrite) while the #271/#331/#549 closing comments pointed at a #619 checklist entry that didn't exist.

Everything is now tracked: **#629** (gate-semantics gaps, do first) → **#631** (de-tiering, full frozen spec + 45-point removal inventory embedded) · **#630** (live verification, independent, now referenced from #619's release gate). The issue description above has been rewritten as the epic summary with a launch prompt; the original body is in the edit history.

## Epic complete — closing.

The adaptive scheduler shipped in three waves and is now the sole scheduling model; FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW is gone as a construct.

- **Solver + budget-aware stretching + AIMD** landed earlier (`3e20f34` / `3071792` / `2cb500d`) — every fetch declared as an `EndpointGroup`, solved against `budget_rps × target_utilization`, floored at its volatility floor.
- **#629** (`55dd4e5`): canonical `mark_ran` semantics — a group is marked ran iff the cycle achieved ≥1 successful fetch; total failure leaves the gate open for a bounded retry. Prerequisite for the attempt layer below.
- **#631** (`cc76452`): the heartbeat compromise removed. Per-collector group-clocked loops (`wake_at = min next_due(g)`), so each group runs at exactly its solved interval — `device_availability` now hits its 120s floor instead of being quantized to 300s. `EndpointScheduler` gained attempt-tracking so a persistently-failing group retries after `failure_retry_seconds` rather than hot-looping. UpdateTier deleted end to end: registry, config (`UpdateIntervals` + per-tier concurrency knobs), TTL fallback, readiness (priority-≤3), liveness (3× fastest solved interval), the `tier` self-metric label + OTel `collector.tier`, `/status` + index UI, Helm values + the staleness alert rule, and the full docs/CLAUDE sweep (incl. the new `docs/observability/scheduler.md` architecture page). Also folded in the v1-sink log findings #632/#633/#634/#635.

Every #617 success criterion is now met (per-group cadence, single scheduling vocabulary, no vestigial tier surface). `make check` green, `make docgen` regenerated, `helm template` renders.

**Remaining, tracked separately and intentionally left open:** #630 — live-verify the frozen assumptions (volatility floors, #271 byBand/6GHz, #549 MV fields, #331 conn-stats dedup, perPage maxima) against a real org. Independent of the dispatch rework; not a blocker for this epic. Dashboards rebuild is Phase 7 (frozen for now).

### Goal / data unlocked
Webhooks today only **count** events; they do not flip state metrics like `meraki_device_up`, so device-down detection is gated on the MEDIUM (300s) poll tier plus Meraki-side lag (~10+ min worst case). Wiring webhook events into faster state transitions would give near-real-time down/up signals. Deferred: significant design (event→state reconciliation, reconvergence with polled truth, the dead `WebhookMetricsCollector`).

### Meraki API
Inbound `POST /api/webhooks/meraki` payloads (no outbound API); reconcile against polled device status.

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/webhook_handler.py`
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/webhook_metrics.py` (currently dead code — wire deliberately or replace)
- device state metric ownership in `collectors/device.py`

### Notes / risks
Source: GAP-22 (deferred). Note the README currently over-claims webhooks as 'real-time' (fixed under the M15 freshness-doc issue, GAP-03). `WebhookMetricsCollector` is dead code today (SEC/MET-12) and its `network_id` label would be a cardinality risk if wired naively — bound labels. Reconciliation with the poll loop is the hard part.

comments.body:
**Execution routing (for #618 orchestration):** agent model: `fable` · thinking effort: `high`.

This is a `fable-candidate` issue: the orchestrator spawns a dedicated **Fable, high-effort subagent** whose FIRST deliverable is the design/spec posted ON THIS ISSUE; mechanical implementation may then be delegated to a cheaper agent per that spec (the spec comment states the implementer routing). The orchestrator itself implements nothing.

## 🧭 FROZEN DESIGN SPEC — #614 (Wave 4E, 2026-07-03)

Produced by the fable/high design-freeze pass. **Key scope decision: webhooks accelerate DOWN transitions only in v1** — `KNOWN_ALERT_TYPES` has no whole-device *recovery* event, so UP recovery stays poll-paced (reconciliation-only; the `up=True` code path is built + tested but the up-alert set is empty pending a Phase-6 live capture of the real recovery `alertType`). The webhook is a fast-path hint; the MEDIUM poll remains sole source of truth and reconverges every cycle.

# FROZEN SPEC — #614: Webhook events → fast `meraki_device_up` down transitions

**Scope decision (binding):** webhooks accelerate **DOWN** transitions only in v1. The webhook is a fast-path *hint*; the MEDIUM poll (`DeviceCollector._process_org_devices` → `device_availability` group, #617) remains the sole source of truth and re-asserts every series each cycle. The stale premise in this issue's body — wiring the dead `WebhookMetricsCollector` — is void: that file was removed in #530; this design targets the live `core/webhook_handler.py::WebhookHandler`.

---

## 1. Serial→labels mechanism (the crux)

`meraki_device_up` is labelled exactly `(org_id, network_id, serial, model, device_type)` (`collectors/device.py:585`). `WebhookPayload` carries no `model`/`device_type`, so the handler cannot construct that tuple itself — a guessed tuple would mint a duplicate wrong-labelled series. **Adopted:** DeviceCollector owns a serial→labels map and exposes one applier method; the webhook can only write series the poll already owns.

**The map.** New instance attribute on `DeviceCollector.__init__`:

```python
# serial -> exact meraki_device_up label dict (create_device_labels output).
# Replaced atomically per-org each poll; read by apply_webhook_device_state.
self._webhook_device_labels: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
```

**Population/pruning.** In `_process_org_devices` (device.py ~line 855 loop), while iterating `devices`, build a local `org_serial_labels: dict[str, dict[str, str]]` with `org_serial_labels[serial] = create_device_labels(device, org_id=org_id, org_name=org_name)` — the *same call* that produces the poll's `_device_up` labels (`_collect_common_metrics` line 1522), so tuples are byte-identical by construction. Populate for every supported device row every cycle (NOT gated on `availability_due` — labels are known whenever devices are fetched, which is every MEDIUM cycle). Skip rows whose `device_type_str` is unsupported (the poll never emits `_device_up` for those; the map must not either). After the loop, prune+merge in one atomic rebind:

```python
self._webhook_device_labels = {
    s: lbl for s, lbl in self._webhook_device_labels.items()
    if lbl[LabelName.ORG_ID.value] != org_id
} | org_serial_labels
```

Removed/renetworked devices thus fall out of (or are updated in) the map on the next poll; a failed org poll leaves the previous org entries intact (stale-but-owned labels; the poll still owns those series until TTL expiry).

**The applier.** One public method on `DeviceCollector`:

```python
def apply_webhook_device_state(self, serial: str, up: bool) -> bool:
    """Fast-path flip of meraki_device_up from a webhook event (#614).

    Returns True if the serial is poll-known and the flip was applied;
    False (no-op) for unknown serials.
    """
    labels = self._webhook_device_labels.get(serial)
    if labels is None:
        return False
    self._set_metric(
        self._device_up,
        labels,
        1.0 if up else 0.0,
        DeviceMetricName.DEVICE_UP.value,
        ttl_seconds=self._group_ttl_seconds(EndpointGroupName.DEVICE_AVAILABILITY),
    )
    return True
```

Going through `self._set_metric` **on DeviceCollector** is load-bearing twice over: (a) the expiration tracking key is `(collector_name, metric_name, frozen_labels)` (`metric_expiration.py:166`) with `collector_name=self.__class__.__name__` (`collector.py:825`) — calling from DeviceCollector yields `"DeviceCollector"`, the identical key the poll writes, so the webhook write *refreshes* the existing tracked series instead of creating a parallel tracking entry; (b) forwarding the same `_group_ttl_seconds(DEVICE_AVAILABILITY)` TTL the poll uses (#617 §1f) means the flipped series expires/refreshes identically to a poll-written one.

**Thread-safety.** No lock. The webhook route is `async def` (app.py:1212) and `process_webhook` is synchronous, so the flip executes on the event loop thread; `_collect_common_metrics`/the map rebind also run as synchronous code on the event loop thread (SDK calls go through `asyncio.to_thread`, but metric writes and the map rebuild do not). Cooperative scheduling serializes them — a sync block never interleaves with another sync block. The map is additionally maintained with single-assignment rebinding (never in-place mutation visible mid-build), so even a future move of `process_webhook` off-loop degrades safely under the GIL (a reader sees the old or new dict, both valid), and `prometheus_client` `Gauge.labels().set()` is itself thread-safe. Document this reasoning in the applier docstring.

**Alternatives rejected:**
- *Separate `meraki_device_up_webhook` series* — doubles cardinality, pushes reconciliation onto every dashboard/alert query (`min()` joins), and breaks the "poll naturally overwrites" property. Rejected.
- *Shared `DeviceStateStore` service* — a third owner for state two components already share cleanly via one method; more seams, no benefit at this scale. Rejected.
- *Webhook handler queries inventory/API for labels* — adds API calls on an unauthenticated-capable request path and races the poll. Rejected.

## 2. Wiring

**Protocol (consumer-side, zero imports).** Define in `core/webhook_handler.py`:

```python
class DeviceStateApplier(Protocol):
    """Narrow seam for webhook-driven device state flips (#614)."""
    def apply_webhook_device_state(self, serial: str, up: bool) -> bool: ...
```

`DeviceCollector` satisfies it structurally — `webhook_handler.py` never imports `collectors/`. (Not `type_definitions.py`: that file holds TypedDicts/aliases; the sole consumer defines its own protocol, matching `CollectorProtocol`-in-`collector.py` precedent.)

**Constructor.** `WebhookHandler.__init__(self, settings: Settings, device_state_applier: DeviceStateApplier | None = None)`; store as `self._device_state_applier`. `None` (default) = feature off; all existing call sites/tests remain valid.

**app.py.** `CollectorManager` (constructed line 202, collectors instantiated in its `__init__`) already exists when the handler is built (line 227). Add a tiny lookup — either a `CollectorManager.get_collector_by_class_name(name: str) -> MetricCollector | None` helper scanning `self.collectors.values()`, or an inline isinstance scan in `ExporterApp.__init__` (implementer's choice; prefer the manager helper for testability):

```python
device_collector = self.collector_manager.get_collector_by_class_name("DeviceCollector")
self.webhook_handler = WebhookHandler(self.settings, device_state_applier=device_collector)
```

If the `device` collector is disabled via `active_collectors`, the applier is `None` and webhooks degrade to today's count-only behaviour (debug log once per event).

**Alert-type → direction mapping.** Module-level frozensets in `webhook_handler.py`, keyed on the **bound** alert type (all members are in `KNOWN_ALERT_TYPES`, so bounding preserves them):

```python
DEVICE_DOWN_ALERT_TYPES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"device_down", "gateway_down"})
DEVICE_UP_ALERT_TYPES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()  # empty in v1 — see below
```

- `device_down` — Meraki's whole-device offline alert (APs/switches/appliances went down). Included: this is the feature.
- `gateway_down` — a gateway device going offline (whole-device for that unit). Included.
- **Excluded with reasons:** `cellular_up`/`cellular_down` (cellular *uplink* state on MG/MX, not device state), `port_down`/`port_error`/`port_link_change` (per-port), `power_supply` (PSU component), `uplink_status_change` (uplink path, device still up), `gateway_to_repeater`/`repeater_to_gateway` (wired-uplink role change; the AP is still online), `vpn_connectivity_change` (tunnel), `dhcp_no_leases`, `rogue_*`, sensor/usage/auth types (not device availability).
- **Up-set is empty — reconciliation-only recovery.** `KNOWN_ALERT_TYPES` contains no whole-device recovery type ("came up"-style alerts are not in the curated allowlist, and their exact `alertType` strings are unverified against live payloads). v1 behaviour: **webhook marks DOWN fast; UP is restored by the next poll** (bounded staleness ≤ one MEDIUM cycle + Meraki lag — exactly today's freshness, so recovery is never *worse* than status quo). The mapping structure supports an up-set the moment verified recovery types exist (⚠ see §7). The applier's `up: bool` parameter ships now so no seam change is needed later.

**Call site in `process_webhook`.** After secret validation and label bounding, alongside the existing counter increments (i.e., after `events_received.inc()`, before `return payload` — concretely between the `logger.info("Webhook event received", ...)` and `events_processed.inc()` blocks):

```python
if (
    self._device_state_applier is not None
    and payload.device_serial
    and alert_type in DEVICE_DOWN_ALERT_TYPES  # bound_alert_type output
):
    applied = self._device_state_applier.apply_webhook_device_state(
        payload.device_serial, up=False
    )
    self.device_state_transitions.labels(
        direction="down",
        result="applied" if applied else "unknown_serial",
    ).inc()
```

Wrap in its own try/except (log + count `result="error"`? No — keep it simple: let the existing outer `except Exception` in `process_webhook` catch pathological failures; `apply_webhook_device_state` already swallows metric-write errors via `_set_metric`'s internal try/except, so the only realistic exceptions are programming errors).

## 3. Reconvergence + edge cases (the guarantee)

**Invariant:** the webhook can only write a series whose exact label tuple the poll computed and owns, via the same `_set_metric` path, same collector identity, same TTL. Therefore it can only **accelerate** a transition the poll would make; it can never create a novel/relabelled series, never changes tracking cardinality, and can never win a permanent disagreement — every MEDIUM cycle with `availability_due` re-asserts polled truth over any webhook write.

- **Stale/wrong webhook** (device already recovered, or spurious down): `device_up=0` for at most one availability-group interval; next poll rewrites `1`.
- **Unknown / never-polled serial** (including attacker-supplied on the insecure path): not in the map → `False` → no metric touched; the event is still counted by the existing `events_received/processed` counters plus `result="unknown_serial"` on the new transition counter.
- **Device expired out of `device_up` but still in the map** (possible in the gap before the map's owning-org next poll): the flip re-creates the series with poll-derived labels and availability TTL — a poll-known device, so not a leak; next poll or TTL reconverges it.
- **Two webhooks in quick succession:** both run synchronously on the event loop → strictly serialized; last write wins; poll re-asserts.
- **Webhook mid-poll:** event-loop interleaving can only occur at `await` points; the map read is a single atomic dict lookup against either the pre- or post-rebind dict (both valid). Worst case ordering (poll writes `1`, webhook writes `0`, or vice versa) self-heals at the next `availability_due` cycle.
- **`device_status_info` is deliberately NOT touched** by the webhook (its `status` label needs the stale-series removal dance, device.py:1541–1566). Accepted transient inconsistency: `device_up=0` while `status_info{status="online"}=1` until the next poll. Document in the applier docstring and metric HELP is unchanged.

## 4. Cardinality / security

- **No new labels on `meraki_device_up`**; no series the poll doesn't already own. `device_serial` is attacker-influenced when `require_secret=false` (SEC-03) — the unknown-serial no-op is the guard: only poll-known serials are flippable, and even those only to values the poll would set. The flip also sits **after** `validate_secret`, so on the secure (default-enforced) path it is authenticated anyway.
- **One new self-obs counter (warranted** — operators need to see whether fast-path flips are actually landing vs. bucketing to unknown_serial): `meraki_webhook_device_state_transitions_total{direction, result}` — `direction ∈ {down, up}`, `result ∈ {applied, unknown_serial}`; ≤4 series, fixed by construction, no payload-derived values. New enum member `WEBHOOK_DEVICE_<net-name-4>TE_TRANSITIONS_TOTAL = "meraki_webhook_device_state_transitions_total"` in `WebhookMetricName` (webhook family, owned by `WebhookHandler._initialize_metrics` like its siblings — NOT `CollectorMetricName`, whose `meraki_exporter_*` prefix is for exporter-internals; this counter describes webhook product events). `direction`/`result`: reuse existing `LabelName` members if `DIRECTION`/`RESULT`-equivalents exist; otherwise add them — **LabelName + metrics_constants edits are funnelled-seam changes the orchestrator pre-adds before the lane starts.**

## 5. File/ownership plan — ONE lane

| File | Change | Seam status |
|---|---|---|
| `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` | +1 `WebhookMetricName` member | **Funnelled seam — orchestrator pre-adds** |
| `core/metrics.py` | `LabelName.DIRECTION` / `RESULT` if absent | **Funnelled seam — orchestrator pre-adds** |
| `core/webhook_handler.py` | `DeviceStateApplier` Protocol, `DEVICE_DOWN/UP_ALERT_TYPES`, constructor kwarg, new counter in `_initialize_metrics`, flip call in `process_webhook` | Lane-owned |
| `collectors/device.py` | `_webhook_device_labels` map (init + populate/prune in `_process_org_devices`), `apply_webhook_device_state` | Lane-owned (coordinator file — single owner, no parallel edits) |
| `collectors/manager.py` | `get_collector_by_class_name` helper | Funnelled coordinator file — same single lane owns it this wave |
| `app.py` | pass applier into `WebhookHandler(...)` | Lane-owned |
| tests (below) | new/extended | Lane-owned |

Post-implementation: `make check` green + `make docgen` (new metric → docs). No dashboard edits (frozen). Commit closes `#614`.

## 6. Test strategy (strict TDD; patterns per `tests/CLAUDE.md`, extend `tests/test_webhook_handler.py` + `tests/unit/test_device_collector.py`)

Failing-first, in order:

1. **Fast down-flip:** seed DeviceCollector via a normal mocked poll (device factory → `_collect_impl`), assert `meraki_device_up{...}=1`; feed a `device_down` webhook payload for that serial through `WebhookHandler.process_webhook` (handler constructed with the collector as applier); assert the exact same-labelled series now `0` — *before* any second poll.
2. **Poll re-asserts truth:** after the flip, run the poll again with the device online → series back to `1`. Also the wrong-webhook case: webhook `down` for an online device, next poll corrects to `1`.
3. **No duplicate series:** capture the full sample set of the `meraki_device_up` family before and after the webhook flip; assert the series *count* is unchanged and the flipped sample's label dict equals the poll-written one exactly.
4. **Unknown serial no-op:** webhook for a never-polled serial → `device_up` family unchanged, `apply_webhook_device_state` returns `False`, `events_received/processed` still incremented, transition counter `result="unknown_serial"` incremented.
5. **Non-device alert types don't flip:** `port_down`, `cellular_down`, `uplink_status_change` payloads with a poll-known serial → no `device_up` write.
6. **No applier configured:** handler with `device_state_applier=None` processes a `device_down` payload exactly as today (regression guard for disabled `device` collector).
7. **Expiration-tracking identity:** after a webhook flip, assert the expiration manager holds ONE tracking entry for that (collector, metric, labels) key (webhook refresh, not a second entry), and that its TTL matches the availability-group TTL.
8. **Pruning:** poll cycle without a previously-seen serial (device removed) → subsequent webhook for it is a no-op.
9. **Concurrency smoke:** interleave `apply_webhook_device_state` calls with a poll cycle on the event loop (e.g., fire the flip from a task scheduled between poll awaits) → no exception, final state = last writer, series count stable.

No live API; all deterministic via the existing mock-API/factory helpers.

## 7. ⚠ #619 Phase-6 flags

- **⚠ Live webhook end-to-end smoke:** configure a real Meraki webhook receiver against the homelab org, take a test device offline, verify `meraki_device_up` drops via webhook ahead of the poll, and **capture the real recovery payload** — confirm the actual `alertType` strings for down AND recovery ("came up"-style) events. If a verified whole-device recovery type exists, add it to `KNOWN_ALERT_TYPES` + `DEVICE_UP_ALERT_TYPES` (one-line follow-up; the `up=True` path is already built and tested).
- **⚠ Docs:** `docs/` freshness/webhook page must state the asymmetry — webhooks accelerate *down* detection only; *up* recovery remains poll-paced (MEDIUM) — replacing any residual "real-time" phrasing (GAP-03 follow-through).

**Area:** `org` · **Type:** `new-metric` · **Priority:** `P2` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** M6 — Config & security-drift metrics

### Goal / data unlocked
Today only org-level firmware **upgrade event counts** are exported (`getOrganizationFirmwareUpgrades`). The device inventory already carries a `firmware` field that goes unused, and there is no per-device firmware **version** signal nor any 'is this network/device up to date' compliance gauge. Unlocks firmware-drift dashboards and alerting.

Proposed metrics (verify exact shape against the installed SDK + spec before implementing):
- `meraki_device_firmware_info{org_id, org_name, network_id, network_name, serial, name, model, firmware}` — value `1`, info-join carrying the running firmware version as the `firmware` label (bounded by device count; join to numeric series on `serial`).
- `meraki_network_firmware_up_to_date{org_id, org_name, network_id, network_name}` — `1` when all devices in the network are on the latest stable firmware, else `0` (derive from `getOrganizationFirmwareUpgradesByDevice` upgrade status).

### Meraki API
`getOrganizationDevices` (inventory `firmware` field, already fetched via inventory) + `getOrganizationFirmwareUpgradesByDevice(organizationId)` for up-to-date status. **Verified present** on the installed SDK (`organizations.getOrganizationFirmwareUpgradesByDevice`).

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/organization.py` (or an org sub-collector under `organization_collectors/`)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (new enum members)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/metrics.py` (any new `LabelName` — `firmware`)
- Pydantic domain model for the response

### Notes / risks
Source: GAP-12. Devices come via `OrganizationInventory` (NetworkFilter enforced) — do not call `getOrganizationDevices` directly. SLOW tier (firmware changes rarely). Cardinality: `meraki_device_firmware_info` is bounded by device count with a bounded `firmware` label; the network gauge is bounded by network count. No PII. Confirm the exact `upgradeStatus`/version fields on the live endpoint before wiring the up-to-date logic.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Metric name(s) declared via the appropriate domain enum in `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (no hardcoded strings) and label names via `LabelName` (`core/metrics.py`).

- [ ] Emitted via `parent._set_metric()` so values participate in metric expiration.
- [ ] Update tier chosen and justified by data volatility; org-wide/bulk endpoint preferred over per-device/per-network loops where one exists.
- [ ] Cardinality reviewed: only bounded label sets (no client MAC / raw SSID/BSSID / per-request rows / attacker-influenced values).
- [ ] Tests added (factory + mock API + metric-value assertions) and `make check` is green.
- [ ] `make docgen` run so the new metric(s) land in generated docs.
- [ ] `meraki_device_firmware_info` emits one series per device with the running firmware version as a label.
- [ ] `meraki_network_firmware_up_to_date` correctly reflects per-network compliance derived from the upgrades-by-device endpoint.

**Area:** `org` · **Type:** `feature` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** M7 — Usability / DX / platform

### Problem / impact
**Decided by Rob 2026-07-02: for v1 one poller instance serves exactly one organization, as a BREAKING change.** Today `org_id` is all-or-exactly-one (`config_models.py:447`) but the surrounding machinery still loops per-org and there is no explicit contract, so an API key that can see several orgs behaves ambiguously and the rate-limit budget can't be reasoned about per instance.

Scope for this issue:
- When the API key sees **exactly one** organization, auto-select it (no `org_id` required).
- When the key sees **several** orgs, **fail fast at startup** with a clear message listing the visible orgs and pointing the operator at the sharding/HA doc and the Helm multi-instance example (one instance per org).
- Document the single-org contract as a **breaking change** in the upgrade/migration notes.
- Internal multi-org loops/machinery are stripped **opportunistically post-v1**, NOT in this issue — this issue only establishes and enforces the contract.

### Meraki API
`getOrganizations` (list orgs the key can see, for both auto-select and the fail-fast org list).

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/config_models.py` (org_id validation / single-org contract)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/discovery.py` and app startup (auto-select + fail-fast with visible-org list)
- docs: upgrade/migration note (breaking) + cross-link to the sharding/HA doc

### Notes / risks
Source: GAP-02. Interactions: simplifies the rate-limit budget (1 instance = 1 org budget, so per-instance sizing is now well-defined); pairs with the **M15 sharding / HA guide** issue (shard-by-org recipes + Helm multi-instance example the fail-fast message must point at); existing user issue **#218** (large-env rate-limit complaint) benefits from the clarified single-org envelope. The error message MUST reference the sharding doc + Helm multi-instance example so a multi-org operator has an immediate path forward.

### Acceptance criteria

**Area:** `dashboards` · **Type:** `qol` · **Priority:** `P3` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** M16 — Dashboard rebuild

### Problem / impact
The MX / MG / MV dashboards each reference only the same 6 generic device metrics (`meraki_device_up`, `meraki_device_status_info`, `meraki_device_memory_{free,total,used}_bytes`, `meraki_device_memory_usage_percent`) and nothing device-type-specific, so ~59 collected `meraki_*` metric families appear on no dashboard at all.

Evidence (validated 2026-07-01): grepping all `meraki_*` tokens in `dashboards/mx-security-appliances.json`, `mg-cellular-gateways.json`, `mv-security-cameras.json` shows exactly those 6 generic metrics in each. The claimed-missing families are real, currently-declared enum members in `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`: `MS_<net-name-4>CK_MEMBER_<net-name-4>TUS` (:150), `MX_UPLINK_LOSS_PERCENT` (:225), `MX_VPN_PEER_<net-name-4>TUS` (:229), `MG_UPLINK_SIGNAL_RSRP_DBM` (:263), `MV_PEOPLE_COUNT` (:272), `MT_GATEWAY_RSSI` (:313), and more — shipped/collected metrics genuinely absent from their dashboards. This is a dashboards-completeness gap, not a code defect.

### Meraki API
N/A — Grafana dashboard JSON, no Meraki API change.

### Files to touch
- `dashboards/mx-security-appliances.json` — add MX uplink-loss/latency, VPN peer status panels.
- `dashboards/mg-cellular-gateways.json` — add MG RSRP/signal panels.
- `dashboards/mv-security-cameras.json` — add MV people-count etc.
- `dashboards/ms-switches*.json` — add MS stack-member status.
- `dashboards/mt-sensors*.json` — add MT gateway-RSSI etc.

Fix direction: build device-type-specific panels from the exporter's own metric metadata; enumerate all device-family families in `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` and give each a home.

### Notes / risks
Validated CONFIRMED (high confidence) — spot-checked rather than trusting the '59 families' aggregate; the specific claims hold. Effort **L**: this is a genuine content build across several dashboards, best done as part of the rebuild by generating panels from the exporter's metric metadata rather than hand-typing series names. Verify every family's label set against `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` / `LabelName` / a live scrape.

**Units nuance (F-115):** `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes` is a bytes-per-**second** rate over the poll window, NOT a cumulative byte counter — any MS-port bandwidth panel must format it as Bps and must never wrap it in `rate()`/`increase()` or render it as a total.

**Dashboards are frozen until the dedicated rebuild task (see `dashboards/CLAUDE.md`); do NOT fix this from a code-change session** — no `dashboards/*.json` edits belong in exporter code work (golden rule #514). This issue is an input to that rebuild task only.

**Post-sweep names:** the M13 metric-naming sweep will rename many series (drop `_total` from gauges, fix `_kb`/`_mb`/`_kbps`/`_ms`/`_percent` unit + suffix conventions), so the rebuild must author panels against the **post-sweep** metric names, not the names quoted here.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MX/MG/MV (and MS/MT) dashboards surface their device-type-specific metric families, not just the 6 generic device metrics
- [ ] Every added panel's series name + label set verified against the collector source / live scrape (post-M13-sweep names)
- [ ] Any `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes` panel is formatted as Bps, never rated
- [ ] No collected device-family metric is left with zero dashboard coverage

### Problem / impact
A licensing panel filters on `status="grace_period"`, a value no license state ever takes, so the query is permanently dead.

Evidence (validated 2026-07-01): `api-usage-licensing.json:778` has query C `sum by (org_name, license_type) (meraki_org_licenses_total{org_id=~"$organization", status="grace_period"})`, and `:375-379` has a `byName`/`grace_period` field-override matcher. In `license.py` the per-device path sets `status = lic.get("state", "Unknown")` (~:169) and the co-term path sets `status = overview.get("status", "Unknown")` (~:279), gating expiry on `status == "OK"` (~:306). The string `"grace_period"` does not appear anywhere in the vendored OpenAPI spec; the per-device `state` enum is exactly `[active, expired, expiring, recentlyQueued, unused, unusedActive]`. Separately, co-term orgs (status `"OK"`) are **excluded** from any `status="active"` panel.

N/A — Grafana dashboard JSON, no Meraki API change.

### Notes / risks

**Area:** `dashboards` · **Type:** `qol` · **Priority:** `P3` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M16 — Dashboard rebuild

### Problem / impact
Two panels use an exact-match `org_id="$organization"` matcher while the `organization` template variable is multi-select with `includeAll` (default `$__all`) and the panel does **not** repeat. With All/multi-select, Grafana interpolates `$organization` as a pipe-joined list and substitutes it literally into the `=` matcher, so it never matches.

Evidence (validated 2026-07-01): the `organization` var in both dashboards has `multi: true, includeAll: true`. `organization-overview.json` panel id 9 ('API Rate Limit Usage', expr at :738 with `org_id="$organization"`) has `repeat: None`; `api-usage-licensing.json` panel id 3 ('API Rate Limit Usage Trend', expr at :304) likewise `repeat: None`. Sibling panels (organization-overview panel 14, api-usage-licensing panel 2) correctly set `repeat: organization` — these two are the odd ones out.

### Meraki API
N/A — Grafana dashboard JSON, no Meraki API change.

### Files to touch
- `dashboards/organization-overview.json` — panel id 9 (expr ~:738)
- `dashboards/api-usage-licensing.json` — panel id 3 (expr ~:304)

Fix direction: either change the matcher to a regex `org_id=~"$organization"` (handles the pipe-joined multi value) or set `repeat: organization` on the panel to match its siblings.

### Notes / risks
Validated CONFIRMED (high confidence). Prefer whichever pattern the rebuild standardises on (regex matcher vs repeat) — be consistent with sibling panels.

**Area:** `dashboards` · **Type:** `qol` · **Priority:** `P2` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M16 — Dashboard rebuild

### Problem / impact
Eight panels wrap `rate(...)` around metrics that are **re-set gauges over a rolling window**, not monotonic counters — so `rate()` is semantically meaningless and the panels render garbage.

Evidence (validated 2026-07-01):
- `meraki_mr_connection_stats_total` is a **gauge** (mr/clients.py:56 `_create_gauge(MRMetricName.MR_CONNECTION_<net-name-4>TS, "...over the last 30 minutes...")`) fetched with `timespan=1800` (clients.py:142).
- `meraki_org_usage_{up,down}stream_kb` use `timespan=3600` (organization_collectors/client_overview.py:48).
- `meraki_network_wireless_connection_stats_total` — same windowed-gauge nature.

Panels wrapping these in `rate(...[$__rate_interval])`:
- `dashboards/mr-access-points.json` ~lines 377, 446, 556 (Connection Events by Type, Overall Connection Success Rate, Success Rate Heatmap by AP)
- `dashboards/network-overview.json` ~lines 392, 461, 539 (same pattern on `meraki_network_wireless_connection_stats_total`)
- `dashboards/client-overview.json` ~lines 843, 856 (`rate(meraki_org_usage_upstream_kb/downstream_kb)`)

### Meraki API
N/A — Grafana dashboard JSON, no Meraki API change.

### Files to touch
- `dashboards/mr-access-points.json` (~377, 446, 556)
- `dashboards/network-overview.json` (~392, 461, 539)
- `dashboards/client-overview.json` (~843, 856)

Fix direction: drop the `rate()` wrapper and query the gauge directly (it already represents the windowed value); adjust legend/units accordingly.

### Notes / risks
Validated CONFIRMED (high confidence). These are windowed **gauges** re-set each poll, not counters — never `rate()`/`increase()` them.

**Related units nuance for the rebuild (F-115 live validation):** `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes` is a bytes-per-**second** rate over the poll window, NOT a cumulative byte counter — panels must format it as bandwidth (Bps) and must **never** wrap it in `rate()`/`increase()` or render it as a total. Same class of 'already-a-rate gauge' mistake as this finding; watch for it across the rebuild.

**Dashboards are frozen until the dedicated rebuild task (see `dashboards/CLAUDE.md`); do NOT fix this from a code-change session** — no `dashboards/*.json` edits belong in exporter code work (golden rule #514). This issue is an input to that rebuild task only.

**Post-sweep names:** the M13 metric-naming sweep will rename many series (drop `_total` from gauges, fix `_kb`/`_mb`/`_kbps`/`_ms`/`_percent` unit + suffix conventions), so the rebuild must author panels against the **post-sweep** metric names, not the names quoted here.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No `rate()`/`increase()` wraps any windowed-gauge metric across the 8 panels
- [ ] `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes` panels (if touched) format as Bps, never rated
- [ ] Panels render sensible values against a live scrape
- [ ] Gauge-vs-counter nature verified against the collector source

### Notes / risks
Validated CONFIRMED (high confidence). `Info` metrics only ever expose `<name>_info` — verify against a live `/metrics` scrape during the rebuild. All three dashboards share the same broken org template variable, so fix the variable definition and every panel that consumes it.

### Problem / impact
Device-down detection latency is undocumented and the README oversells it. Device state is refreshed on the MEDIUM (300s) tier, and Meraki's own offline-detection lag stacks on top, so worst-case device-down visibility is ~10+ minutes — but nothing documents this. The README calls webhooks 'real-time', yet webhooks only **count** events; they don't flip `meraki_device_up`. Users therefore write alerts with wrong `for:` durations and expect real-time state they won't get. Fix: a data-freshness doc with a per-tier staleness table + Meraki-side detection lag + alert `for:` guidance, and soften the README webhook claim.

### Meraki API

- `/clients` renders client MAC / IP / hostname / username (PII).
- `/cardinality` (and its 5 sub-routes) leaks label values.
- `/status`, `/metrics` expose full topology and metric surface.
- `POST /api/collectors/trigger` being open by default lets an unauthenticated caller burn the org API-rate-limit budget on demand.

There is no TLS on the listener and no documented reverse-proxy pattern, so a 'just expose the port' deployment leaks everything. This is a v1 exposure gate: we need (a) a threat-model doc enumerating every endpoint and exactly what it leaks, and (b) a real mitigation — extend the bearer token to the sensitive GET UIs, and/or add a `ui_enabled=false` flag to drop the human UI surface entirely, plus (c) a documented reverse-proxy / TLS-termination pattern.

### Meraki API
N/A — HTTP-surface / config hardening, not a Meraki API change.

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/app.py` — endpoint auth guards (currently only app.py:179-195, 784, 813); extend the `SERVER__API_TOKEN` check to sensitive GETs (`/clients`, `/cardinality*`, `/status`) and/or add a `ui_enabled` gate.
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/config_models.py` — `SERVER__API_TOKEN` (:339); add `ui_enabled` (or equivalent) setting.
- `docs/security.md` — new 'Endpoint exposure & threat model' section enumerating each endpoint + what it leaks + the recommended reverse-proxy/TLS pattern (nav: Deployment & Operations → Security, zensical.toml).
- `docs/reference/endpoints.md` — annotate which endpoints carry PII / are auth-gated.

### Notes / risks
Sources: SEC-01 (P1), GAP-05, CFG-16 (no listener TLS), SEC-08. Native listener TLS/mTLS is deliberately out of scope here (roadmap item GAP-23 / #321-adjacent, M8) — v1 minimum is docs + token-extension/ui_enabled + reverse-proxy guidance. Pairs with item 52 (privacy doc) and item 56 (NetworkPolicy). Constant-time token compares already exist (SEC OK-list) — reuse them for any new guard.

- [ ] `make check` (ruff + mypy + pytest) is green — evidence, not assertion
- [ ] `make docgen` re-run and any regenerated docs committed if metrics/config changed
- [ ] Change follows repo law (enums, Pydantic + `validate_response_format`, NetworkFilter via inventory, `_set_metric` expiration, bounded cardinality)

### Problem / impact
Mutable human names — `name`, `org_name`, `network_name`, `port_name` — are denormalized onto **every** series (MET-08). When an org/network/port is renamed, Prometheus sees the old label set die and a new one appear: series churn, orphaned samples, broken `rate()` continuity, and range-vector gaps across the rename. `services/inventory.py:143` already demonstrates the correct pattern for the filter gauges (id-keyed series + name on a join metric).

**Decide the pre-v1 policy:** either (a) **accept + document** that name labels are convenience denormalization and churn on rename (cheap, honest), or (b) **move names to `_info` join metrics** keyed by id (consistent with the item #533 client-info decision) and drop them from numeric series. This is a contract decision that should be settled before 1.0 and stated in the stability doc (item #535).

### Meraki API
N/A — internal label-shape policy.

- If option (b): `collectors/**` emission sites, `core/metrics.py` (`LabelName`), new `_info` metrics, `services/inventory.py` pattern reused
- Tests + `make docgen` if metrics change

### Notes / risks
- If the decision is (b) it becomes a larger metric-shape change and should be sequenced with item #533 to reuse the info-join machinery. If (a), this collapses to a documentation task.

# Sweep spec — #534: drop mutable name labels from numeric series; join via id-keyed `*_info` metrics

Decision context (settled, do not re-open): **Option B**, per Rob 2026-07-02 and the settled contract in `docs/stability.md` ("Name labels are not part of numeric series", lines 123–155). Numeric series carry stable IDs only; display names live on id-keyed `*_info` join metrics; consumers re-attach via `<numeric> * on(<id>) group_left(<name>) <..._info>`. This spec is a full inventory of **current** code (validated 2026-07-02 against `main` @ `42322b6` — all line refs below are from this validation, not the original issue).

---

## (A) Summary + magnitude

- **202 metric definitions** across **24 collector files** currently carry at least one name-family label (`org_name`, `network_name`, `name`, `port_name`, `sensor_name`, `zone_name`, `description`, `hostname`). That is essentially **every Meraki-data metric family** — only exporter self-metrics (`meraki_exporter_*`), webhook metrics, and the `meraki_network_filter_*` gauges (already ids-only, F-079) are clean.
- **The single biggest lever is `core/label_helpers.py`**: `create_org_labels` / `create_network_labels` / `create_device_labels` / `create_port_labels` / `create_client_labels` inject the name labels at ~150 emission call sites. Rewriting the five helpers to ID-only output flips most emissions at once; the per-collector work is then the `labelnames=[...]` definition lists, hand-built label dicts (`alerts.py`, `config.py`, `device.py`, `clients.py`, `mt_alerts.py`, `network_health.py`, `devices/mt.py`, `devices/mv.py`), and tests.
- **3 new `_info` metrics** are needed: `meraki_network_info` (the backbone of the sweep — nothing today maps network_id→network_name), `meraki_ms_port_info`, `meraki_mv_zone_info`. `meraki_org_info` and `meraki_device_status_info` already exist and are retained as the org/device name carriers.
- **~30 test files** need label-set updates; `make docgen` regenerates the metrics reference.
- Sizing: **wave-0 seam + 10 parallel lanes**; the whole sweep is one coordinated change (see Risks) — everything is transiently red between the seam landing and the last lane finishing, green at the integration checkpoint.
- Scope boundary with **#533**: `description`/`hostname`/`mac` removal from client series and the creation of `meraki_client_info` are #533's contract; this sweep's clients lane drops only `org_name`/`network_name` from client series. **Recommendation: fold #533 and the #534 clients lane into one lane** (same file, one owner). Note: contrary to earlier recon, #533 is **not yet implemented in code** — `collectors/clients.py:89–307` still carries `description`/`hostname`/`mac` and no `meraki_client_info` exists; only the docs contract is in place.

---

## (B) Inventory

Bucket key: **DJ** = DROP+JOIN (ID already present, `_info` carrier exists after wave 0) · **NI** = needs the NEW/extended `_info` defined in section C · **KEEP** = name label retained (see G). Homogeneous blocks are grouped; labels shown are the name-family labels to drop → the stable ID(s) that remain.

### `collectors/organization.py` (23 defs; emissions also in `organization_collectors/{api_usage,license,client_overview,firmware,device_availability_history}.py`)

| `meraki_exporter_org_collection_status` | organization.py:85 | `org_name` | `org_id` | DJ |
| `meraki_org` (prometheus `Info` → exposed `meraki_org_info`) | organization.py:92 | — (carrier) | `org_id` | **KEEP** `org_name` |
| All 21 numeric org metrics: `meraki_org_api_requests_count`, `_api_requests_by_status`, `_networks`, `_devices`, `_devices_by_model`, `_devices_availability`, `_devices_availability_changes_count`, `_firmware_upgrades`, `_firmware_upgrades_pending`, `_licenses`, `_licenses_expiring`, `_clients_count`, `_usage_{total,downstream,upstream}_bytes`, `_packetcaptures`, `_packetcaptures_remaining`, `_application_usage_{total,downstream,upstream}_bytes`, `_application_usage_percent` | organization.py:99–256 | `org_name` | `org_id` | DJ |

### `collectors/config.py` (16 defs)
| Metric(s) | Def site | Drop | Join key | Bucket |

## (C) New/extended `_info` metrics (full definitions)

**NI-1 — `meraki_network_info` (NEW — the backbone; nothing maps network_id→network_name today):**
- Enum: `NetworkMetricName.NETWORK_INFO = "meraki_network_info"` (`core/constants/metrics_constants.py`).
- Type: Gauge, constant value `1` (info pattern, matching `meraki_device_status_info`).
- Labels: `org_id`, `network_id` (join key), `network_name`. Nothing else — additive later if needed.
- Emitter: `OrganizationCollector` (MEDIUM tier), inside `_collect_network_metrics` (`collectors/organization.py`) — it already fetches the filtered network list via `api_helper.get_organization_networks()` (inventory-routed, `NetworkFilter` enforced), so this costs **zero extra API calls**. One `1` per allowed network.
- Expiration: emit via `self._set_metric(...)` so `MetricExpirationManager` retires series when a network is deleted or filtered out.
- Join: `<numeric> * on(network_id) group_left(network_name) meraki_network_info`.

**NI-2 — `meraki_ms_port_info` (NEW):**
- Enum: `MSMetricName.MS_PORT_INFO = "meraki_ms_port_info"`.
- Type: Gauge, value `1`.
- Labels: `org_id`, `network_id`, `serial`, `port_id` (join keys `serial`+`port_id`), `port_name`.
- Emitter: `MSCollector` (`devices/ms.py`), in the per-port status loop (org-wide `getOrganizationSwitchPortsStatusesBySwitch` path and the per-device fallback) — the port `name` is already in hand at every emission site via `create_port_labels`. Zero extra API calls. Emit via `self.parent._set_metric()` (DeviceCollector expiration bucket, same as all other MS series).
- Cardinality: 1 series per switch port (~9.6k at LARGE scale) — <3% on top of the ~34 existing per-port families. Trivial.
- Join: `meraki_ms_port_status * on(serial, port_id) group_left(port_name) meraki_ms_port_info`.

**NI-3 — `meraki_mv_zone_info` (NEW; experimental family):**
- Enum: `MVMetricName.MV_ZONE_INFO = "meraki_mv_zone_info"`.
- Type: Gauge, value `1`.
- Labels: `org_id`, `network_id`, `serial`, `zone_id` (join keys `serial`+`zone_id`), `zone_name`.
- Emitter: `MVCollector._collect_analytics_zones` (`devices/mv.py`) — it already builds and caches the `zone_id → zone_label` map (`_last_zone_maps`, mv.py:50–53); emit one series per zone from that map. On SLOW-gated cycles where the zones call is skipped, re-emit from the cached map (same mechanism people_count already uses for zone-name resolution). Via `parent._set_metric()`.
- Join: `meraki_mv_people_count * on(serial, zone_id) group_left(zone_name) meraki_mv_zone_info`.

**Existing carriers (retained, adjusted):**
- `meraki_org_info` (`meraki_org` prometheus `Info`, organization.py:92, emitted :372–377): unchanged — keys `org_id`, carries `org_name` (+`url`, `api_enabled`). The canonical org join.
- `meraki_device_status_info` (device.py:226): **keeps `name`** (canonical device join per the docs/stability.md example), keeps `model`/`device_type`/`status`, **drops `org_name`/`network_name`** (org/network names chain-join via their own info metrics). Safe for `on(serial) group_left(name)` because exactly one status series per serial is live at a time (stale-status removal at device.py:1040–1060 — that positional `.remove()` list must be updated to the new label set).
- `meraki_client_info` — **#533 scope**, keyed `client_id`, carries `description`/`hostname`/`mac`. Not defined here; the clients lane implements it under #533.

**RISKS / MAGNITUDE (plain statement):** this is a single coordinated breaking change, not an incremental one — the `label_helpers.py` seam makes ~every collector red until its lane lands, so the sweep must merge as one change-set (or a tight commit train on the same day), never partially. Every numeric series in the exporter changes identity once (label set shrinks) — a full-fleet TSDB series reset for consumers, explicitly permitted by the one-time pre-1.0 sweep in docs/stability.md and already the declared contract. No new collector is required (all three new `_info` metrics piggyback on existing fetch paths, zero extra API calls) and cardinality added is trivial (≈ networks + switch ports + camera zones ≈ +10k series at LARGE scale vs the ~0.5–1M baseline). Biggest execution risks: the positional `.remove()`/series-clear sites (device.py:1047, mx.py uplink clear) which fail silently if the label order drifts, and test-assertion sprawl (~30 files). Total honest size: ~200 metric definitions, ~36 source files, ~30 test files, 10 lanes + seam + docs pass.
