body:
**Area:** `clients` · **Type:** `feature` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** M13 — V1 readiness: metric contract

### Problem / impact
Per-client numeric metrics (`meraki_client_status`, `meraki_client_usage_{sent,recv,total}_kb`, `meraki_client_application_usage_{sent,recv,total}_kb`, `meraki_wireless_client_rssi`, `meraki_wireless_client_snr`) are labelled with `mac` + `hostname` + `description` — high-cardinality, mutable, attacker-influenceable **PII** stamped onto every time series (MET-07 / APIORG-12 / SCALE-06 / GAP-11). The emission path is also **uncapped** (`max_clients_per_network` caps only `ClientStore`, not the metric fan-out) and the 9 client families emit via raw `.labels().set()` so they are **never expiration-tracked** — departed clients leak for the process lifetime (SCALE-06). Signal-quality (RSSI/SNR) costs one API call per client (~80k calls/600s at scale).

**Rob DECIDED (2026-07-02): ID-only numeric series + an info-join metric.** Scope:
1. **Drop `mac`/`hostname`/`description` from all numeric client series** — keep only a stable `client_id` (+ bounded network/org labels).
2. **Add `meraki_client_info{client_id, mac, hostname, description, ...}` = 1** as the single join metric carrying the descriptive/PII fields (Prometheus info-join pattern), so dashboards join on `client_id` instead of denormalizing PII everywhere.
3. **Cap the metric emission path** (not just `ClientStore`) with a global/per-network client cap and alarm-don't-silently-drop.
4. **Route all client families through `parent._set_metric()`** so they expire when a client departs.
5. **Make signal-quality (RSSI/SNR) opt-in** given its per-client call cost.

### Meraki API
Existing client fetchers (network clients, application usage, wireless signal quality). No new endpoint — verify current SDK methods and response shapes in `collectors/clients.py` before editing.

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/clients.py` (emission path, labels, caps, opt-in flag)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (`ClientMetricName`: add `CLIENT_INFO`)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/metrics.py` (`LabelName` for the info metric)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/config_models.py` (signal-quality opt-in setting)
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/services/client_store.py` (cap wiring)
- Tests + `make docgen`

### Notes / risks
- **Merges MET-07 + APIORG-12 + SCALE-06 + GAP-11** — the numeric-label contract half. The privacy **documentation** half (GDPR/PII doc) is a separate M14 issue; the anonymize/allowlist knobs, if any, live with the privacy doc.
- Clients collector is OFF by default (`CLIENTS__ENABLED=false`), so this is not a default-config regression, but it IS a breaking metric-shape change for anyone who enabled it — land pre-1.0.
- Info-join is the same pattern `services/inventory.py` already uses for filter gauges.
- Source findings: MET-07, APIORG-12, SCALE-06, GAP-11.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Metric name(s) added to the correct domain enum in `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`
- [ ] Labels drawn from the `LabelName` enum (`core/metrics.py`); no hardcoded label strings
- [ ] Response parsed through a Pydantic domain model and wrapped with `core.error_handling.validate_response_format`
- [ ] Emitted via `parent._set_metric()` so the value is expiration-tracked
- [ ] Update tier (FAST/MEDIUM/SLOW) chosen and justified; org-wide bulk endpoint preferred where available
- [ ] Cardinality bounded — no client MAC / raw SSID/BSSID / per-request or attacker-influenced labels
- [ ] `make docgen` run and the generated metric reference updated
- [ ] `mac`/`hostname`/`description` removed from all numeric client series (only `client_id` + bounded labels remain)
- [ ] `meraki_client_info` join metric emitted with the descriptive fields, value 1
- [ ] Client metric emission path capped (global/per-network) with an alarm, not silent drop
- [ ] All client families routed through `_set_metric()`; departed clients expire (regression test)
- [ ] RSSI/SNR signal-quality collection gated behind an opt-in setting, default off

# Implementation spec — #533: Client metrics v1 label contract (ID-only numeric series + `meraki_client_info` join, capped, expiration-tracked, signal-quality opt-in)

## 1. TL;DR

Strip the PII/mutable labels (`mac`, `description`, `hostname`, and also `ssid`) off every per-client numeric series in `collectors/clients.py`, leaving exactly `{org_id, network_id, client_id}` (+ `type` on app-usage), and emit one new join metric `meraki_client_info{org_id,network_id,client_id,mac,description,hostname,ssid} = 1` per client — the only client metric allowed to carry descriptive fields, following the exact pattern of `meraki_network_info` (`collectors/organization.py:99-106,604-619`: plain Gauge, value 1, routed through `_set_metric` for expiration). All client metric families switch from raw `.labels().set()` to `self._set_metric(...)` so departed clients expire (SCALE-06). A new emission-path cap (per-network reuse of `max_clients_per_network` + new global `max_clients_total`) truncates the client list before DNS/store/metrics with a WARNING log and a new `meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap` alarm gauge; `ClientStore` gains the same global cap. Per-client wireless RSSI/SNR collection becomes opt-in behind new `ClientSettings.signal_quality_enabled` (default False). `create_client_labels` (`core/label_helpers.py:150`) becomes genuinely ID-only. SDK methods confirmed present in installed meraki 3.3.0: `Networks.getNetworkClients`, `Networks.getNetworkClientsApplicationUsage`, `Wireless.getNetworkWirelessSignalQualityHistory`.

## 2. FROZEN SEAM ADDITIONS (paste verbatim; no other seam files change)

**`core/constants/metrics_constants.py` — two enum members:**

In `ClientMetricName` (after `CLIENT_<net-name-4>TUS`, line 392):
```python
    # id-keyed join carrier (issue #533): the ONLY client metric allowed to carry
    # descriptive/PII-ish labels (mac/description/hostname/ssid). Numeric client
    # series are ID-only and join via
    # `<numeric> * on(client_id) group_left(mac, hostname, ...) meraki_client_info`.
    CLIENT_INFO = "meraki_client_info"
```

In `CollectorMetricName` (after `EXPORTER_CARDINALITY_LIMIT_REACHED` block, ~line 449):
```python
    # Clients dropped from metric emission by the per-network/global client cap
    # (#533). Per-cycle snapshot gauge (0 = within caps), not a Counter.
    CLIENTS_OVER_CAP = "meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap"
```

**`core/config_models.py` — two fields appended to `ClientSettings` (after `max_clients_per_network`, line 432-437):**
```python
    max_clients_total: int = Field(
        25000,
        ge=100,
        le=1_000_000,
        description=(
            "Global cap on clients emitted as metric series across ALL networks per "
            "collection cycle. Clients beyond the cap are dropped from metric emission "
            "with a warning and counted in meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap."
        ),
    )
    signal_quality_enabled: bool = Field(
        False,
        description=(
            "Enable per-client wireless signal quality (RSSI/SNR) collection. Costs one "
            "API call per wireless client per cycle (interval-gated); prohibitively "
            "expensive at scale, so disabled by default."
        ),
    )
```
Env vars (auto, `env_nested_delimiter="__"`, `core/config.py:29,33`): `MERAKI_EXPORTER_CLIENTS__MAX_CLIENTS_TOTAL`, `MERAKI_EXPORTER_CLIENTS__SIGNAL_QUALITY_ENABLED`.

**Frozen internal signatures (collectors/clients.py):**
```python
def _apply_emission_cap(
    self, org_id: str, network_id: str, network_name: str, clients: list[NetworkClient]
) -> list[NetworkClient]: ...          # NEW; sync (no awaits) so the shared counter is race-free

async def _collect_application_usage(
    self, org_id: str, org_name: str, network_id: str, network_name: str,
    clients: list[NetworkClient],

async def _collect_wireless_signal_quality(
    self, org_id: str, org_name: str, network_id: str, network_name: str,
    clients: list[NetworkClient],

```
`create_client_labels` keeps its exact signature (`core/label_helpers.py:150-157`); only its returned dict changes to `{org_id, network_id, client_id}` (+extras).

**Frozen label contract:**

| Metric | Labels |
|---|---|
| `meraki_client_status`, `meraki_client_usage_{sent,recv,total}_bytes`, `meraki_wireless_client_rssi`, `meraki_wireless_client_snr` | `org_id, network_id, client_id` |
| `meraki_client_application_usage_{sent,recv,total}_bytes` | `org_id, network_id, client_id, type` |
| `meraki_client_info` (Gauge, value 1) | `org_id, network_id, client_id, mac, description, hostname, ssid` |
| `meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap` (Gauge) | `org_id, network_id` |

No `LabelName` additions needed — `CLIENT_ID/MAC/DESCRIPTION/HOSTNAME/SSID` all exist (`core/metrics.py:84-87,64`). **`core/metrics.py` is NOT touched** (issue's file list is stale on this point).

## 3. Per-file change list

**`collectors/clients.py`** (all anchors current as of `main`):
- `_initialize_metrics` (82-297): reduce `labelnames` on `client_status` (92-100), `client_usage_sent/recv/total` (105-145), `client_app_usage_*` (227-267, keep `LabelName.TYPE`), `wireless_client_rssi/snr` (270-297) per the table above. Add two new gauges: `self.client_info = self._create_gauge(ClientMetricName.CLIENT_INFO, "Client information join metric (client_id -> mac/description/hostname/ssid); value is always 1. Labels churn (old series expire) when a client's hostname/description/SSID changes.", labelnames=[LabelName.ORG_ID, LabelName.NETWORK_ID, LabelName.CLIENT_ID, LabelName.MAC, LabelName.DESCRIPTION, LabelName.HOSTNAME, LabelName.SSID])` and `self.clients_over_cap = self._create_gauge(CollectorMetricName.CLIENTS_OVER_CAP, "Clients excluded from metric emission in the most recent cycle because the per-network or global client cap was reached (0 = within caps)", labelnames=[LabelName.ORG_ID, LabelName.NETWORK_ID])`. Append to RSSI/SNR HELP (272-273, 287): keep the existing "most recent 5-min sample" phrase intact (test `test_windowed_metric_help_states_window`, tests/unit/test_clients_collector.py:118 asserts it) and add "; collected only when MERAKI_EXPORTER_CLIENTS__SIGNAL_QUALITY_ENABLED=true". Import `CollectorMetricName` alongside `ClientMetricName` (line 15) and `create_labels` from `..core.metrics` (line 23).
- `_collect_impl` (299-349): add `self._cycle_clients_emitted = 0` next to the existing counter resets (306-307).
- NEW `_apply_emission_cap` (place after `_collect_network_clients`): per-network truncate to `self.settings.clients.max_clients_per_network`, then to `max(self.settings.clients.max_clients_total - self._cycle_clients_emitted, 0)`; `self._cycle_clients_emitted += len(allowed)`; always emit dropped-count (0 included) via `self._set_metric(self.clients_over_cap, create_labels(org_id=org_id, network_id=network_id), dropped, CollectorMetricName.CLIENTS_OVER_CAP.value)`; `logger.warning("Client cap exceeded; dropping clients from metric emission", org_id=..., network_id=..., network_name=..., total_clients=..., emitted=..., dropped=..., per_network_cap=..., global_cap=...)` when `dropped > 0`; return the truncated list.
- `_collect_network_clients` (407-509): after `clients = [NetworkClient.model_validate(c) ...]` (463) and the counters (466-467), insert `clients = self._apply_emission_cap(org_id, network_id, network_name, clients)` — BEFORE DNS resolution (479-487) so DNS fan-out is also bounded. Update the two call sites at 502-509 to drop the `hostnames` argument.
- `_update_metrics` (685-846): keep `hostnames` param (needed for info metric + `_determine_hostname`). Per client: build ID-only labels via `create_client_labels({"id": client.id}, org_id=org_id, org_name=org_name, network_id=network_id, network_name=network_name)` — remove the `ssid=` extra (765) and the mac/description/hostname dict entries (753-758). Replace direct sets 770, 779-781 with `self._set_metric(self.client_status, labels, status_value, ClientMetricName.CLIENT_<net-name-4>TUS.value)` etc. Emit the info series once per client: `info_labels = create_labels(org_id=org_id, network_id=network_id, client_id=client.id, mac=client.mac, description=sanitized_description, hostname=sanitized_hostname, ssid=ssid or "Unknown")` then `self._set_metric(self.client_info, info_labels, 1, ClientMetricName.CLIENT_INFO.value)`. Route the three aggregate loops (804, 822, 840) through `self._set_metric` too (they're client families; SSIDs/VLANs/capabilities that vanish must expire).
- `_collect_application_usage` (854-1007): remove `hostnames` param; delete the hostname/description resolution block (942-948) and shrink `client_data`/labels (960-973) to `create_client_labels({"id": client_id}, org_id=..., org_name=..., network_id=..., network_name=..., type=sanitized_app)`; replace the three `.labels().set()` (976-978) with `self._set_metric(..., ClientMetricName.CLIENT_APPLICATION_USAGE_*_BYTES.value)`.
- `_collect_wireless_signal_quality` (1015-1195): add the opt-in gate as the FIRST statement of the body: `if not self.settings.clients.signal_quality_enabled: logger.debug("Client signal quality collection is disabled", network_id=network_id); return`. Remove `hostnames` param; delete hostname resolution (1138-1144); labels become ID-only (drop `ssid=` extra at 1159 and mac/desc/hostname at 1147-1152); replace 1164/1167 with `self._set_metric(..., ClientMetricName.WIRELESS_CLIENT_RSSI.value / WIRELESS_CLIENT_SNR.value)`. Keep the existing interval gate and `client_signal_quality_max_clients` cap (1045-1075) — they still apply when enabled.
- Leave the unlabeled `meraki_exporter_client_dns_*` / `client_store_*` self-metrics (148-192, 1197-1259) exactly as they are — `_set_metric` requires labelled Gauges (`.labels(**{})` raises on unlabeled metrics) and these are exporter-lifetime series that must not expire.

**`core/label_helpers.py:150-205`** — `create_client_labels`: drop `mac/description/hostname` extraction (188-191) and from the `create_labels(...)` call (197-205); return `{org_id, network_id, client_id}` (+extras). Rewrite the docstring (esp. 160-163, which currently says the removal is "out of scope") to state the #533 contract: numeric client series are ID-only; descriptive fields live on `meraki_client_info`.

**`services/client_store.py`** — `__init__` (21-44): add `self.max_clients_total = settings.clients.max_clients_total`. `update_clients` (46-188): compute `global_total = sum(len(c) for c in self._clients.values())` and `global_capacity = max(self.max_clients_total - global_total, 0)` before the loop; in the new-client branch (136-173) skip creation once `new_count >= global_capacity` (updates to existing clients always proceed), count skips, and after the loop emit one `logger.warning("Global client store cap reached; not adding new clients", network_id=..., skipped=..., global_cap=self.max_clients_total)` when skips > 0. The `/clients` web page keeps full descriptive data — the store's fields are unchanged.

**`core/constants/metrics_constants.py`, `core/config_models.py`** — seam additions above, nothing else.

**Docs**: `make docgen` regenerates `docs/config.md` (ClientSettings is already in `generate_config_docs.py`'s `nested_models` — existing model, new fields picked up automatically) and `docs/metrics/metrics.md` (AST-based, picks up new label sets + new gauges). `scripts/generate_metrics_docs.py` `CONDITIONAL_NOTES` is per-owner only (scripts/generate_metrics_docs.py:30-33) — do NOT modify it; the signal-quality requirement rides in the RSSI/SNR HELP text. `docs/stability.md` already documents this contract — no edit. `docs/metrics/overview.md` has no stale client-label references (verified by grep).

## 4. TDD test plan (write these failing first)

In `tests/unit/test_clients_collector.py` (reuse `BaseCollectorTest` patterns; `settings.clients.*` direct assignment bypasses pydantic validation — existing tests already do `settings.clients.enabled = True`):

1. **`test_numeric_client_series_are_id_only`** — set up like `test_collect_basic_client_metrics` (166-222); after collection assert for each of `meraki_client_status`, `meraki_client_usage_sent_bytes/_recv_bytes/_total_bytes`: `all(set(ls.keys()) == {"org_id", "network_id", "client_id"} for ls in metrics.get_all_label_sets(name))` and non-empty. For app usage (mock `getNetworkClientsApplicationUsage` like 315ff): keys == `{"org_id","network_id","client_id","type"}`. For rssi/snr (with `settings.clients.signal_quality_enabled = True`, mock like 408ff): keys == `{"org_id","network_id","client_id"}`. **This is the acceptance regression test — fails today because labels include mac/description/hostname/ssid.**
2. **`test_client_info_join_metric_emitted`** — same setup; `metrics.assert_gauge_value("meraki_client_info", 1, client_id="c1", mac="aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:01", network_id="N_123")`; assert full key set of every `meraki_client_info` label set == `{"org_id","network_id","client_id","mac","description","hostname","ssid"}`; assert hostname label equals the DNS-resolved value (`client1-example-com` after `_sanitize_label_value` hyphenation of dots — compute expected via the same rule) and one info series per client.
3. **`test_per_network_cap_drops_and_alarms`** — `settings.clients.max_clients_per_network = 2`; 3 clients; with `capture_logs()` assert a warning event containing `"Client cap exceeded"`; assert only 2 `client_id` values across `meraki_client_status` label sets; `metrics.assert_gauge_value("meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap", 1, network_id="N_123")`.
4. **`test_global_cap_drops_and_alarms`** — `settings.clients.max_clients_total = 2`, per-network cap left large; 3 clients in one network → 2 emitted, over_cap == 1, warning logged. (Also assert `meraki_exporter_clients_over_cap` == 0 in the happy-path test 1.)
5. **`test_signal_quality_default_off`** — default settings (only `clients.enabled = True`); wire `api.wireless.getNetworkWirelessSignalQualityHistory = MagicMock(...)`; after collection assert the mock was **not called** and `metrics.assert_metric_not_set("meraki_wireless_client_rssi")`.
6. **`test_client_metrics_are_expiration_tracked`** — construct the collector manually (pattern at 24-47) passing `expiration_manager=MagicMock()`; after collection assert `expiration_manager.track_metric_update` was called with `metric_name="meraki_client_status"` and with `metric_name="meraki_client_info"` among the calls (inspect `call.kwargs["metric_name"]`).
7. **Update existing assertions**: sweep `test_clients_collector.py` + `test_clients_collector_enhanced.py` for label kwargs `ssid=`, `mac=`, `hostname=`, `description=` on client numeric series (e.g. 214-215 `ssid="Corporate"`) → re-key on `client_id` only, or move to `meraki_client_info` assertions. Signal-quality tests (408, 576, 654, 701) must set `settings.clients.signal_quality_enabled = True`.

In `tests/test_metrics.py:172-193` — rewrite `test_create_client_labels_drops_org_and_network_name` to assert the returned dict is exactly `{"org_id": "111", "network_id": "N_1", "client_id": "k1"}` and rename it (e.g. `test_create_client_labels_is_id_only`).

In `tests/unit/test_client_store.py` — **`test_global_cap_blocks_new_clients_but_updates_existing`**: `settings.clients.max_clients_total = 2` (direct assignment); `update_clients` net-A with 2 clients → both stored; `update_clients` net-B with 2 clients → 0 new stored + warning in `capture_logs`; re-`update_clients` net-A with changed status → existing clients still updated.

Gate: `make check` green + `make docgen` committed alongside.

## 5. Lane decomposition & routing

- **Lane 0 — seams (wave 0, before fan-out)**: `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` + `core/config_models.py`, exactly the frozen additions in §2. Routing: **orchestrator applies directly** (or sonnet/low) — it's paste work on funnelled seam files.
- **Lane A — collector + labels + collector tests** (the bulk, one owner): `collectors/clients.py`, `core/label_helpers.py`, `tests/unit/test_clients_collector.py`, `tests/unit/test_clients_collector_enhanced.py`, `tests/test_metrics.py`. Routing: **sonnet/high** — mechanical in shape but judgement-bearing (label plumbing across 3 emission paths, cap counter placement before DNS, preserving HELP phrases).
- **Lane B — store cap**: `services/client_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_client_store.py`. Disjoint from Lane A. Routing: **sonnet/medium**.
- **Lane C — docs/gate (after A+B merge)**: run `make docgen`, verify `docs/config.md` + `docs/metrics/metrics.md` diffs show the new fields/labels/metrics (check the generators' "Found N" counts), run `make check`. Routing: **sonnet/medium**. No hand-edits to generated files; no `dashboards/*.json`, no `docs/stability.md` changes.

Lanes A and B can run concurrently after Lane 0. Orchestrator owns commit (`Closes #533`) and the final gate.

## 6. Stale/wrong items in the issue (validated against current code)

1. **Metric names**: issue says `meraki_client_usage_{sent,recv,total}_kb` / `meraki_client_application_usage_{sent,recv,total}_kb` — already renamed to `_bytes` by the #531 sweep (`metrics_constants.py:396-410`). The label change applies to the `_bytes` names; no rename here.
2. **`core/metrics.py` LabelName addition**: NOT needed — every label the info metric uses already exists (`CLIENT_ID/MAC/DESCRIPTION/HOSTNAME/SSID`, `core/metrics.py:64,84-87`). The seam file stays untouched.
3. **`ssid` disposition** (issue silent): decided — dropped from numeric series (it is mutable per client and violates "stable client_id + bounded network/org labels"; evidence flags it: metric-contract-audit.md:86 "(+ssid)") and carried on `meraki_client_info` instead. The bounded aggregates `meraki_clients_per_ssid_count` / `_per_vlan_count` / `_capabilities_count` keep their existing label sets — they are not per-client series.
4. **"parent._set_metric()"**: `ClientsCollector` is a top-level `MetricCollector` (`@register_collector(UpdateTier.MEDIUM)`, clients.py:31), so the correct call is `self._set_metric(...)` (`core/collector.py:600-660`); `parent._set_metric` phrasing applies only to sub-collectors.
5. **Signal-quality "~80k calls/600s" mitigation partially exists**: interval gate + per-network 200-client cap already landed as F-060 (clients.py:1045-1075, `APISettings.client_signal_quality_interval/_max_clients`, config_models.py:171-185). #533's addition is only the default-OFF boolean; keep the F-060 knobs as the when-enabled throttles.

**Area:** `core` · **Type:** `ops` · **Priority:** `P1` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M13 — V1 readiness: metric contract

### Problem / impact
Three exporter self-metrics have type/name mismatches (MET-06):

1. **`meraki_exporter_cardinality_analyzed_total` is a Gauge, not a Counter** (`collectors/cardinality.py:117`). The `_total` suffix implies a monotonic counter safe under `rate()`; it is actually a per-cycle snapshot gauge. Drop `_total` (or make it a real Counter).
2. **`meraki_exporter_collection_errors_total_expired` is a Counter but the `_total` is not the suffix** (`core/metric_expiration.py:91`) — the `_expired` tail after `_total` breaks the convention. Rename so the counter ends `_total` (e.g. `..._expired_total`).
3. **`meraki_exporter_cache_size_tracked_metrics` is a misnamed concatenation** (`core/metric_expiration.py:96`) built from `INVENTORY_CACHE_SIZE` — the name reads as a cache-size gauge but measures tracked-metric count. Rename to reflect what it measures.

### Meraki API
N/A — exporter self-metrics only.

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/cardinality.py`
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/metric_expiration.py`
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (`CollectorMetricName`)
- Tests asserting these names; `make docgen`

### Notes / risks
- Pre-1.0 renames, no dual-emit (consistent with item #531 decision).
- Coordinate with item #531 if landing in the same wave to avoid double docgen churn.
- Source finding: MET-06.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Implemented per the CLAUDE.md roadmap workflow (validate-before-implement, strict TDD)
- [ ] `make check` (ruff + mypy + pytest) green — evidence, not assertion
- [ ] Docs regenerated (`make docgen`) if user-facing metrics/config changed
- [ ] `cardinality_analyzed` gauge no longer carries `_total` (or is converted to a real Counter)
- [ ] `collection_errors_*_expired` counter ends in `_total`
- [ ] `cache_size_tracked_metrics` renamed to describe the tracked-metric count it holds
- [ ] Grep confirms no old names remain in source/tests; docgen updated

body:
**Area:** `core` · **Type:** `feature` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** M13 — V1 readiness: metric contract

### Problem / impact
The metric surface carries systematic naming and unit inconsistencies that violate the Prometheus naming/base-unit conventions. These are cheap to fix now and **impossible to fix cleanly after 1.0** without a deprecation dance. **Rob DECIDED (2026-07-02): rename NOW, pre-1.0, with NO dual-emit / no deprecation window.** The old names are simply replaced. This is the one coordinated sweep that closes MET-01..05 + APIDEV-03 together because they all touch `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`, every collector that emits them, and `make docgen` in a single wave.

**MET-01 — drop `_total` from snapshot GAUGE counts** (`_total` is reserved by Prometheus for monotonic counters safe under `rate()`/`increase()`; these are point-in-time gauges):

| Current | New |
|---|---|
| `meraki_org_networks_total` | `meraki_org_networks` |
| `meraki_org_devices_total` | `meraki_org_devices` |
| `meraki_org_devices_by_model_total` | `meraki_org_devices_by_model` |
| `meraki_org_devices_availability_total` | `meraki_org_devices_availability` |
| `meraki_org_licenses_total` | `meraki_org_licenses` |
| `meraki_org_clients_total` | `meraki_org_clients` |
| `meraki_org_admins_total` | `meraki_org_admins` |
| `meraki_org_admins_two_factor_enabled_total` | `meraki_org_admins_two_factor_enabled` |
| `meraki_org_firmware_upgrades_pending_total` | `meraki_org_firmware_upgrades_pending` |
| `meraki_ms_ports_active_total` | `meraki_ms_ports_active` |
| `meraki_ms_ports_inactive_total` | `meraki_ms_ports_inactive` |
| `meraki_ms_ports_by_media_total` | `meraki_ms_ports_by_media` |
| `meraki_ms_ports_by_link_speed_total` | `meraki_ms_ports_by_link_speed` |
| `meraki_ms_stack_members_total` | `meraki_ms_stack_members` |
| `meraki_mx_vpn_peers_total` | `meraki_mx_vpn_peers` |
| `meraki_mx_firewall_rules_total` | `meraki_mx_firewall_rules` |
| `meraki_network_bluetooth_clients_total` | `meraki_network_bluetooth_clients` |
| `meraki_mr_air_marshal_ssids_total` | `meraki_mr_air_marshal_ssids` |
| `meraki_mr_air_marshal_bssids_total` | `meraki_mr_air_marshal_bssids` |
| `meraki_mr_air_marshal_contained_bssids_total` | `meraki_mr_air_marshal_contained_bssids` |
| `meraki_mr_air_marshal_wired_detected_total` | `meraki_mr_air_marshal_wired_detected` |

(Note: F-091 consciously *kept* some of these `_total` gauges last cycle — this issue re-litigates that decision pre-1.0 and reverses it.)

**MET-02 — `_total` on WINDOWED / resetting gauges** (most dangerous class: they look like counters but reset every collection cycle, so `rate()` is meaningless). Drop the misleading `_total` and adopt the unified windowed-count suffix decided in MET-03:

| Current | Note |
|---|---|
| `meraki_org_api_requests_total` | flagship — 'last hour' windowed value, NOT monotonic |
| `meraki_org_configuration_changes_total` | windowed config-change count |
| `meraki_org_usage_total_kb` | windowed **and** unit bug (see MET-04) |
| `meraki_ms_port_packets_total` (+ broadcast/multicast/crcerrors/fragments/collisions/topologychanges) | 5-minute window |
| `meraki_mr_connection_stats_total` | windowed |
| `meraki_network_wireless_connection_stats_total` | windowed |
| `meraki_mr_ssid_failed_connections_total` | windowed |
| `meraki_mr_packets_total` / `meraki_mr_packets_lost_total` (+ network variants) | windowed |
| `meraki_alerts_total_by_severity` / `meraki_alerts_total_by_network` | windowed snapshot |
| `meraki_sensor_alerts_total` | windowed |

**MET-03 — unify `_count` vs `_total` for identical windowed semantics.** F-091 swept only 2 families, leaving `_count` metrics (`meraki_ms_port_client_count`, `meraki_mr_ssid_client_count`, `meraki_mt_alerting_sensors_count`, `meraki_wireless_client_capabilities_count`, `meraki_clients_per_ssid_count`, `meraki_clients_per_vlan_count`, `meraki_mx_security_events_count`) inconsistent with the windowed `_total` set above. **Decide ONE windowed-count convention** (bare name vs a documented suffix) and apply it uniformly across MET-02 + MET-03.

**MET-04 — non-base units in names** (Prometheus wants base units: bytes, seconds, ratio/percent). Convert name AND value:

| Current | New | Value fix |
|---|---|---|
| `meraki_org_usage_total_kb` / `_downstream_kb` / `_upstream_kb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000 |
| `meraki_org_application_usage_total_mb` / `_downstream_mb` / `_upstream_mb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000² |
| `meraki_mr_ssid_usage_total_mb` / `_downstream_mb` / `_upstream_mb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000² |
| `meraki_client_usage_sent_kb` / `_recv_kb` / `_total_kb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000 |
| `meraki_client_application_usage_sent_kb` / `_recv_kb` / `_total_kb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000 |
| `meraki_mx_vpn_usage_sent_kb` / `_recv_kb` | `..._bytes` | ×1000 |
| `meraki_network_wireless_download_kbps` / `_upload_kbps` | `..._bytes_per_second` | **DOUBLE BUG** (F-065): value is kiloBYTES/s, so ×1000 to bytes/s AND rename |
| `meraki_mx_uplink_latency_ms` | `..._seconds` | ÷1000 |
| `meraki_mx_vpn_stats_avg_latency_ms` | `..._seconds` | ÷1000 |
| `meraki_mr_device_latency_ms` | `..._seconds` | ÷1000 |
| `meraki_mr_network_client_latency_ms` | `..._seconds` | ÷1000 |
| `meraki_org_login_security_idle_timeout_minutes` | `..._seconds` | ×60 |
| `meraki_org_login_security_password_expiration_days` | `..._seconds` | ×86400 |
| `meraki_ms_poe_port_power_watthours` / `_total_watthours` / `_network_total_watthours` | verify: base energy unit (joules ×3600) vs keep watthours | see risks |

**APIDEV-03 — SI standardization (×1024 → ×1000).** Data-volume `_kb`/`_mb` conversions currently use ×1024 in several fetchers (e.g. `ms.py` `usageInKb`) while `_kbps` uses ×1000 in the same functions — ~2.4% over-report. Standardize on **×1000 for all data-volume** conversions during the `_bytes` migration above. Device **memory** KiB (`base.py`, already `_bytes`) may stay ×1024 (KiB is defensible) — call it out explicitly in the HELP text.

**MET-05 — `_percent` vs `_percentage`.** 10 metrics end `_percent`, 3 end `_percentage` (`meraki_org_application_usage_percentage`, `meraki_mr_ssid_usage_percentage`, `meraki_mt_battery_percentage`). Pick ONE suffix (recommend `_percent`, keeping values 0–100) and settle the percent-vs-ratio question in the same pass. Rename the 3 `_percentage` outliers to match.

### Meraki API
N/A — this is an internal naming/unit refactor. No new endpoints; verify existing units against the OpenAPI spec + live API before flipping value multipliers (see APIORG-01 spec-vs-live lesson).

### Files to touch
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (all enum string values — the frozen seam)
- Every collector that emits an affected metric: `collectors/organization_collectors/*`, `collectors/devices/*` (ms, mr, mx, mt), `collectors/network_health_collectors/*`, `collectors/alerts.py`, `collectors/clients.py`, `services/inventory.py`
- Value-conversion sites for the unit fixes (`_kb`/`_mb`/`_kbps`/`_ms`/`_minutes`/`_days`)
- Tests: every metric-name/value assertion referencing an old name
- `make docgen` regenerates the metric reference

### Notes / risks
- **Single coordinated wave.** `metrics_constants.py` is the frozen seam; edit it first, then fan out collector + test edits, then one `make docgen`. Transient red mid-wave is fine; `make check` must be green at the integration checkpoint and before commit.
- **No dual-emit / no deprecation alias** — Rob's explicit decision. Old names disappear.
- **Dashboards are FROZEN** — do NOT edit `dashboards/*.json`. The M16 dashboard rebuild will be authored against the new names.
- **Verify every value multiplier against the live API/spec before flipping** — some fields may already be in the target unit. The `_kbps` families are a confirmed double bug (value is kB/s).
- **`_watthours` is a genuine open decision** — energy base unit is joules (×3600), but PoE consumers may prefer watthours or instantaneous watts. Decide + document in HELP; don't silently pick.
- Update HELP strings in the same edit (ties into MET-09 window-language issue).
- Source findings: MET-01, MET-02, MET-03, MET-04, MET-05, APIDEV-03 (F-065, F-091).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Implemented per the CLAUDE.md roadmap workflow (validate-before-implement, strict TDD)
- [ ] `make check` (ruff + mypy + pytest) green — evidence, not assertion
- [ ] Docs regenerated (`make docgen`) if user-facing metrics/config changed
- [ ] All MET-01 snapshot gauges have `_total` removed
- [ ] All MET-02 windowed gauges renamed to the unified windowed-count convention
- [ ] MET-03 `_count` vs `_total` inconsistency resolved to one documented convention
- [ ] All `_kb`/`_mb` → `_bytes` (×1000) and `_kbps` → `_bytes_per_second` (value ×1000, double-bug fixed)
- [ ] All `_ms`/`_minutes`/`_days` → `_seconds` with correct value multipliers
- [ ] `_percent`/`_percentage` unified to one suffix; `_watthours` unit decision made + documented in HELP
- [ ] Grep confirms zero old metric names remain in source or tests; `make docgen` reference reflects only new names

This is a `fable-candidate` issue: the orchestrator spawns a dedicated **Fable, high-effort subagent** whose FIRST deliverable is the design/spec posted ON THIS ISSUE; mechanical implementation may then be delegated to a cheaper agent per that spec (the spec comment states the implementer routing). # Issue #531 design spec — coordinated v1 metric naming & unit sweep (MET-01..05 + APIDEV-03)

*(Authored by the dedicated Fable/high design subagent per #618 rule 4; posted by the orchestrator.)*

Verified against code at `f9e4316` (enum→file map built by grep over every `*MetricName.` reference; conversion sites confirmed by reading `devices/ms.py`, `devices/base.py`, `collectors/organization.py`). Where the issue/evidence and code disagreed, the code won (discrepancies noted in §6). Rename now, pre-1.0, **no dual-emit**. `dashboards/*.json` are frozen and WILL reference stale names after this lands — expected; the dashboard rebuild task owns that.

## 1. Decisions

**D1 — Windowed-count convention: `_count` suffix (MET-02/03).** Every gauge that counts events/objects observed *within a reporting window* (resets each cycle) gets `_count`; `_total` becomes strictly reserved for monotonic Counters. This matches the two F-091 precedents already shipped (`meraki_mx_security_events_count`, `meraki_mt_alerting_sensors_count`), so we extend the existing in-repo convention rather than invent one. Every `_count` metric's HELP MUST state the window (folds the affected part of MET-09 in for renamed metrics).

**D2 — Snapshot-count convention: bare plural, no suffix (MET-01).** Point-in-time inventory counts drop `_total` and take no replacement suffix (`meraki_org_devices`, `meraki_ms_ports_active`). Prometheus naming guidance reserves `_total` for counters and does not require a suffix on gauges; a bare noun reads naturally with `sum()`/`count()` and avoids inventing a third suffix. (`total`/`sent`/`recv` as an *infix* discriminator — `usage_total_bytes` — is fine; only the *suffix* is reserved.)

**D3 — Energy: joules, and `power`→`energy` in the name (MET-04).** `watthours` is a non-base unit AND the current names say "power" for what is energy. Rename `meraki_ms_poe_*_power_watthours` → `meraki_ms_poe_*_energy_joules`, value ×3600. Base-unit purity is the whole point of this one-shot pre-1.0 break; doing watthours→joules later would be a second break.

**D4 — Percent suffix: `_percent`, values 0–100 (MET-05).** 10 existing names already use `_percent` vs 3 `_percentage` — rename the 3. All three sources are already 0–100; **no value change**.

**D5 — Memory KiB ×1024 stays; all data-volume/network conversions standardize on ×1000 (APIDEV-03).** Device memory (`devices/base.py` ×1024) is genuinely binary (KiB) — keep, and say "KiB×1024" in HELP. Switch-port `usageInKb` in `devices/ms.py` currently uses ×1024 while `trafficInKbps` in the *same functions* uses ×1000/8; Meraki dashboard data-volume KB is decimal — change the three `usage_counters`/`usage_*_kb` site groups to **×1000**.

**D6 — Link-speed Mbps: KEEP `_mbps` names/values.** `meraki_mr_port_link_negotiation_speed_mbps` / `meraki_mr_aggregation_speed_mbps` are *nominal* link capacities (evidence flags them ⚠). Link rates are universally quoted in Mbps, the values are exact small integers (100/1000/2500), and no rate() math is ever done on them. Converting buys purity at real usability cost. Documented exception, like `_mhz`/`_dbm`.

**D7 — `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes` is a rate, not a volume** (found during verification; evidence: "=bytes/SEC rate!"). ms.py converts `kbps ×1000/8` → the value is bytes/second but the name says bytes. In-scope: rename → `meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes_per_second`, multiplier 1 (already converted).

## 2. THE COMPLETE RENAME TABLE

Multiplier = factor applied at the emit site relative to today's emitted value. StrEnum means collectors reference enum members, so **the string change lives entirely in `metrics_constants.py`**; lane work = HELP text, value conversion, comments, tests. Enum member *identifiers* should be renamed alongside their strings (e.g. `ORG_USAGE_TOTAL_KB`→`ORG_USAGE_TOTAL_BYTES`) so grep never lies again.

### 2a. MET-01 — snapshot gauges, drop `_total` (21 metrics, multiplier 1, HELP: reword "Total number of" → "Number of")

## 3. Verified NOT changing (checked-OK)

- All `_info` metrics; `meraki_device_up`; `meraki_device_memory_*_bytes` names; `meraki_mx_uplink_{sent,recv}_bytes` (genuinely bytes); `meraki_ms_power_usage_watts`, `meraki_ms_poe_budget_watts` (instantaneous power → watts correct); all MT domain units (`_celsius/_volts/_amps/_watts/_va/_hz/_ppm/_ppb/_ug_m3/_db/_dbm`, scores); `meraki_mt_gateway_last_connected_timestamp_seconds`; channel-utilization `_percent` family; `meraki_mx_security_events_count`, `meraki_mt_alerting_sensors_count`, `meraki_ms_port_error_active/_warning_active` (F-091 conformant); `_count` snapshot names (`ms_port_client_count`, `mr_ssid_client_count`, `clients_per_ssid/vlan_count`, `wireless_client_capabilities_count`, `login_security_different_passwords_count`); `meraki_alerts_active`; `meraki_org_licenses_expiring`; `meraki_org_api_requests_by_status` (windowed but no bad suffix — HELP window via MET-09/#536); `meraki_mr_radio_channel_width_mhz`; `meraki_mr_*_speed_mbps` (D6); `meraki_mr_cpu_load_5min`; all `meraki_exporter_*` self-metrics (#532/#539 own those); webhook + DNS/client-store counters (true Counters); `meraki_ms_port_packets_rate_{broadcast,…}` members other than `_rate_total`; `meraki_network_filter_match/_resolved`.
- **Dead enums — do NOT rename; they're #538 deletions** (grep-confirmed zero non-constants references): `ORG_LOGIN_SECURITY_ENABLED`, `ORG_LOGIN_SECURITY_IP_RE<net-name-6>ICTIONS_ENABLED`, `NETWORK_CLIENTS_TOTAL`, `NETWORK_TRAFFIC_BYTES`, `NETWORK_DEVICE_<net-name-4>TUS`, `ORGANIZATION_HEALTH_ALERTS_TOTAL`, `HEALTH_ALERT_INFO`.
- **Hardcoded literals:** all 15 `"meraki_*"` literals outside the constants file are exporter self-metrics (DNS, client-store, cardinality, total_series) or `meraki_device_up` — none match a renamed string; no literal fix-ups needed.

## 4. Implementation plan — lanes & routing

- **Wave 0 — seam (one Fable/high lane):** `metrics_constants.py` full table (strings + member identifiers), publish frozen old→new member map to all lanes. Owns `tests/unit/test_metrics_constants.py`.
- **Lane A (Sonnet/medium):** `collectors/organization.py`, `collectors/config.py` + `tests/unit/test_organization_collector.py` + config tests. HELP rewrites; ×1000/×1e6/×60/×86400 conversions.
- **Lane B (Sonnet/HIGH — biggest value-conversion risk):** `collectors/devices/ms.py`, `ms_stack.py`, `ms_power.py` + `tests/unit/collectors/test_ms_collector.py`. Joules ×3600, usage ×1024→×1000, traffic rename (NO value change), packets `_count` family, HELP windows.
- **Lane C (Sonnet/medium):** `collectors/devices/mr/*` + `test_mr_collector.py`. Packet `_count` families, SSID usage ×1e6, percent.
- **Lane D (Sonnet/medium):** `collectors/devices/mx_vpn.py`, `mx_uplink_health.py`, `mx_firewall.py` + mx tests. ÷1000 latencies, ×1000 vpn kb.
- **Lane E (Sonnet/medium):** `collectors/network_health.py` + `network_health_collectors/*` + `test_network_health_collector.py`, `test_latency_stats_collector.py`. F-065 ×1000 (bytes, NOT bits!), latency ÷1000, air-marshal/bluetooth/connection-stats counts.
- **Lane F (Sonnet/medium):** `collectors/alerts.py`, `collectors/mt_sensor.py`, `collectors/clients.py`, `services/inventory.py`, `collectors/devices/base.py` (HELP-only) + their tests incl. `tests/helpers/factories.py` if it references names.
- **Wiring pass (orchestrator):** `make check` green; `make docgen` (commit regenerated `docs/metrics/metrics.md` — never hand-edit); repo-wide grep for every OLD string (incl. README, docs/, charts/, tools/apidrift) → zero survivors outside `dashboards/` and `evidence/` (both untouched by design).

One file = one owner; tests live with their code's lane. Subagents never commit / never run gh.

## 5. Windows to verify at implementation time
`configuration_changes`, `devices_availability_changes`, `ssid_failed_connections`, `sensor_alerts` — HELP must state the actual `timespan` used at the fetch site; not confirmed by the design pass.

## 6. Risks / gotchas

1. **F-065 direction:** download/upload values are kiloBYTES/s (live-verified in evidence) — multiplier ×1000 to bytes/s, NOT ×1000/8. An implementer "fixing" it as kilobits would be 8× off; Lane E must cite F-065.
2. **`meraki_ms_port_traffic_bytes*` needs NO value change** — already bytes/s at emit; only the name was wrong (D7). Do not add ÷8 or ×1000.
3. **Tests assert raw values** in test_ms/mx_vpn/mx_uplink/organization/latency_stats/network_health/clients/device tests + `tests/helpers/factories.py` — update expected values to converted units; never loosen assertions.
4. **No web-UI/status exposure:** templates and `services/status.py` reference no renamed names (grep-verified); cardinality pages read live registry — no UI lane needed.
5. **`meraki_network_filter_networks` (was `_filter_total`) lives in `services/inventory.py`**, not a collector — easy to miss; Lane F owns it.
6. `meraki_org_api_requests_count` dissolves the #539 collision with `meraki_exporter_api_requests_total` as a side effect — note on #539.
7. **Discrepancies vs issue/evidence:** MET-02's list omitted suffix-free windowed family members (`_lost`, `_broadcast`, …) — this spec renames them too for family uniformity (D1). `ms_power.py`/`ms_stack.py` own metrics evidence attributed to `ms.py`. Everything else matched the code.
8. Dashboards will show no-data after deploy — expected, frozen, do not touch (fatal rule).

### Notes / risks
Only reachable when the clients collector is enabled (off by default). Smaller batches mean more requests — keep the batch as large as is safe under the URL limit to protect the rate budget.
Source: v1-readiness findings APIORG-15.

- [ ] Change implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] Behaviour covered by tests; `make check` green
- [ ] Docs/config docs regenerated if user-facing (`make docgen`)
- [ ] No single request encodes more than ~200 client IDs
- [ ] Multi-batch case is covered by a test

body:
**Area:** `core` · **Type:** `ops` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `M` · **Milestone:** M12 — V1 readiness: correctness & health-signal integrity

### Problem / impact
Total API failure is reported as SUCCESS. **Live-confirmed with a fake API key:** coordinators swallow all child failures (`collectors/device.py:364-365`, `collectors/organization.py:308-309`, plus the network_health / config coordinators and `collectors/devices/mt.py:169-170` bare `try/except` + `continue_on_error=True` org fetches), so `collect()` records success even when every underlying API call failed. Result: `/ready` stays 200, `/health` stays 200 forever, the success timestamp keeps advancing, `failure_streak` stays 0, and `/status` shows 100%. Operators get a green exporter that is silently emitting nothing — the single worst health-signal-integrity bug for v1. Related: under total auth failure `/health` stays 200 for ~45min (liveness = 3×slow tier) while `/ready` is correct (CFG-14); `/status` should also surface `authenticated=false`.

### Meraki API
N/A (affects all fetchers; reproduce with a deliberately invalid `MERAKI_EXPORTER_MERAKI__API_KEY`).

### Files to touch
- `collectors/device.py:364-365` (coordinator swallow)
- `collectors/organization.py:308-309` (coordinator swallow + `continue_on_error=True` org fetches)
- network_health + config coordinators (same swallow pattern)
- `collectors/devices/mt.py:169-170` (bare try/except + continue)
- `core/collector.py` / manager: where per-collector success + success_timestamp + failure_streak are recorded
- `/status` payload (surface `authenticated`)

### Notes / risks
Minimum viable fix: a coordinator that collected zero successful updates AND saw errors must record a FAILURE (re-raise on org-fetch failure or on all-org-task failure), OR the manager treats `0 updates + errors > 0` as failure; gate readiness on API 200s. Depends on RES-02 (issue #510) to distinguish all-orgs-failed from partial success cleanly. Regression test (from RES lane): a fake-key run must yield `/ready` 503 and `failure_streak > 0`.
Source: v1-readiness findings RES-01, CFG-14.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] Behaviour covered by tests; `make check` green
- [ ] Docs/config docs regenerated if user-facing (`make docgen`)
- [ ] Fake-API-key run yields `/ready` 503 and `failure_streak > 0` (regression test asserts this)
- [ ] Success timestamp does NOT advance on a cycle where all API calls failed
- [ ] `/status` reports `authenticated=false` under total auth failure

# SPEC #509 — Treat "collected nothing" as a collection failure (P0, area:core) — FROZEN SEAM for Phase 2 core-resilience lane

## 1. TL;DR

Every fan-out coordinator (`DeviceCollector`, `OrganizationCollector`, `NetworkHealthCollector`, `ConfigCollector`, `MTSensorCollector`→`MTCollector`, plus validated additions `AlertsCollector` and `MTSensorAlertsCollector`) currently swallows total API failure (blanket `try/except Exception: logger.exception` in `_collect_impl` + `continue_on_error=True` org fetches), so `MetricCollector.collect()` records success, the manager resets `failure_streak`, advances `last_success_time`, and `/ready`+`/health` stay 200 forever on a revoked key (LIVE-CONFIRMED, `evidence/resilience-failure-modes.md` RES-01). The fix: **a collector's failure signal IS an exception raised out of `_collect_impl()`** — no new manager bookkeeping. Coordinators remove the blanket swallows, per-org workers propagate their failures into `ManagedTaskGroup` (whose new `failed_count`/`succeeded_count` properties are the #510 seam), and each coordinator raises a new `NothingCollectedError` when orgs were present but **zero org-scope units succeeded** (all failed, or all skipped for backoff — the backoff checks move from workers into the coordinator loop so all-in-backoff cycles can't masquerade as success). Additionally: readiness gains a defense-in-depth gate on ≥1 HTTP-200 API request, and `/status` surfaces `authenticated: true/false/null` from a new auth-state latch recorded in `inventory._make_api_call`. No new metric names, labels, or config keys — the existing `collector_health` dict (`manager.py:743-758`), `meraki_exporter_collector_success_timestamp_seconds` (`collector.py:178-182`), and `meraki_exporter_collector_failure_streak` (`manager.py:755-758`) become honest once exceptions propagate.

## 2. FROZEN SEAM ADDITIONS (verbatim — #510/#511/#528/#547 code against these)

### 2a. `core/error_handling.py` — new exception (insert after `RetryableAPIError`, i.e. after line 117)

```python
class NothingCollectedError(CollectorError):
    """A collection cycle produced zero successful organization-scope updates.

    Raised by coordinator collectors when organizations were present but every
    attempted unit of work failed (or every org was skipped for backoff), so the
    manager records the cycle as a FAILURE instead of a spurious success
    (#509 / RES-01). The failure seam contract: a collector signals failure by
    raising out of ``_collect_impl()``; success/failure accounting lives ONLY in
    ``collectors/manager.py`` (collector_health) and ``core/collector.py``
    (success timestamp / error counter).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        collector: str,
        *,
        attempted: int,
        failed: int,
        skipped_backoff: int = 0,
        context: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            f"{collector} collected nothing this cycle: "
            f"attempted={attempted} failed={failed} skipped_backoff={skipped_backoff}",
            ErrorCategory.API_CLIENT_ERROR,
            context,
        )
        self.attempted = attempted
        self.failed = failed
        self.skipped_backoff = skipped_backoff
```

### 2b. `core/async_utils.py` — `ManagedTaskGroup` failure accounting (the #510 seam)

In `__init__` (after `self._total_completed = 0`, line 119):
```python
        self._cancelled_count = 0
```
In `_on_complete` (`create_task`'s done-callback, lines 261-273) — add cancelled tracking:
```python
        def _on_complete(t: Task[T]) -> None:
            self.tasks.discard(t)
            self._total_completed += 1
            if t.cancelled():
                self._cancelled_count += 1
                return
            exc = t.exception()
            if exc is not None and not isinstance(exc, asyncio.CancelledError):
                self._task_exceptions.append(exc)
```
New properties (insert after `create_task`/`_run_with_semaphore`, before `gather`):
```python
    @property
    def failed_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of tasks that completed with an exception (cancellations excluded)."""
        return len(self._task_exceptions)

    @property
    def succeeded_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of tasks that completed without raising (cancellations excluded)."""
        return self._total_completed - self._cancelled_count - len(self._task_exceptions)
```
**Contract for #510:** these counters are valid immediately after `async with` exits (`__aexit__` awaits all tasks and does `await asyncio.sleep(0)` at line 174 so done-callbacks have run). `__aexit__`'s default behavior (log-only, never re-raise child exceptions — lines 178-184) **must stay the default**: #509 coordinators decide failure themselves from the counters because they need backoff-skip awareness the group cannot have. #510 may add opt-in propagation (e.g. a `raise_on_all_failed=False` ctor flag) ON TOP of these counters, but must not change the default and must not rename/repurpose `failed_count`/`succeeded_count`/`_task_exceptions`.

### 2c. The FROZEN coordinator failure rule (identical in device.py / organization.py / network_health.py / mt_alerts.py)

Backoff check moves OUT of workers INTO the coordinator's task-creation loop (checked **before** constructing the worker coroutine, to avoid never-awaited-coroutine warnings):
```python
        skipped_backoff = 0
        async with ManagedTaskGroup(name=..., max_concurrency=...) as group:
            for org in organizations:
                if self.org_health_tracker is not None and not self.org_health_tracker.should_collect(org_id):
                    skipped_backoff += 1
                    logger.debug("Skipping <domain> collection for organization in backoff", org_id=..., org_name=...)
                    continue
                await group.create_task(<worker coro>, name=f"org_{org_id}")
                organizations_processed += 1

        attempted = len(organizations) - skipped_backoff
        if organizations and group.succeeded_count == 0 and (group.failed_count > 0 or attempted == 0):
            raise NothingCollectedError(
                self.__class__.__name__,
                attempted=attempted,
                failed=group.failed_count,
                skipped_backoff=skipped_backoff,
            )
```
Semantics (frozen): empty org list with no error = legitimate no-op = SUCCESS. Org-fetch failure = raises out of `_collect_impl` (no blanket except). Partial org success = SUCCESS (child failures logged by the group + tracked per-org). All orgs failed OR all orgs in backoff = FAILURE. Org-scope worker verdict: an org SUCCEEDS if its primary fetch produced data (or genuinely empty data); it FAILS (raises) if it produced zero data with ≥1 error.

### 2d. `api/client.py` — `AsyncMerakiClient` auth latch + 200-counter

Class attrs (after `_api_retry_attempts: Counter | None = None`, line 46):
```python

    # response yet), True after any HTTP 200, False after any HTTP 401 (#509).
    _auth_ok: bool | None = None
```
New methods (after `get_total_api_requests`, line 209):
```python
    @classmethod
    def record_auth_outcome(cls, ok: bool) -> None:
        """Record the auth outcome of an API response (200 → True, 401 → False)."""
        cls._auth_ok = ok

    @classmethod
    def get_auth_ok(cls) -> bool | None:
        """Last observed authentication state (None until a 200 or 401 is seen)."""
        return cls._auth_ok

    @classmethod
    def reset_auth_state(cls) -> None:
        """Reset recorded auth state (test isolation helper)."""
        cls._auth_ok = None

    def get_successful_api_requests(self) -> int:
        """Total Meraki API requests that returned HTTP 200 (readiness gate, #509)."""
        counter = type(self)._api_requests_total
        if counter is None:
            return 0
        total = 0.0
        for metric in counter.collect():
            for sample in metric.samples:
                if sample.name.endswith("_created"):
                    continue
                if sample.labels.get(LabelName.<net-name-4>TUS_CODE.value) == "200":
                    total += sample.value
        return int(total)
```

### 2e. `collectors/manager.py` — readiness API-200 gate (manager is a seam file; only these changes)

Replace `is_ready` (lines 396-403) and `get_readiness_status` (lines 405-421):

        """Whether FAST+MEDIUM tiers completed their first collection AND at
        least one Meraki API request has returned HTTP 200 (#509 hardening).

        """

            self._tier_initial_complete["fast"]
            and self._tier_initial_complete["medium"]
            and self._has_api_success()
        )

    def _has_api_success(self) -> bool:

**NO other manager/collector.py changes.** Frozen seam statement for #510/#511/#528/#547: per-collector `success`/`success_timestamp`/`failure_streak` are recorded ONLY in `_run_collector_with_timeout`'s `finally` block (`manager.py:743-758`) and `MetricCollector.collect()`'s success/error paths (`collector.py:146-233`). Assert: `collector_health["StubCollector"]["failure_streak"] == 2`, `total_failures == 2`, `total_successes == 0`, `last_success_time is None`, `manager._tier_initial_complete["fast"] is False`, `manager.is_ready is False`, and the `meraki_exporter_collector_success_timestamp_seconds` series for the stub is ABSENT from the registry (success timestamp did not advance). Then swap to a succeeding `_collect_impl`, run once → `failure_streak == 0`, tier complete.
- Per-coordinator total-failure tests (each in its collector's existing test module, `BaseCollectorTest` style; base settings are multi-org so `getOrganizations` errors RAISE through inventory):

## 5. Lane decomposition & implementer routing

Wave 0 (must land first — everything else imports it):
- **Lane 0 — seam**: `core/error_handling.py`, `core/async_utils.py`, `api/client.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, + their tests (`test_managed_task_group.py`, `test_error_handling.py`, `test_api_client.py`). Routing: **sonnet/high** (mechanical once frozen, but done-callback semantics need care).

Wave 1 (parallel, disjoint files, all depend only on Lane 0):
- **Lane 1**: `collectors/device.py` + `tests/unit/test_device_collector.py`. **sonnet/high** (the `except CollectorError: raise` restructure inside a 260-line worker needs judgement).
- **Lane 2**: `collectors/organization.py` + `tests/unit/test_organization_collector.py`. **sonnet/high** (F-040/F-172 semantics must be preserved exactly; signature change).
- **Lane 3**: `collectors/network_health.py` + `tests/unit/test_network_health_collector.py`. **sonnet/medium**.
- **Lane 4**: `collectors/config.py` + `tests/unit/test_config_collector.py` (+ touch `test_config_admins_collector.py` if error-path tests break). **sonnet/medium**.
- **Lane 5**: `collectors/devices/mt.py` + `collectors/mt_sensor.py` + `tests/unit/test_mt_collector.py` (+ `test_mt_gateway_connections.py` if needed). **sonnet/medium**.
- **Lane 6**: `collectors/alerts.py` + `collectors/mt_alerts.py` + `tests/unit/test_alerts_collector.py` + `tests/unit/test_mt_alerts_collector.py`. **sonnet/medium**.
- **Lane 7**: `collectors/manager.py` + `services/inventory.py` + `services/status.py` + `templates/status.html` + `tests/unit/test_readiness_endpoint.py` + `tests/unit/test_status_service.py` + `tests/test_inventory_service.py` + new `tests/unit/test_manager_failure_accounting.py`. **sonnet/high** (manager is a funnelled seam file; MagicMock pitfalls documented above).

Wiring pass (orchestrator, opus): CLAUDE.md doc updates (4 files listed in §3), integration-test triage (`tests/integration/test_collection_cycle.py`, `test_collector_manager_integration.py` may need error-path updates), full `make check` gate. Subagents never commit, never run `gh`.

## 6. Validation flags (issue-body corrections)

1. **Line drift**: issue's `device.py ~364-365` → actual swallow at `device.py:349-350`; `organization.py ~308-309` → actual `organization.py:316-317`; `mt.py ~169-170` correct.
2. **"core/collector.py / manager (success + success_timestamp + failure_streak)" needs NO code change** beyond the manager readiness gate: validated that `MetricCollector.collect()` (collector.py:146-233) and `_run_collector_with_timeout` (manager.py:743-758) already do the right accounting the moment `_collect_impl` raises. The seam is definitional, not a bug site.
3. **Evidence drift — MTSensorAlertsCollector does NOT propagate today**: `evidence/resilience-failure-modes.md` (RES-01) says its exceptions propagate, but current `mt_alerts.py:74-77` decorates `_collect_impl` with `continue_on_error=True`, which swallows everything. Fixed in Lane 6. `ClientsCollector` DOES propagate (verified: `clients.py:309` → inventory raise, no blanket except) — no changes there.
4. **AlertsCollector is a required scope addition** not in the issue's file list: its blanket swallow (`alerts.py:274-275`) would otherwise mark the MEDIUM tier complete and keep advancing `last_success_time` under a fake key, permanently defeating the `/health` dead-man even after the listed files are fixed.
5. **All-orgs-in-backoff must count as failure** (not in the issue text): without it, once `OrgHealthTracker` backs off every org (~5 MEDIUM cycles under a revoked key), skip-cycles would register as successes and re-poison `failure_streak`/`last_success_time`. Handled by moving backoff checks into coordinator loops + the `attempted == 0` arm of the frozen rule.
6. **CFG-14 (/health stays 200 ~45 min under total auth failure)**: out of scope — that's the liveness threshold gap, owned by #596. After #509 the dead-man WILL trip at the threshold because `last_success_time` stops advancing.
7. **The fake-key AC is encoded as unit/endpoint tests** (no live API in CI per tests/CLAUDE.md fatal rules); a manual fake-key live run re-verifying `/ready` 503 + `failure_streak>0` + `authenticated:false` is recommended at the wiring checkpoint (harness transcript in evidence shows the exact procedure).

**#510 interaction (explicit):** #509 implements and freezes `ManagedTaskGroup.failed_count`/`succeeded_count`/`_cancelled_count` (2b) — this IS the child-failure-visibility half of #510. The remaining #510 scope (opt-in propagation, e.g. `raise_on_all_failed`) layers on top without changing default `__aexit__` behavior; #509's coordinators intentionally do NOT use auto-raise because the all-failed decision requires backoff-skip context (`attempted == 0` arm) that only the coordinator has. #511 keeps `_track_error` hooks for the residual deep swallows (`mt.py:406-410` gateway connections, config partial failures); #528 removes the still-dead app.py:449-471 kill switch; #547 hooks `OrgHealthTracker` writes into the per-org worker verdicts this spec creates in device.py/network_health.py.

Landed in 61c4bb1 (fix(core): honest health signals). Fable/high design spec posted above; implemented across 8 disjoint lanes (seam + 7 coordinator/manager lanes) per that spec. Full `make check` green (1572 passed) + ruff format clean. Frozen the ManagedTaskGroup failed_count/succeeded_count seam that #510/#511/#528/#547 build on.

**Area:** `dx` · **Type:** `ops` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M12 — V1 readiness: correctness & health-signal integrity

### Problem / impact
CI is **red on `main` right now**. The apidrift conformance check exits 3 because `DevicePowerModuleStatus.network` is typed as the `PowerModuleNetworkRef` submodel (`core/domain_models.py:651`, commit 10c9d87) while the OpenAPI spec declares that field as a bare `object`. apidrift flags submodel-vs-bare-`object` as a WARNING → exit 3, failing the last ~5 pushes and blocking the pending 0.32.0 release PR. **Live-API verification (org <maintainer-org-id>):** the power-modules `network` field is a structured object `{"id": ...}`, so `PowerModuleNetworkRef` is the CORRECT model and the spec is merely untyped. The fix is to demote submodel-vs-bare-`object` to INFO in the conformance checker — NOT to loosen the model to `dict`, and NOT to paper over it with `|| true`.

### Meraki API
N/A (apidrift tooling; the underlying endpoint is `getOrganizationDevicesPowerModulesStatusesByDevice`).

### Files to touch
- `tools/apidrift/.../conformance.py` — demote a strictly-narrower submodel typed against a spec bare `object` from WARNING to INFO so it no longer drives a non-zero exit.
- Leave `core/domain_models.py:651` (`PowerModuleNetworkRef`) as-is (live-verified correct).

### Notes / risks
Do NOT loosen the domain model to `dict`; the structured model is right. Do NOT mask with `|| true`. Confirm the conformance severity/exit-code mapping so only genuine drift keeps failing CI.
Source: v1-readiness findings TCI-01.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] Behaviour covered by tests; `make check` green
- [ ] Docs/config docs regenerated if user-facing (`make docgen`)
- [ ] apidrift conformance run exits 0 on current `main` (`PowerModuleNetworkRef` unchanged)
- [ ] Genuine spec drift (missing/renamed fields) still produces a non-zero exit
- [ ] The 0.32.0 release PR checks go green

body:
The shared `OrgHealthTracker` (per-org exponential backoff for graceful degradation) was consulted only by `OrganizationCollector`. `DeviceCollector`, `NetworkHealthCollector`, `ClientsCollector`, `AlertsCollector`, and `MTSensorAlertsCollector` fanned out per-org every cycle with no gating, so a persistently-failing/backed-off org still got full-rate collection from every non-Organization collector.

Fix: pass the shared tracker to those five collectors (manager wiring) and skip an org's per-org collection when `should_collect(org_id)` is False. The five are gating consumers only — `OrganizationCollector` remains the sole owner of `record_success`/`record_failure`. Behaviour is unchanged when the tracker is None.

body: Reverse-DNS `gethostbyaddr` ran on the loop's default ThreadPoolExecutor — the same pool `asyncio.to_thread` uses for Meraki API calls. The finding suspected `meraki_client_application_usage_*_kb` might be mislabeled (spec text for `/networks/{id}/clients/applicationUsage` says "bytes"). Validated against the live API instead of static analysis:

- For each client, compared `sum(applicationUsage sent+received)` to that client's `getNetworkClients` total usage. The ratio clusters at **~0.90–0.95** for high-usage clients (e.g. 0.953, 0.952, 0.938) — **not ~1000×**. No code change. Closing as not planned.

_Adjacent check while live: MS250 switch port throughput is also correct — `ms.py` converts `trafficInKbps × 1000/8 → bytes/sec` and `usageInKb × 1024 → bytes`; the busiest port on a core switch reads ~3.1 Mbit/s hourly average (megabit range, as expected). Any "kilobits" appearance on dashboards is a panel unit-formatting issue → dashboard rebuild task._

In `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` the `edge` job (`needs: release-please`, `if: needs.release-please.outputs.release_created != 'true'`) had no status function in its `if:`, so an implicit `success()` was ANDed on. If the release-please job fails — e.g. an expired `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` PAT makes `googleapis/release-please-action` 401 — the edge job is SKIPPED entirely, silently freezing `:main` edge image + edge Helm chart publishing on every ordinary push to main. (This repo's edge/docker-release jobs are bespoke composition around the local `publish.yml`; the central `rknightion/.github` release-please reusable has no edge job, so the fix is necessarily local.)

**Fix:** changed the edge `if:` to `${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-please.outputs.release_created != 'true' }}`. A failed release-please job yields an empty `release_created` output (`!= 'true'`), so edge still runs; a real release (`== 'true'`) still routes to docker-release instead; a cancelled run skips both. The RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN wiring is untouched. actionlint clean.

**Acceptance:** edge :main publishing continues on non-release pushes even when the release-please job fails; a real release still skips edge.

Source: bug-bash finding F-137 (validated).

`tests/CLAUDE.md`'s BASE TEST PATTERN example injects `Exception("Rate limit exceeded")` via `with_error()`. `with_error_handling`'s retry knobs (max_retries=3, base_delay=10.0) are decorator params, not settings-driven — `fast_test_settings` does NOT disable them. **Fix:** changed the doc example message to `"Connection error"` and added a Caution paragraph explaining the trap and the safe way to test the rate-limit/retry path deliberately (int status code + patched `asyncio.sleep`).

`RFHealthCollector._fetch_channel_utilization` (`collectors/network_health_collectors/rf_health.py`) passed only `total_pages="all"`. SDK 3.3.0 defaults for `getNetworkNetworkHealthChannelUtilization` are timespan=1 day, resolution=600 (only valid value), perPage=10 (range 3-100), so each network paged `ceil(APs/10)` requests and transferred up to a day of buckets to use one. Buckets were read via `ap_data["wifi0"][0]` with no sort. Separately, `base_labels` was assigned only inside the `wifi0` block but read in the `wifi1` block, so an AP reporting only wifi1 (5GHz) raised `UnboundLocalError` and silently dropped its 5GHz metric.

**Fix:** pass `timespan=600, resolution=600, perPage=100, total_pages="all"`; sort each radio's buckets by end timestamp (`endTime`→`endTs`) descending and pick the newest; build `device_data`/`base_labels` once per AP before both radio blocks.

**Acceptance:** fetch called with the pinned params; a wifi1-only AP emits 5GHz metrics without crashing; out-of-order buckets pick the newest reading. Regressions: `test_channel_utilization_fetch_pins_query_params`, `test_channel_utilization_wifi1_only_does_not_crash`, `test_channel_utilization_picks_latest_bucket`. (Note: open issue #271's org-wide endpoint migration would obsolete this call — this is the tactical fix.)

body:
**Mechanism:** F-040 (#381) made `OrganizationCollector._run_org_sub_collections` record failures to `OrgHealthTracker`, but that only observes the 6 sub-collections implemented directly in `organization.py`. The 5 separate sub-collectors — `api_usage`, `firmware`, `device_availability_history`, `license`, `client_overview` (in `organization_collectors/*.py`) — swallow their own exceptions via their own `with_error_handling(continue_on_error=True)`, so a failure isolated to one of them never surfaces to `OrgHealthTracker` and cannot engage backoff/export-suppression.

**Files:** `collectors/organization.py`, `collectors/organization_collectors/{api_usage,firmware,device_availability_history,license,client_overview}.py`

**Acceptance criteria:** each of the 5 sub-collectors exposes a success/failure signal (return value or raised sentinel) that `_run_org_sub_collections` records; a failure isolated to one sub-collector is counted by `OrgHealthTracker`.

Source: bug-bash follow-up surfaced while fixing F-040 (validated).

comments.body:
Fixed in 960e336. The 5 separate org sub-collectors now return a bool success/failure signal that `_run_org_sub_collections` records, so a failure isolated to one of them reaches OrgHealthTracker; a 404 (not-available) is not counted as failure.

Full gate green (`make check`: 1295 passed, 1 skipped). Fixed with strict TDD; no dashboards touched.

## Mechanism (validated)

In `services/inventory.py`, `_filter_match_gauge = Gauge("meraki_network_filter_match", ...)` is built from a raw string literal (fatal-rule violation — should be a `CollectorMetricName`/enum). `_emit_filter_metrics` sets `.labels(org_id, network_id).set(value)` only for network IDs present in the current refresh; there is no `.remove(...)` anywhere in the file, so a network once seen is never cleared. The `_cache_size` gauge (keyed org_id/cache_type, set at multiple sites) has the same leak for orgs/networks that disappear. Both gauge families leak stale series indefinitely post-deletion until process restart.

## Why parked

`OrganizationInventory` is a service (not a `MetricCollector`), so it has no `_set_metric`/expiration-manager wiring — fixing the leak needs a new per-refresh removal path (track previously-emitted (org_id, network_id) / cache keys and `.remove()` the ones absent this cycle). That's a small but real data-model addition to the inventory service, and it interacts with the enum/name questions in F-080 (same file). Best done together with F-080 in the observability lane. `meraki_network_filter_match` is referenced in docs/scaling-guide.md + docs/metrics.md (no dashboards).

## Acceptance criteria

- `_filter_match_gauge` uses an enum name, not a raw literal.
- filter_match and cache_size series for deleted networks/orgs are removed on the next refresh (no unbounded stale-series leak).
- `make check` green; docs regenerated.

title: [F-039] Remove frozen collector_success_age_seconds gauge — freezes when runs stop

body:
## Mechanism

`core/collector.py::_initialize_performance_metrics` pre-seeded a hardcoded grid of 6 collectors × 3 tiers = 18 series each for `meraki_exporter_collector_success_timestamp_seconds`, `..._collection_smoothing_window_seconds` and `..._collector_start_offset_seconds`, all `.set(0)`. But each of those collectors runs in exactly one tier (5 MEDIUM, 1 FAST, 1 SLOW), so of the 18 success_timestamp series only 6 ever get a real timestamp; the other 12 stay `0` forever. A `0` timestamp reads as "last success at the epoch" → `time() - 0` is a ~56-year age → those collector/tier pairs look perpetually stale, breaking any staleness alert built on the timestamp gauge. The phantom pairs also describe collector/tier combinations that do not exist.

## Fix

Remove the pre-initialization loop entirely. The real series are created on first successful collection (`collector.py:177` success path) and by `_record_smoothing_metrics` (`collector.py:509/515`) for the actual collector/tier that runs — so only real collector/tier pairs ever exist, and `time() - success_timestamp` works.

## Confirmed file refs

- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/collector.py:718-743` — the removed pre-init loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- After init (before any collection), the three gauges have no child series.
- Real series still appear once a collector runs / records smoothing metrics.
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-025 (validated; primary claim — the merged multi-org clear() sub-issue is handled by F-001).

comments.body: Fixed in 57181fe. Removed the pre-init loop that seeded a 6×3 collector/tier grid of success_timestamp/smoothing_window/start_offset series at 0; the 12 phantom success_timestamp series (wrong collector/tier pairs) no longer read as ~56-year stale. Real series are created on first collection and by _record_smoothing_metrics. New test asserts no phantom series exist after init. `make check` green.

## Mechanism (validated)

`api/client.py` registers `_api_request_duration` (`meraki_exporter_api_duration_seconds`) and `_api_retry_attempts` (`meraki_exporter_api_retry_total`), but both are only observed inside `AsyncMerakiClient._request`. `_request` is dead in production: the sole `AsyncMerakiClient` is constructed once in `app.py:72` and only its `.api` (raw SDK) and `.close()` are used; every collector and `services/inventory.py` call the raw SDK via `asyncio.to_thread`, never `_request`/`get_*`. Commit 86ced18 removed `mt.py`'s own `AsyncMerakiClient` (switched to raw `self.api.sensor.getOrganizationSensorReadingsLatest`), so nothing exercises `_request` anymore. `inventory.py::_make_api_call` increments only `api_requests_total` (no duration histogram). Net effect: `meraki_exporter_api_duration_seconds` and `meraki_exporter_api_retry_total` are registered + dashboarded but sample-less; the wrapper `get_*` methods are exercised only by `tests/test_api_client.py`.

## Why parked (decision needed)

Two viable fixes with different blast radius, needs a deliberate call:

**Option A — wire real instrumentation into the used path.** Add duration observation + retry accounting to `services/inventory.py::_make_api_call` (and/or a shared call wrapper) so the existing metrics populate from the calls that actually run. Populates the dashboard panels. Moderate scope; must pick labels (endpoint/status_code) consistent with the dashboards.

**Option B — remove the dead code + metrics + panels.** Delete `_request` and the test-only `get_*` wrapper methods, drop `_api_request_duration`/`_api_retry_attempts`, and remove/repoint the empty dashboard panels + docs that reference `meraki_exporter_api_duration_seconds` / `meraki_exporter_api_retry_total`. Larger, touches dashboards.

## Affected refs

- `api/client.py` — `_request` (obs sites ~281/315/350/392), metric registration ~91/127.
- `services/inventory.py::_make_api_call` — the real call path (only increments `api_requests_total`).
- Dashboards referencing `meraki_exporter_api_duration_seconds` / `meraki_exporter_api_retry_total`.
- `docs/metrics/*` documenting both series.

## Acceptance criteria

- The two metrics either emit real samples on the used call path (A) or are removed along with their dead code, dashboard panels and docs (B) — no registered-but-empty series left dashboarded.
- `make check` green; dashboards validated if touched.

body:
## Mechanism

`core/otel_tracing.py::_instrument_libraries` calls `RequestsInstrumentor().instrument(..., span_callback=self._requests_span_callback)`. The installed `opentelemetry-instrumentation-requests` (0.64b0) does not accept `span_callback` — its `_instrument` only reads `tracer_provider`, `excluded_urls`, `meter_provider`, `duration_histogram_boundaries`, `request_hook`, `response_hook`. So the kwarg is silently dropped and `_requests_span_callback` (which sets `meraki.request_id`/`retry_after`/`rate_limit.remaining`/`http.response.size`) never runs.

## Fix

Use the supported `response_hook` with the correct signature `(span, request, response)`; rename the callback to `_requests_response_hook(self, span, request, response)` and read the response as before.

## Acceptance criteria

- `RequestsInstrumentor().instrument(..., response_hook=...)` with the correct 3-arg signature.
- Span enrichment attributes are set on the response hook.
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-022 (validated).

body:
## Mechanism

Three `_track_api_call` sites increment `meraki_exporter_collector_api_calls_total` immediately before a cache-served inventory read, so cache hits are counted as upstream API calls (overcounting the exporter's own API-budget telemetry):

- `network_health.py::_fetch_organizations` — before `inventory.get_organizations()`
- `network_health.py::_fetch_networks_for_health` — before `inventory.get_networks(org_id)`
- `network_health_collectors/rf_health.py::_fetch_organization_devices` — before `inventory.get_devices(...)` (cache path)

## Fix

Remove the two network_health tracks (always cache-served). In rf_health, move the `_track_api_call` into the `inventory is None` fallback branch — the only path that makes a real direct API call — so genuine calls are still counted but cache hits are not.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `_track_api_call` on a cache-served read.
- rf_health still counts the real fallback call.
- network-health tests updated to not assert the removed cache-hit tracking.
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-063 (validated).

title: [F-063] Cache hits counted as API calls in _track_api_call call sites

body:
## Mechanism

`@log_api_call(op)` (`core/logging_decorators.py:59-63`) already calls `self._track_api_call(op)` (or `self.parent._track_api_call(op)`) for every decorated method. Many decorated fetchers ALSO call `self._track_api_call(op)` for the same op in their body, so `meraki_exporter_collector_api_calls_total{endpoint=op}` is incremented twice per real call. Two tests even codified the 2x (`test_api_usage_collector.py`, `test_client_overview_collector.py` asserting `== 2`).

Unconditional same-op duplicates removed (14 sites):
`clients.py` (getNetworkClients), `devices/ms_stack.py`, `devices/mx_firewall.py` (L3 + security-events), `devices/mx_vpn.py` (statuses + stats), `organization_collectors/api_usage.py`, `client_overview.py`, `device_availability_history.py`, `firmware.py`, `license.py` (overview + licenses).

Not duplicates (kept): `clients.py::_collect_application_usage` (`if i > 0` guard correctly counts *additional* batched calls); `mx_firewall.py::collect_for_network` L7 track (different op than the L3 decorator). The per-client `clients.py::_collect_wireless_signal_quality` was overcounting by exactly one (decorator counts the first, loop counted every client) — fixed with an `if idx > 0` guard so N clients count N calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- No decorated method manually re-tracks its own decorator op.
- Loop/batch fetchers count exactly one increment per real call (decorator + guarded manual for the rest).
- The two `== 2` tests updated to `== 1`.
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-014 (validated).
