Removed 14 redundant manual `_track_api_call` calls from decorated fetchers; kept the guarded batch tracking (`if i > 0`) and the L7 track (distinct op); fixed the per-client signal-quality loop overcount with an `if idx > 0` guard. The two tests asserting `== 2` now assert `== 1`. `make check` green (1158 passed).

body:
**Area:** `otel` · **Type:** `feature` · **Priority:** `P2` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** M11 — OTEL metrics emission · **Kind:** Epic

> [!NOTE]
> **Queued behind the bug bash (M9/M10).** Do not start implementation until the production-readiness / optimisation bug bash is landed. This epic is design-complete enough to pick up immediately afterwards.

## Goal / what this unlocks

Today the exporter emits **metrics via Prometheus `/metrics` only**. OpenTelemetry is wired for **traces and logs only** (`core/otel_tracing.py`, `core/otel_logging.py`; `docs/observability/otel.md` states this outright). There is no `MeterProvider`, no OTLP metric exporter, no bridge — `core/collector.py::_create_gauge/_create_counter/_create_histogram/_create_info` all instantiate `prometheus_client` objects against the default `REGI<net-name-6>Y`.

This epic adds an **optional OTLP metrics export path** so users who run a push-based pipeline (e.g. straight to Grafana Cloud OTLP, or via a local OpenTelemetry Collector) can get the metrics without scraping `/metrics`. Scraping stays the default and the supported primary path; OTLP metrics export is strictly opt-in.

Historical note: OTLP metrics export was prototyped once before (`feat(otel): add metrics export routing config` e199645, `feat(otel): add metrics filtering system` a67287e, `feat(otel): integrate filtering into app` 84633f0) and then **removed** — current `OTelSettings` is the tracing-only survivor. Treat that prior work as reference, not as something to blindly revert; the routing/filtering ideas are directly relevant (see the two-plane design below).

## Chosen approach: bridge the Prometheus registry (not dual-emit)

We will **bridge the existing `prometheus_client` registry to OTLP**, not re-emit every metric through parallel OTEL instruments.

- **Why:** OTLP metrics is a minority path (most users scrape). Bridging keeps a **single source of truth** — collectors keep calling `_create_gauge/_set_metric` exactly as today, and the bridge reads the registry and pushes. No collector churn, no risk of the two paths drifting metric-by-metric, and metric-expiration / cardinality logic keeps working unchanged.
- **Mechanism:** a `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` fed by an OTEL SDK reader that snapshots `prometheus_client`'s registry each interval and translates families → OTLP data points, or the equivalent community bridge. Spike must confirm the current best mechanism (OTEL Python `prometheus_client` interop has moved; verify against current SDK — do **not** trust training data, check the docs).
- **Non-goal:** rewriting collectors to emit via `meter.create_*` instruments.

## Two telemetry planes — keep them distinct (load-bearing design requirement)

The exporter produces **two conceptually different kinds of telemetry**, and this epic must not blur them. This maps cleanly onto the **two metric prefix families already documented in `core/constants/metrics_constants.py`**:

1. **Self-observability of the exporter itself** — how the *app* is doing. Today: the OTEL **traces** and **logs**. In metrics terms this is the **`meraki_exporter_*`** family (`CollectorMetricName` — collector durations, API call counts, error counts, etc.).
2. **Product-line emissions** — the actual **Meraki data** the exporter exists to surface. The **`meraki_*`** family (device/network/org metrics).

Users will legitimately want these at **different destinations** (e.g. self-obs → internal platform collector; product metrics → Grafana Cloud, or vice versa), or want one but not the other. So the design must:

- Let product-metric OTLP export be **enabled independently** of the existing self-obs traces/logs OTEL config, with its **own endpoint** (do not force product metrics through the single existing `otel.endpoint`).
- Use the **`meraki_` vs `meraki_exporter_` prefix split as the routing key** to classify a series as product vs self. This is exactly what the removed "metrics filtering system" was reaching for — reuse the idea.
- Ideally allow routing self-obs metrics and product metrics to **separate OTLP endpoints** (at minimum: a clean toggle so a user can export product metrics without also shipping self-obs metrics, and vice versa).

Proposed config shape (finalise in the spike — names not frozen):

```
# existing (self-observability: traces + logs) — unchanged
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__ENABLED=true
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__ENDPOINT=...

# new: product-line metrics export (independent opt-in + destination)
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__ENABLED=true
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__ENDPOINT=...        # may differ from the traces/logs endpoint
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__EXPORT_INTERVAL=60
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__INCLUDE=product|self|all   # prefix-based routing
MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__TEMPORALITY=cumulative
```

## Parity gaps to resolve (rolled in from the assessment)

Even though Grafana Cloud stores OTLP as Prometheus, the scrape path and the OTLP-push path are **not byte-identical**. Each of the following must be explicitly addressed (and documented) before the export path is considered "at parity". These are acceptance sub-items of this epic, not separate milestones:

- [ ] **(2) `up` / scrape-health metrics disappear on push.** Scrapers get `up`, `scrape_duration_seconds`, `scrape_samples_scraped` for free; OTLP push has no `up`. Every "target down" alert breaks for OTLP-only users. Decide: synthesise a heartbeat/`up`-equivalent product metric, or clearly document the loss and the alternative (`meraki_exporter_*` liveness). **Highest-impact gap.**
- [ ] **(3) `job` / `instance` identity.** Scrape derives these from Prometheus scrape config; OTLP derives them from resource attributes → `target_info` + Grafana Cloud's mapping. Series identity and dashboard/alert selectors diverge between paths. Define the resource attributes (`service.name`, `service.instance.id`, `deployment.environment`) and document the resulting label mapping so dashboards work on both. Reuse the existing `otel.resource_attributes` + `service_name`.
- [ ] **(4) Metric-name normalization / unit suffixing.** Grafana Cloud's OTLP→Prom conversion appends `_total` to monotonic sums and does unit suffixing (`_bytes`, `_ratio`, dots→underscores). Our names are **already** Prometheus-native (`meraki_*_total`, `_bytes`), so the OTLP path risks **double-suffixing or name drift** vs. the scraped names. Audit every metric name/unit through the bridge and assert scrape-name == push-name (post-GC-normalization). **Second-highest-impact gap.**
- [ ] **(5) Counter temporality.** `prometheus_client` counters are cumulative-since-process-start. OTLP needs an explicit temporality choice; Grafana Cloud expects **cumulative**. Wrong choice silently breaks `rate()`. Set and document temporality (default cumulative).
- [ ] **(6) Metric-expiration semantics.** `core/metric_expiration.py::MetricExpirationManager` deletes stale series from the registry (offline/removed devices). On scrape that yields a clean staleness marker/gap; on OTLP push a deleted series just stops (no staleness marker) and cumulative start-times reset. Verify the bridge handles series-disappearance and counter start-time correctly so offline-device behaviour matches the scrape path (this manager is the whole point of the expiration design — regressions here are silent).
- [ ] **(7) `Info` metrics + `_created` series.** `prometheus_client` `Info` → `_info{}=1` has no native OTEL type (becomes a gauge=1 with attributes); `_created` series behave differently. Minor, but audit for series-count / label differences and document.

## Implementation plan (phased — pick up after bug bash)

**Phase 0 — Spike / verify (do first, do not skip).**
- Confirm the current best registry→OTLP bridge mechanism against the **current** OpenTelemetry Python + `prometheus_client` docs (the interop surface has changed; verify, don't assume).
- Confirm `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` metrics deps and pin (project already allows beta OTEL deps — `3bf880c`).
- Stand up a throwaway pipeline: exporter → local OTel Collector → Prometheus/Mimir, and **diff the resulting series against a direct `/metrics` scrape** of the same run. This diff is the parity oracle for gaps (2)–(7).

**Phase 1 — Config surface + plumbing.**
- Add the `otel.metrics` sub-settings (above) to `core/config_models.py`; wire logging in `core/config_logger.py`; document in `.env.example` and `docs/observability/otel.md`. Endpoint independent of the traces/logs endpoint.
- `model_validator`: metrics export requires its own endpoint when enabled.

**Phase 2 — The bridge.**
- New `core/otel_metrics.py`: `MeterProvider` + `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` + OTLP metric exporter, reading the `prometheus_client` `REGI<net-name-6>Y`.
- Prefix-based routing (`meraki_` = product, `meraki_exporter_` = self) driven by the `INCLUDE` setting.
- Resource attributes shared with the tracing setup (single definition point) so `service.name`/`instance` are consistent across traces, logs, and metrics.
- Wire startup/shutdown into `app.py` lifespan alongside `otel_logging`/tracing; only when `otel.metrics.enabled`.

**Phase 3 — Parity hardening.**
- Work through callouts (2)–(7) using the Phase 0 diff harness as the gate. Each must be either matched or explicitly documented as a known difference.

**Phase 4 — Tests + docs.**
- Unit tests: bridge translates gauge/counter/histogram/info correctly; prefix routing; temporality; naming assertions (scrape-name == push-name post-normalization).
- Integration test extending the existing metric-assertion harness (`tests/CLAUDE.md`).
- Rewrite `docs/observability/otel.md` metrics section (it currently says metrics are *not* exported — update once shipped), and a "scrape vs OTLP: what differs" table capturing (2)–(7).
- `make check` green; `make docgen` if config/metric surface changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OTLP metrics export is **opt-in** and **off by default**; scraping `/metrics` is unchanged and remains the primary path.
- [ ] Product-metric export can be enabled **independently** of the existing self-obs traces/logs OTEL config, with its **own endpoint**.
- [ ] Product (`meraki_*`) vs self-obs (`meraki_exporter_*`) planes are routable separately (prefix-based `INCLUDE`).
- [ ] Registry is the single source of truth — no collector code re-emits via parallel OTEL instruments.
- [ ] Parity callouts (2)–(7) each resolved-or-documented, evidenced by the scrape-vs-push diff harness.
- [ ] `docs/observability/otel.md` updated (no longer claims metrics aren't exported) + scrape-vs-OTLP differences table.
- [ ] Tests added; `make check` green; `make docgen` run if surface changed.

<sub>Epic drafted 2026-07-02 from an OTEL/Prometheus parity assessment. Verify OTEL Python + prometheus_client bridge mechanics against current docs before implementing — the interop surface has changed since training data.</sub>

comments.body: **v1-readiness enrichment:** sequence after the metric naming sweep (#531) so the OTLP bridge only ever emits final v1 names; the single-org contract (#585) simplifies resource attributes. Child: #313; TLS: #314.

**Execution routing (for #618 orchestration):** agent model: `fable` · thinking effort: `high`.

This is a `fable-candidate` issue: the orchestrator spawns a dedicated **Fable, high-effort subagent** whose FIRST deliverable is the design/spec posted ON THIS ISSUE; mechanical implementation may then be delegated to a cheaper agent per that spec (the spec comment states the implementer routing). The orchestrator itself implements nothing.

## 🧭 FROZEN DESIGN SPEC — OTLP metrics bridge (Wave 4D, 2026-07-03)

Produced by the fable/high design-freeze pass, verified against live SDK 1.43. This is the implementation contract for #339 + #313 + #314. Key decision: a **bespoke periodic snapshotter** (no MeterProvider — none exists for the registry→OTLP direction in OTel Python), building `MetricsData` directly for byte-exact metric-name control. All 7 parity gaps resolved as explicit decisions below.

# FROZEN SPEC — OTLP metrics export via Prometheus-registry bridge (epic #339; features #313, #314)

**Design-frozen 2026-07-03.** Verified against installed `opentelemetry-sdk 1.43.0` / `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc 1.43.0` / `prometheus-client 0.25.0` by live introspection, and against current opentelemetry-python readthedocs (via context7). Template precedent: `core/otel_data_logs.py` (#622).

**LOCKED constraint (front and centre):** Prometheus `/metrics` remains the sole, default, supported metrics surface. OTLP metrics export is strictly opt-in / off-by-default, and enabling it must not alter `/metrics` output in any way. The registry stays the single source of truth — no collector re-emits via parallel OTel instruments; `_create_gauge/_create_counter/_create_histogram/_create_info` and `MetricExpirationManager` are untouched.

---

## 1. Config surface — `OTelMetricsSettings` nested under `OTelSettings.metrics`

New `class OTelMetricsSettings(BaseModel)` in `core/config_models.py`, placed beside `OTelLogsSettings` (~line 557) and mirroring its shape exactly. Env prefix: `MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__*`.

| Field | Type | Default | Env var | Description (verbatim intent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool` | `False` | `...METRICS__ENABLED` | Enable the OTLP metrics bridge (push a periodic snapshot of the Prometheus registry via OTLP gRPC). Independent of `otel.enabled` (tracing) and `otel.logs.enabled`. Off by default; `/metrics` scrape is unchanged either way. |
| `endpoint` | `str \| None` | `None` | `...METRICS__ENDPOINT` | OTLP gRPC endpoint for metrics. When None, falls back to `otel.endpoint`. Must resolve (own or inherited) when `metrics.enabled` is True. |
| `insecure` | `bool \| None` | `None` | `...METRICS__INSECURE` | Non-TLS channel toggle. When None, inherits `otel.insecure`. |
| `export_interval_seconds` | `int`, `Field(ge=10, le=3600)` | `60` | `...METRICS__EXPORT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | Seconds between registry snapshots pushed via OTLP. |
| `include` | `Literal["product", "self", "all"]` | `"all"` | `...METRICS__INCLUDE` | Which telemetry plane to push, keyed on the metric-name prefix split: `product` = `meraki_*` excluding `meraki_exporter_*`; `self` = everything else (`meraki_exporter_*` plus the process/python runtime families); `all` = both. |
| `temporality` | `Literal["cumulative"]` | `"cumulative"` | `...METRICS__TEMPORALITY` | Counter/histogram temporality. **v1 accepts only `cumulative`** (Grafana Cloud expects cumulative; `prometheus_client` counters are cumulative-since-start, so this is the only faithful translation). The field exists so `delta` can be added later without an env-var rename; the `Literal` makes any other value a validation error today. |

**`include` default = `"all"` — decision + rationale:** an OTLP-only user (no scraper at all, the target persona of #313) must not silently lose exporter self-observability metrics — they are the gap-(2) mitigation. `"product"` is the documented knob for cost-sensitive users who already collect self-obs elsewhere. The partition is total and two-way: `product` ⇔ `name.startswith("meraki_") and not name.startswith("meraki_exporter_")`; `self` ⇔ everything else in the registry (`meraki_exporter_*`, `process_*`, `python_*`). No family is ever in both or neither.

**#314 cert fields — on the PARENT `OTelSettings`, paths only, shared by all three OTLP channels (traces, data logs, metrics):**

| Field | Type | Default | Env var |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ca_cert_path` | `str \| None` | `None` | `MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__CA_CERT_PATH` |
| `client_cert_path` | `str \| None` | `None` | `MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__CLIENT_CERT_PATH` |
| `client_key_path` | `str \| None` | `None` | `MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__CLIENT_KEY_PATH` |

Decision: **paths-only, no `SecretStr` inline PEM material** — inline certs are the secrets footgun #314 warns about (they end up in env dumps, `/status`, config logging). Paths are how k8s/docker mount certs anyway. Per-channel cert overrides are deliberately out of scope for v1 (one collector endpoint per trust domain is the norm); note as a future extension if someone needs different CAs per channel.

**Validators (extend `OTelSettings.validate_endpoint`, keep one validator):**
- `metrics.enabled and not (metrics.endpoint or endpoint)` → `ValueError("OTEL metrics endpoint must be provided (otel.metrics.endpoint or otel.endpoint) when otel.metrics.enabled is True")` — exact analogue of the logs clause at line 662.
- `client_cert_path` XOR `client_key_path` → `ValueError` (mTLS needs both).
- Any cert field set while the channel that would use it resolves `insecure=True` for **all** enabled channels → `ValueError` ("cert paths configured but every OTLP channel is insecure") — catches the silent-no-op misconfiguration. (Per-channel: certs are simply unused on a channel whose resolved insecure is True.)

**Resolved-value properties on `OTelSettings`, mirroring `logs_endpoint`/`logs_insecure` (lines 669–677):**
```python
@property
def metrics_endpoint(self) -> str | None:
    return self.metrics.endpoint or self.endpoint

@property
def metrics_insecure(self) -> bool:
    return self.insecure if self.metrics.insecure is None else self.metrics.insecure
```

---

## 2. The bridge mechanism (the crux — verified against OTel Python 1.43)

**Verified current-SDK facts (introspected live, confirmed against readthedocs):**
- `opentelemetry.exporter.prometheus.PrometheusMetricReader` goes the **other** direction only (OTel meters → prom registry for scrape). There is **no** official prom-registry→OTLP bridge in OTel Python.
- `MetricReader` / `PeriodicExportingMetricReader` pull exclusively from the `MeterProvider`'s own instrument pipeline (the provider injects the collect callback); there is no supported hook to feed foreign metric families through a reader. A "custom MetricReader" is the wrong tool — you'd be fighting `SdkConfiguration`/`MeasurementConsumer` internals.
- **The clean path exists and is public:** `OTLPMetricExporter.export(metrics_data: MetricsData, timeout_millis=10000) -> MetricExportResult` is a documented public method, and the entire OTLP data model is public dataclasses in `opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export`: `MetricsData(resource_metrics)`, `ResourceMetrics(resource, scope_metrics, schema_url)`, `ScopeMetrics(scope, metrics, schema_url)`, `Metric(name, description, unit, data)`, `Sum(data_points, aggregation_temporality, is_monotonic)`, `Gauge(data_points)`, `Histogram(data_points, aggregation_temporality)`, `NumberDataPoint(attributes, start_time_unix_nano, time_unix_nano, value, exemplars)`, `HistogramDataPoint(attributes, start_time_unix_nano, time_unix_nano, count, sum, bucket_counts, explicit_bounds, min, max, exemplars)`, `AggregationTemporality.CUMULATIVE`. Field names above are the verified 1.43.0 dataclass fields.

**FROZEN DECISION — bespoke periodic snapshotter, no `MeterProvider` at all.** This is an honest deviation from the epic's provisional "MeterProvider + PeriodicExportingMetricReader" wording (which the epic itself said to verify): there is nothing for a MeterProvider to do here — we have no OTel instruments, and constructing `MetricsData` directly gives byte-exact control over metric names (the whole of parity gap 4). Also stronger than the data-log emitter's "private provider, never set global": there is no provider to leak globally.

**Class shape — `core/otel_metrics.py`:**

```python
class OTelMetricsBridge:
    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, *,
                 registry: CollectorRegistry | None = None,   # default: global REGI<net-name-6>Y
                 exporter: MetricExporter | None = None) -> None: ...
        # Cheap no-op when otel.metrics.enabled is False (log + return),
        # exactly like DataLogEmitter.__init__. `exporter` is the TEST SEAM:
        # tests pass a stub MetricExporter capturing MetricsData; production
        # builds OTLPMetricExporter(endpoint=settings.otel.metrics_endpoint,
        # insecure=..., credentials=..., max_export_batch_size=10_000).
        # Setup wrapped in try/except -> log + self-disable, never abort startup.

    async def start(self) -> None: ...   # spawn the asyncio export loop (lifespan startup)
    async def stop(self) -> None: ...    # cancel loop, one final export (flush), exporter.shutdown()

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        # every export_interval_seconds:
        #   metrics_data = await asyncio.to_thread(self._snapshot)   # registry iteration off-loop
        #   result = await asyncio.to_thread(self._exporter.export, metrics_data)  # blocking gRPC off-loop
        #   bump self-obs counters; failures logged + counted, NEVER raise out of the loop

    def _snapshot(self) -> MetricsData: ...
        # registry.collect() -> route families by prefix (include) -> translate_families(...)
        # -> MetricsData(resource_metrics=[ResourceMetrics(resource=build_otel_resource(settings),
        #      scope_metrics=[ScopeMetrics(scope=InstrumentationScope("meraki_dashboard_exporter.otlp_metrics",
        #      get_version()), metrics=[...], schema_url="")], schema_url="")])

# module-level PURE function — the unit-test surface:
def translate_families(families, *, now_unix_nano, fallback_start_unix_nano, include) -> list[Metric]
```

`max_export_batch_size=10_000` on the exporter (verified constructor param) makes the SDK split requests under gRPC's 4 MB cap — large fleets can exceed it in one snapshot.

**Family → OTLP translation table (frozen; `family.type` from `prometheus_client` `Metric` families):**

| prom family type | OTLP `Metric.name` | OTLP data | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `counter` | `f"{family.name}_total"` (== exact scrape sample name) | `Sum(is_monotonic=True, aggregation_temporality=CUMULATIVE)`; one `NumberDataPoint` per `_total` sample | `start_time_unix_nano` = that label-set's `_created` sample ×1e9 when present, else bridge start time. `_created` samples are consumed as start-times and **never exported as their own series**. |
| `gauge` | `family.name` | `Gauge` | `start_time_unix_nano=0` (gauges carry no start time). |
| `histogram` | `family.name` (bare — backends re-render `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count`) | `Histogram(aggregation_temporality=CUMULATIVE)`; one `HistogramDataPoint` per label-set | Prom `le` buckets are **cumulative**; OTLP `bucket_counts` are **per-bucket**: de-cumulate adjacent buckets, `explicit_bounds` = the `le` values excluding `+Inf` (the `+Inf` bucket becomes the final `bucket_counts` entry). `count`/`sum` from `_count`/`_sum`; `min`/`max` = `None`; start-time from `_created`. |
| `info` | `f"{family.name}_info"` (exact scrape name) | `Gauge`, value 1, labels → attributes | No native OTel type; gauge=1 is the standard mapping (gap 7). |
| `unknown`/untyped | `family.name` | `Gauge` | |
| `summary` | **skipped** + one-time debug log | — | 1.43's export model has no Summary dataclass; the codebase registers no `prometheus_client.Summary` (verified). Guard, don't translate. |

**`Metric.unit` is ALWAYS `""` (frozen).** Our names already embed units (`_bytes`, `_seconds`, `_total`); populating `unit` invites backend unit-suffixing → double suffixes (gap 4).

`Metric.description` = the family's `documentation` (HELP parity for backends that surface it). Labels map 1:1 to data-point attributes (values are already strings; `None` already coalesced to `""` upstream by `create_labels`).

---

## 3. Parity gaps (2)–(7) — explicit decisions

**(2) `up` / scrape-health loss — DECIDED: synthesise a heartbeat, do NOT fake `up`.** Pushing a literal `up` series collides with backend scrape-semantics and every convention around it. Instead the bridge registers a self-obs gauge `meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_last_success_timestamp_seconds` (unix ts of last successful export) and **always includes it in every push regardless of `include`** — the single, documented routing exemption, so an `include=product` user still gets liveness. Documented alert recipe in otel.md: `time() - meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_last_success_timestamp_seconds > 3 * interval`, plus `absent(...)` for hard-down. Needs Phase-6 live check: end-to-end alert behaviour on Grafana Cloud (⚠ flag).

**(3) `job`/`instance` identity — DECIDED: reuse `build_otel_resource(settings)`** (`core/otel_tracing.py:41`) verbatim — the single definition point already shared by traces and data logs, so `service.name`/`service.version`/`service.instance.id`/`deployment.environment` are byte-identical across all three channels. Backends map `service.name`→`job`, `service.instance.id`→`instance`, remainder → `target_info`. Document the mapping table in otel.md so dashboard selectors are writable for both paths. Known wrinkle to state in docs: `service.instance.id` falls back to `HOSTNAME` env or `"unknown"` — multiple instances without `HOSTNAME` collide (pre-existing behaviour, not this epic's to change). Phase-6: verify actual `job`/`instance` labels on Grafana Cloud (⚠ flag).

**(4) Name normalization / double-suffix — DECIDED: assert byte-equality at the bridge.** Because we hand-build `Metric.name`, the invariant is enforceable in unit tests: OTLP name == exact scrape family/sample name (counters keep `_total`, unit field empty). Residual risk is entirely backend-side: the OTLP→Prom translator must not append `_total` again to a monotonic Sum already ending in `_total`, and must not unit-suffix with `unit=""`. Current translators check for an existing suffix, but this is exactly the thing training data can't be trusted on. Phase-6: diff scrape names vs pushed-and-stored names for the full fleet — this is the highest-value item of the round-trip (⚠ flag, second-highest impact per epic).

**(5) Counter temporality — DECIDED: cumulative, hard-frozen** (`Literal["cumulative"]`), matching `prometheus_client` semantics and Grafana Cloud expectation. Delta would require inter-snapshot state and is explicitly out of scope; field shape reserves the option. No Phase-6 dependency beyond (4)'s round-trip confirming `rate()` works.

**(6) Metric expiration / series disappearance + start-time — DECIDED: snapshot semantics, `_created`-derived start-times.** Since the bridge reads the live registry, a series `MetricExpirationManager` deletes simply stops appearing in subsequent pushes — the same "series went away" signal a scraper gets, minus the explicit staleness marker (OTLP push has none; backends staleness-mark after their ingest window, ~5 min on GC/Mimir — document this as the known difference: expired devices linger up to that window on the push path). Counter re-creation after expiry: `prometheus_client` mints a fresh `_created`, and because start-time comes from `_created`, the pushed point carries a **new start time** → backends correctly detect the reset instead of seeing a counter go backwards. No bridge-side extra state needed. Phase-6: observe an actual expire→recreate cycle end-to-end (⚠ flag — regressions here are silent, the epic's own words).

**(7) `Info` / `_created` — DECIDED:** Info → `Gauge`=1 named `<name>_info` (exact scrape name, labels as attributes). `_created` samples are consumed as start-times and dropped as series — the push path deliberately has **no** `_created` series (they're a prom-text exposition artefact, not data). Document as a known scrape-vs-push difference (push has fewer series: no `_created`). No Phase-6 dependency.

---

## 4. File / lane plan (disjoint-file, single-owner seams)

New module `core/otel_metrics.py`: `OTelMetricsBridge` + pure `translate_families` (+ small helpers), private everything, no global provider, self-obs counters registered **only when enabled** (mirrors `DataLogEmitter`). Shared TLS helper `build_otlp_credentials(ca_cert_path, client_cert_path, client_key_path) -> grpc.ChannelCredentials | None` lives in `core/otel_tracing.py` next to `build_otel_resource` (already the shared-otel-plumbing home); reads the PEM files, returns `grpc.ssl_channel_credentials(root_certificates=..., private_key=..., certificate_chain=...)`, `None` when no paths set (exporter then uses system trust store when `insecure=False` — today's behaviour, preserved).

New `CollectorMetricName` members (seam — mirrors the `DATA_LOG_*` pair at lines 647–648):
```
OTLP_METRICS_EXPORTS_TOTAL            = "meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_exports_total"       # label: status=success|failure (reuse LabelName.<net-name-4>TUS)
OTLP_METRICS_POINTS_EXPORTED_TOTAL    = "meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_points_exported_total"
OTLP_METRICS_POINTS_DROPPED_TOTAL     = "meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_points_dropped_total"  # translation failures, best-effort
OTLP_METRICS_LAST_SUCCESS_TIME<net-name-4>MP   = "meraki_exporter_otlp_metrics_last_success_timestamp_seconds"  # the heartbeat, gap (2)
```
No new `LabelName` needed (`<net-name-4>TUS` exists, `metrics.py:38`).

`app.py` wiring (mirrors DataLogEmitter/tracing exactly): construct `self.otel_metrics_bridge = OTelMetricsBridge(self.settings)` in `ExporterApp.__init__` beside the emitter (~line 157); `await self.otel_metrics_bridge.start()` in lifespan startup (it needs the running loop, unlike the emitter whose batch processor is thread-based); `await self.otel_metrics_bridge.stop()` in lifespan shutdown before the tracing/logging shutdowns (~line 498), so the final flush still has a live channel.

**Lane decomposition (all seams single-owner):**

| Lane | Files owned | Work | Model/effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — config seam** | `core/config_models.py` only | `OTelMetricsSettings`, parent cert fields, validator extension, `metrics_endpoint`/`metrics_insecure` properties + its config tests file | Sonnet, medium |
| **B — the bridge** | `core/otel_metrics.py` + `tests/unit/test_otel_metrics.py` | Snapshotter, translation, routing, self-obs, heartbeat; codes against Lane A's frozen field names above | **Opus/high** (the crux; subtle translation semantics) |
| **C — TLS plumbing (#314)** | `core/otel_tracing.py`, `core/otel_data_logs.py` + their existing test files | `build_otlp_credentials`, pass `credentials=` into `OTLPSpanExporter`/`OTLPLogExporter` (both verified to accept it) | Sonnet, medium. ⚠ Lane B consumes `build_otlp_credentials` from Lane C's file — freeze the signature above; B imports it, C implements it |
| **D — wiring pass** | `app.py`, `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` | Enum members + lifespan wiring; run after A–C land | **Orchestrator** (seam files) |
| **E — docs** | `docs/observability/otel.md`, `.env.example` | New metrics-plane section, scrape-vs-OTLP differences table (gaps 2–7), remove the "sole metrics surface / future bridge" caveat paragraph, heartbeat alert recipe, TLS docs | Sonnet, low |

`core/config_logger.py`: check whether nested `otel.logs` needed explicit handling when it landed; if so Lane A mirrors it, otherwise no change (pydantic nesting is automatic).

---

## 5. Issue mapping

- **#313** (add OTLP metrics exporter) — IS the epic's core bridge. Satisfied by Lanes A+B+D. Close with the commit that lands `core/otel_metrics.py` + wiring: `Closes #313`.
- **#314** (TLS for OTLP endpoint) — premise **partly stale**: `insecure` is already configurable for traces (`OTelSettings.insecure`, `config_models.py:623` → `otel_tracing.py:118–121`) and inherited by data logs (`logs_insecure`). What genuinely remains: (a) extend the insecure/TLS control to the new metrics channel (Lane A's `metrics.insecure` + inheritance), (b) CA/mTLS cert-path support across all three OTLP exporters (Lane C). Close with the Lane C commit: `Closes #314`, with a comment noting the stale half.
- **#339** (epic) — satisfied when A–E land with gaps (2)–(7) each *resolved-or-documented* per §3 (the epic's own acceptance wording). The live scrape-vs-push diff harness (epic Phase 0/3) cannot run in this environment; recommend closing #339 on the docs commit **and transferring the ⚠ §7 items to #619 (Phase 6)** with an explicit comment, rather than holding the epic open on the round-trip. Orchestrator's call; the spec supports either.

Suggested commit slicing: (1) Lane A config `Refs #339`; (2) Lane C TLS `Closes #314`; (3) Lanes B+D bridge+wiring `Closes #313, Refs #339`; (4) Lane E docs `Closes #339` (or `Refs` if holding for Phase 6).

---

## 6. Test strategy (deterministic, no live collector)

- **Pure translation (`translate_families`)** against a throwaway `CollectorRegistry` with one of each: Counter (assert → `Sum`, `is_monotonic=True`, `CUMULATIVE`, name `*_total`, `start_time_unix_nano` == the `_created` sample, no `_created` metric in output), Gauge, Histogram (assert de-cumulated `bucket_counts`, `explicit_bounds` without `+Inf`, `count`/`sum` correct), Info (→ Gauge=1 named `*_info`), and `unit == ""` on every `Metric`.
- **Routing:** registry seeded with `meraki_*`, `meraki_exporter_*`, and a `python_*`-style family; assert exact partition for `product`/`self`/`all`, and that the heartbeat gauge appears under **all three** include modes.
- **Bridge loop:** inject a ~10-line stub `MetricExporter` subclass capturing `MetricsData` (the test seam; SDK 1.43 ships `InMemoryMetricReader` but no in-memory *exporter*, so a stub it is — same pattern as `DataLogEmitter`'s `exporter=` seam). Assert resource attrs match `build_otel_resource`, export failure increments `..._exports_total{status="failure"}` and never raises, `stop()` performs a final export + `shutdown()`.
- **Sole-surface invariant (the load-bearing test):** `generate_latest(REGI<net-name-6>Y)` byte-identical with `otel.metrics.enabled=False` before vs after constructing the bridge; and with it enabled, `/metrics` differs **only** by the four new self-obs series (which, like the data-log counters, register only when enabled).
- **Config:** validator error matrix (enabled w/o resolvable endpoint; cert-path XOR; certs-with-all-insecure), inheritance properties, env-var round-trip for `MERAKI_EXPORTER_OTEL__METRICS__*`.
- **TLS (Lane C):** monkeypatch `grpc.ssl_channel_credentials`; assert exporters receive `credentials=` when paths set + resolved `insecure=False`, and `credentials=None`/system-trust behaviour otherwise preserved.
- **Golden metrics:** existing goldens (`tests/unit/golden/metrics/*.txt`) are collector-scoped and unaffected; the new self-obs series need no golden file, but the golden harness must stay green — the invariant test above is the guard.

---

## 7. ⚠ #619 Phase-6 flags (require a real exporter → OTel Collector → Prometheus/Mimir round-trip)

1. **Name-normalization diff (highest value):** full-fleet diff of scrape names vs OTLP-pushed-and-stored names on Grafana Cloud — confirms no double `_total`, no unit suffixing with `unit=""`, histogram `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count` re-rendering equality. This is the parity oracle for gap (4).
2. **`job`/`instance`/`target_info` mapping:** confirm GC's resource-attribute → label mapping matches the documented table; confirm dashboard selectors work on both paths (gap 3).
3. **Expiration round-trip:** expire a device series mid-run, confirm backend staleness window behaviour, then re-create and confirm the new `_created`-derived start-time yields a clean counter reset, not a negative `rate()` (gap 6).
4. **Heartbeat alerting:** validate the `last_success_timestamp` alert recipe end-to-end, including behaviour when the collector endpoint is down (gap 2).
5. **Scale/limits:** full-fleet snapshot size vs gRPC 4 MB with `max_export_batch_size=10_000`; export duration vs interval; DPM cost of `include=all` on GC (informs whether the docs should steer cost-sensitive users to `product`).
6. **Dependency pin advice (no new dep needed — verified installed & importing):** `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp 1.43.0` + `opentelemetry-sdk 1.43.0` already satisfy everything; keep the existing `>=1.29` floors, but note the bridge relies on the public dataclasses in `opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export` (present and stable across 1.29→1.43) — a Renovate major bump should re-run the bridge unit tests as the canary, same posture as the `_logs` confinement note in `otel_data_logs.py`.
7. **`temporality` future:** if delta support is ever requested, it needs inter-snapshot state in the bridge — flag as explicitly out of v1 scope, revisit only with a concrete backend requirement.

title: Epic: optional OTLP metrics emission via Prometheus-registry bridge

body:
## Mechanism

`collectors/devices/mx_firewall.py::collect_org_security_events` counts events into a per-org `counts` dict, then calls `self._security_events_total._metrics.clear()` unconditionally before re-setting only the current org's `{org_id, org_name, event_type}` series via `parent._set_metric`. The gauge is shared across orgs and the method runs once per org concurrently (`device.py` → `ManagedTaskGroup(max_concurrency=settings.api.concurrency_limit)`, default > 1), so the global clear wipes every org's series — only the last-writer org's `meraki_mx_security_events_total` survives per cycle. Same defect class as #F-001 / #F-020.

## Fix

Remove the `_metrics.clear()` call. Event types with zero events this cycle are reclaimed by the metric expiration manager (#334) via `parent._set_metric` tracking.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `_metrics.clear()` in mx_firewall.py.
- A series seeded for org2 survives an org1 `collect_org_security_events` call (including the empty-response path).
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-087 (validated). Depends on #334.

Removed the global `_metrics.clear()` call(s); the affected gauges already emit via `parent._set_metric`, so stale label series are now reclaimed by the expiration manager (#334) on TTL expiry rather than a cross-org wipe. Tests updated to assert the multi-org-safe property (a series seeded for org2 survives an org1 collection cycle). `make check` green (1158 passed).

title: [F-020] MXHACollector _metrics.clear() wipes other orgs' HA mode/role series

body:
## Mechanism

Several device sub-collectors call `<gauge>._metrics.clear()` at the top of an org-scoped `collect_*` method to drop stale label series after a label transition. But these sub-collectors are instantiated **once** on `DeviceCollector` and share a single gauge instance across all orgs, while `device.py` fans org processing out concurrently via `ManagedTaskGroup(max_concurrency=settings.api.concurrency_limit)` (default > 1). `_metrics.clear()` wipes **every label combination of that gauge globally** — so org B's collection wipes org A's just-set series mid-cycle. After a full cycle only the last-writer org's series survive at scrape time in a multi-org deployment.

The 7 offending sites (this umbrella issue covers mg/ms_power/mx; the mx_ha sites are #F-020 and the mx_firewall site is #F-087):

- `collectors/devices/mg.py` — `_mg_uplink_status_info._metrics.clear()`, `_mg_uplink_roaming._metrics.clear()`
- `collectors/devices/ms_power.py` — `_ms_power_supply_status._metrics.clear()`
- `collectors/devices/mx.py` — `_mx_uplink_info._metrics.clear()`

All these gauges are already set via `parent._set_metric`, which now (per #334) registers each series with the expiration manager carrying its Gauge reference.

## Fix

Remove the `_metrics.clear()` calls. Stale label series (status/provider transitions, mode churn) are reclaimed by the metric expiration manager on TTL expiry — no cross-org wipe. Tests are updated to assert the multi-org-safe property: collecting one org must not wipe another org's pre-seeded series.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `_metrics.clear()` remains in mg.py / ms_power.py / mx.py.
- A series seeded for org2 survives an org1 collection cycle on the shared gauge.
- `make check` green.

Source: bug-bash finding F-001 (validated). Depends on #334.

title: [F-001] Multi-org gauge wipe: per-org _metrics.clear() erases other orgs' series

body:
## Mechanism

Three `OrganizationCollector` gauges keyed by grouped label sets are written with raw `self._x.labels(**labels).set(count)` — never through `self._set_metric()` — so they are never registered with the `MetricExpirationManager` and never removed when a label combination disappears from the current cycle:

- `meraki_org_devices_total` (label `device_type`) — `organization.py:_collect_device_metrics`
- `meraki_org_devices_by_model_total` (label `model`) — `organization.py:_collect_device_counts_by_model`
- `meraki_org_devices_availability_total` (labels `status`, `product_type`) — `organization.py:_collect_device_availability_metrics`

Because these never zero-fill disappeared combos and never expire, a combo that drops out (e.g. all devices of a model removed, or the last `offline` device coming back online) leaves its **last value frozen forever** — a stuck `offline>0` series can hold an alert firing indefinitely. This is the same defect class the codebase already solves elsewhere (`device.py` calls `.remove()` for stale status transitions).

Depends on #334 (real series removal in `MetricExpirationManager`) which is now merged; this finding wires these gauges into that machinery.

## Confirmed file refs

- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/organization.py` — the three `.labels(**labels).set(count)` sites (`_collect_device_metrics`, `_collect_device_counts_by_model`, `_collect_device_availability_metrics`).

## Acceptance criteria

- All three gauges are emitted via `self._set_metric(gauge, labels, count, <MetricName>.value)`.
- Each therefore registers with the expiration manager carrying its Gauge reference, so stale label combinations are removed on TTL expiry (MEDIUM: 600s).
- Emitted values are unchanged; existing org-collector tests stay green.
- A test proves the three gauge families participate in expiration tracking (tracked with a Gauge reference).

Source: bug-bash finding F-094 (validated).

comments.body: Fixed in d5ec85b. All three org device-count gauges (`meraki_org_devices_total`, `meraki_org_devices_by_model_total`, `meraki_org_devices_availability_total`) now emit via `self._set_metric(...)` instead of raw `.labels().set()`, so they register with the expiration manager carrying their Gauge reference (#334) and stale label combinations are removed on TTL expiry (MEDIUM, 600s). Emitted values unchanged; new test `test_device_count_gauges_participate_in_expiration` proves all three families are tracked with a Gauge reference. `make check` green (1158 passed).

title: [F-094] Route org device-count gauges through _set_metric so grouped label sets expire

body:
## Mechanism

`MetricExpirationManager._cleanup_expired_metrics` was an admitted no-op placeholder: its docstring stated *"This is a placeholder for actual cleanup. In practice, Prometheus doesn't provide an easy way to delete individual metric series."* It only deleted entries from the internal `self._metric_timestamps` / `self._metric_counts` dicts and incremented an `_expired_metrics_total` counter — it never called `Gauge.remove()`/`.clear()`, so **no series was ever removed from `/metrics`**.

`track_metric_update` (called from `MetricCollector._set_metric`) only stored `(collector_name, metric_name, frozen_labels) -> (timestamp, tier)`, keeping no reference to the actual Gauge object, so removal was impossible even in principle.

Consequences: any metric family that relies on "expires automatically via the metric expiration manager" for correctness (e.g. `ms.py::_emit_port_error_warning_metrics`, which emits only currently-active `error_type=1` series and depends on expiration to drop cleared errors) leaves a **stale `error_type` series set to 1 forever** with no code path that ever removes it. This is the foundational seam blocking every "stale series / expires automatically" finding (F-094 and the multi-org wipe findings F-001/F-020/F-087).

## Confirmed file refs

- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/metric_expiration.py:217-260` — `_cleanup_expired_metrics` placeholder; `track_metric_update:106-137`; `check_cardinality:276-321`.
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/core/collector.py:598-657` — `_set_metric` calls `track_metric_update` (had no metric reference).
- `src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/collectors/devices/ms.py:487-524` — depends on real expiration for correctness.

## Acceptance criteria

- `track_metric_update` accepts the owning `Gauge` object and records it per tracked series.
- On TTL expiry **and** on cardinality shedding, the actual Prometheus series is removed via `Gauge.remove(*ordered_label_values)`, not just untracked; removal is resilient to already-removed series.
- `_set_metric` passes the Gauge through so expiration participates automatically.
- Backward compatible: callers that don't pass a Gauge keep bookkeeping-only behaviour.
- Tests prove the child series disappears from the Gauge after expiry and after cardinality shed.

Source: bug-bash finding F-038 (validated).

**Area:** `mt` · **Type:** `new-metric` · **Priority:** `P3` · **Effort:** `S`

### Goal / data unlocked
A metric for MT20 button presses (`pressType`: long/short), deferred from #246 which shipped the no2/o3/pm10 air-quality metrics.

### Why it was deferred from #246
The MT sensor pipeline normalizes every reading through `core/domain_models.py::SensorMeasurement`, which requires a **float value** and a fixed `metric` Literal. A button press has no numeric value — only a `pressType` string (`long`/`short`) — so it does not fit that pipeline without a dedicated code path. Issue #246 explicitly sanctioned scoping button out ("explicitly scope this item to no2/o3/pm10 only and treat button separately").

### Additional design constraint
Button presses are **event-shaped**, not steady-state. `getOrganizationSensorReadingsLatest` returns only the *last* reading, so at the 60s FAST-tier poll cadence any presses between polls are lost. A plain gauge snapshot will silently miss presses.

### Suggested approach (verify against the spec before implementing)
Verified response shape (Meraki OpenAPI v1.72.0): `button: { pressType: "long" | "short" }` on `/organizations/{organizationId}/sensor/readings/latest`. Options:
- A label-valued "last known press" info gauge, e.g. `meraki_mt_button_last_press_info{press_type=...}` set to the reading timestamp (last-known semantics; accepts missed presses between polls), OR
- Drive button presses via the webhook sink (`core/webhook_handler.py`) which is event-driven and would not miss presses — likely the better long-term home.

Needs: `SensorMetricType.BUTTON`, `SensorDataField.PRESS_TYPE` (`sensor_constants.py`), `LabelName.PRESS_TYPE` (`metrics.py`), an `MTMetricName` member, and a dedicated (non-`SensorMeasurement`) handling path in `collectors/devices/mt.py`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Metric implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md`
- [ ] Domain enums for metric + label names; response validated via a Pydantic model
- [ ] Cardinality reviewed (press_type is bounded: long/short)
- [ ] Tests added; `make check` green
- [ ] Docs regenerated (`make docgen`)

Executed the deferred #630 field-diff live (2026-07-03, org <maintainer-org-id>, MR56 network) between the two connection-stats endpoints:

- `getNetworkWirelessConnectionStats` (network-aggregate, `nh_connection_stats`) → returns a **single dict** `{assoc, auth, dhcp, dns, success}` for the whole network.
- `getNetworkWirelessDevicesConnectionStats` (per-device, `mr_connection_stats`) → returns a **list of per-`serial` rows**, each with its own `connectionStats` sub-object.

### Goal / data unlocked
would finally give real values to the long-dead `MR_SIGNAL_QUALITY_PERCENT`/`MR_SIGNAL_NOISE_RATIO_DB` enum entries — actual SNR/RSSI per AP, the classic "is this AP in a good RF spot" metric

### Meraki API
`GET /networks/{networkId}/wireless/signalQualityHistory` (`getNetworkWirelessSignalQualityHistory`) — requires `clientId` **or** `deviceSerial` (or `apTag`) as a mandatory filter; there is no bulk/org-wide equivalent for this data

Recommend SLOW tier only, bounded concurrency, and possibly restricting to a configurable subset (e.g. only APs tagged for RF troubleshooting) rather than the full fleet. This is why the enum members were probably stubbed and abandoned — flagging as the likely reason, and recommending either accepting the cost explicitly at SLOW tier with tight concurrency limits, or resolving to delete the dead enum entries instead (see item above).

**v1 decision (Rob 2026-07-03): BUILD, default-ON with opt-out.** Per-AP signal quality (SNR/RSSI) ships as a bounded metric (per-AP, not per-client). Default-on but with a documented opt-out and the per-AP fan-out API cost explained so operators can disable it knowingly. NOTE: the per-*client* variant (mandatory clientId filter → per-client fan-out) does NOT belong here — that routes to the OTel log emitter #622. Build in Phase-4 wave 4B.

## 🔧 Scope decision (Rob, 2026-07-03) — tag-scoping added to the build spec

Building #324 in Wave 4B as **default-ON, opt-out**, PLUS an **AP-tag scoping** control so operators can bound the API burden without turning the feature off entirely.

**Config surface (core/config_models.py):**
- `collect_ap_signal_quality: bool = True` — master switch (default on; opt-out).
- `ap_signal_quality_tags: list[str] = []` — **empty ⇒ all APs** (the default, full coverage); **non-empty ⇒ only APs carrying at least one of these Meraki device tags** are fetched. This is the burden-reduction lever.

**Mechanism:** per-AP fan-out over `getNetworkWirelessSignalQualityHistory` (no bulk/org-wide form exists — one call per selected AP per network, SLOW tier, `ManagedTaskGroup`-bounded). When `ap_signal_quality_tags` is set, filter the AP list to devices whose `tags` intersect the configured set before fan-out (device tags are already in inventory — zero extra calls to resolve them). Endpoint group `MR_SIGNAL_QUALITY`; its `cost_fn` scales with the **selected** AP count, and it composes with the #623 `enabled_fn` (skip entirely when `collect_ap_signal_quality` is false or the selected-AP count is 0).

**Metrics:** gives real values to the existing long-dead `MR_SIGNAL_QUALITY_PERCENT` / `MR_SIGNAL_NOISE_RATIO_DB` enums (per-AP, labels = std device labels; no per-client cardinality — per-client signal detail routes to the #622 OTel log stream, not metrics).

**Docs:** the config-doc + support-matrix entry must state the rate-limit cost plainly and show the tag-scoping example, so the opt-out/scope-down path is discoverable.

body:
**Area:** `ops` · **Type:** `feature` · **Priority:** `P3` · **Effort:** `L` · **Milestone:** M8 — Larger / optional (deferred)

### Goal / data unlocked
Every single collector call today is `asyncio.to_thread(self.api.X.Y, ...)` (sync SDK blocking a thread-pool thread per in-flight call), explicitly called out as required in `api/CLAUDE.md`/`core/CLAUDE.md`. The SDK ships a fully async variant that would remove the thread-pool indirection, let real `aiohttp` connection pooling/keep-alive kick in, and centralize concurrency control in one place instead of the current mix of `AsyncMerakiClient`'s semaphore + `ManagedTaskGroup` + ad-hoc batch smoothing.

### Meraki API
`meraki.aio.AsyncDashboardAPI` (confirmed present in installed SDK 3.2.0 at `.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/meraki/aio/`), backed by `aiohttp` with its own `AIO_MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS` semaphore and native async retry/backoff — no thread pool involved.

### Files to touch
`api/client.py` (swap underlying client construction), every collector (`self.api.X.Y(...)` sync calls → `await self.api.X.Y(...)` async calls, drop `asyncio.to_thread` wrapping throughout).

### Notes / risks
Large blast radius — touches essentially every collector file and all tests/mocks. Not urgent (current approach works and Python's default thread-pool executor has headroom at this app's call volume), but worth a scoped spike given how much of the existing concurrency-control code (semaphores, ManagedTaskGroup, batch smoothing) exists specifically to compensate for wrapping a sync client. Do this only as a deliberate, isolated migration project — not bundled with the other items here.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md` ("Implementing a roadmap task")
- [ ] Behaviour covered by tests; `make check` green
- [ ] Docs/config docs updated if user-facing (`make docgen`)

none new — this is about the existing apidrift tool's input spec.

comments.body: **v1-readiness assessment (2026-07-02) — related addition** (finding MET-10): alongside per-cycle API-call cost, customers also lack an org-budget *headroom* signal (the old `rate_limit_remaining` gauges were removed as dead in F-073, and the client-side token gauge is only the exporter's own estimate). #537 tracks `meraki_exporter_build_info` + evaluating a budget-headroom gauge — coordinate the two so the self-observability surface lands coherently. The adaptive-scheduler epic #617 would consume the same signal as feedback.

**Execution routing (for #618 orchestration):** agent model: `opus` · thinking effort: `medium`.

The orchestrator spawns one dedicated subagent per issue with these settings and implements nothing itself. Implementer: if this issue turns out materially harder than scoped (cross-seam impact, unclear design, contradicting evidence), STOP and report back for escalation to a stronger model — do not improvise architecture.

Cross-referenced from #537 (MET-10), which evaluated adding a first-class org API-budget headroom gauge and **deferred it here** with the following finding:

Do not add a `meraki_exporter_org_api_budget_*` gauge sourced from the rate limiter. `OrgRateLimiter` (`core/rate_limiter.py`) is a **token bucket** — its state is per-org instantaneous token count, burst capacity, and `rate_per_second = base_rps * rate_limit_shared_fraction`. It measures **bucket occupancy at each `acquire()`**, not request rate over time. Its only self-metrics are `meraki_exporter_api_rate_limiter_tokens` (instantaneous, gauge), `_throttled_total`, and the wait-seconds histogram — none is a request-rate.

A "budget utilization/headroom" gauge would therefore either re-expose token-fraction (`tokens/burst`), which is misleading as "budget consumed" and only updates on acquire, or require **new time-windowed request-rate accounting** — a rate-limiter refactor, out of scope for a self-contained metric add.

The honest answer already exists in PromQL from the existing per-request counter:
`sum by (org_id)(rate(meraki_exporter_api_requests_total[5m]))`, optionally `/ <org budget>` for utilization. Note "budget" is ambiguous: the limiter deliberately uses `base_rps * rate_limit_shared_fraction`, not the raw ~10 rps, so numerator/denominator need a product decision.

**Recommendation:** scope #276 as a **dashboard/runbook change** (PromQL recording rule / panel), not a new metric. If a first-class gauge is still wanted, it belongs here as a small measured-rate module (recording rule or a windowed counter), not bolted onto `OrgRateLimiter`. #537 (build-info half) is done and closed; this budget-headroom part is fully delegated to this issue.

Closing as already-answerable (confirmed per the issue's own 'worth confirming before building anything' note). The exporter already emits `meraki_exporter_collector_api_calls_total{collector,tier,...}` (CollectorMetricName.COLLECTOR_API_CALLS_TOTAL, core/collector.py) — a real measured per-collector API-call counter, not the old inline guess. Per-cycle cost per tier/org is a PromQL away, e.g.:

```promql
sum by (tier) (increase(meraki_exporter_collector_api_calls_total[5m]))
```

This measures the same thing a new metric would, so no new code is warranted; the capacity/regression view belongs in the runbook + Grafana dashboard rebuild (Phase 7). Rate-limiter wait/throttle histograms (`meraki_exporter_api_rate_limiter_*`) cover the budget-pressure angle. Closing as done/redundant.

**v1-readiness assessment (2026-07-02) — concrete defect list for this issue** (finding SCALE-04; full context: label `v1-readiness`, capacity analysis in #542):

A single org can therefore draw ~20 req/s outbound (org bucket + global bucket in parallel) → guaranteed 429s. Only 4 of the 8 network-health fetchers got the F-170 `org_id=` threading fix.
3. **Undecorated call sites acquire no token at all**: `ms.py:1488` (STP), `mr/performance.py:922` (packet-loss byNetwork), `mt.py:305` (sensor readings latest).

**Area:** `ms` · **Type:** `new-metric` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M1 — Quick wins & correctness

### Goal / data unlocked
`meraki_ms_port_errors_total{error_type=...}` / `meraki_ms_port_warnings_total{warning_type=...}` — surfaces things like duplex mismatches, port flapping, PoE budget exceeded that Meraki already detects but the exporter throws away today

### Meraki API
no new call — `errors`/`warnings` arrays are already present in the `getDeviceSwitchPortsStatuses`/`getOrganizationSwitchPortsStatusesBySwitch` response consumed in `ms.py::collect()`/`collect_port_statuses_by_switch` (spec-verified field names on `/devices/{serial}/switch/ports/statuses`)

### Files to touch
`ms.py` (`collect()`, `collect_device_port_usage_metrics()`, `collect_port_statuses_by_switch()`), `core/constants/metrics_constants.py` (`MSMetricName.MS_PORT_ERRORS_TOTAL`/`MS_PORT_WARNINGS_TOTAL`), `core/metrics.py` (reuse `LabelName.ERROR_TYPE`, add e.g. `WARNING_TYPE` or reuse `TYPE`)

### Notes / risks
Free — zero extra API calls or rate-limit cost. Cardinality: each port emits 0..N error/warning strings; if you gauge-per-string-value it multiplies by port count — better to emit a single `meraki_ms_port_error_count`/`warning_count` gauge (no per-string label) plus optionally an `_info`-style gauge only for currently-active distinct error types (bounded by Meraki's fixed enum of error/warning strings, not user data) to keep cardinality flat.

- [ ] Metric(s) implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md` ("Implementing a roadmap task")

- [ ] Emitted via `parent._set_metric()`; correct update tier chosen and justified
- [ ] Cardinality reviewed — no unbounded/attacker-influenced labels
- [ ] Tests added (factory + metric assertions); `make check` green
- [ ] Docs regenerated if metrics/config changed (`make docgen`)

**Area:** `config` · **Type:** `qol` · **Priority:** `P0` · **Effort:** `S` · **Milestone:** M1 — Quick wins & correctness

### Goal / data unlocked
A new user who forgets to set the API key currently gets a raw, confusing pydantic `ValidationError` dump instead of the friendly guided message that was clearly written for exactly this case.

### Meraki API
N/A

### Files to touch
`src/meraki_dashboard_exporter/__main__.py` (lines ~32, 48-58)

### Notes / risks
Verified by running `Settings()` with a clean env: the real error is `[('meraki',), 'missing', 'Field required']` because `MerakiSettings` is a required nested model. `__main__.py`'s check is `if error["loc"] == ("api_key",)` — this never matches (real loc is `("meraki",)` or `("meraki","api_key")`), so the nicely-formatted "❌ ERROR: Meraki API key is required..." block is unreachable dead code. Compounding it, both the `--help` text and that same dead message tell the user to set `MERAKI_API_KEY`, but the actual required var (per `.env.example` and `core/config.py`'s `env_prefix="MERAKI_EXPORTER_"` + `env_nested_delimiter="__"`) is `MERAKI_EXPORTER_MERAKI__API_KEY`. Fix: match on `error["loc"][0] == "meraki"` (or check for any loc starting with `"meraki"`), and correct every env var name in `--help`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Change implemented following the standard workflow in `CLAUDE.md` ("Implementing a roadmap task")
- [ ] Behaviour covered by tests; `make check` green

body:
## Summary
The published `linux/arm64` image fails at startup on every container with:
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'
```
The exporter never starts (CrashLoopBackOff under Kubernetes on arm64 nodes).

## Environment
- Platform: `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon M1 bare-metal → Fedora Asahi → k3s v1.35)
- Image: `ghcr.io/rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter:latest` and recent `main-*` tags
- Confirmed against the explicit arm64 sub-manifest digest `sha256:c7d345273c4ed9da92078844662a67d449caa15ce2af1620465c42f114c37f7e`

## Reproduction
```sh
docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 \
  ghcr.io/rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter:latest \
  python -c "import pydantic_core._pydantic_core"
# → ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'
```
Reproduced on `latest`, `main-3d430f8`, and `main-b77128e` — not a stale-tag issue; every published arm64 build is affected. The amd64 image is fine.

## Likely cause
The `pydantic_core` native extension (`_pydantic_core.*.so`) in the image is not the aarch64 build. The Dockerfile's builder stage runs `uv sync` and then `COPY --from=builder /app/.venv` into the runtime image. If the multi-arch build runs the builder stage on an amd64 host under emulation (or otherwise resolves wheels for the build platform rather than `TARGETARCH`), the venv copied into the arm64 image contains the wrong-arch `pydantic_core` wheel — exactly this failure.

## Workaround
Building the same source **natively on arm64** (no QEMU/cross-build) produces a working image — `uv` then resolves the correct `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` wheel. So this is a CI/build-platform issue, not a source bug.

## Suggested fix
Ensure the builder stage resolves/installs for `TARGETARCH` (e.g. native arm64 runners in the multi-arch matrix, or `uv`/pip platform pinning), so the copied `.venv` carries the aarch64 `pydantic_core` wheel.

comments.body:
Your diagnosis was spot on - build-platform issue, not a source bug.

The multi-arch image was getting built in a single buildx job under QEMU emulation. On the arm64 leg that emulation pulled the wrong-architecture `pydantic_core` wheel into the venv, which is exactly the import you saw blow up.

Fix: build each platform on its own native runner (arm64 on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, no QEMU at all), push by digest, then merge the per-platform images into a manifest list. Shipped in **v0.30.1**.

While I was in the release pipeline I also found a separate bug: release builds had only been publishing `main-*` tags since ~August 2025, so `:latest` had been stale on 0.26.0 this whole time. Fixed the release tagging and republished `0.30.1` / `latest`.

Verified the new arm64 image imports `pydantic_core._pydantic_core` cleanly - the exact thing that was failing before.

Thanks @iamdexterpark - the writeup, the cross-digest reproduction, and confirming it worked under a native build all pointed straight at the build platform. That's what pinned it down immediately. Closing this out.

**Update (2026-07-02):** a full v1 production-readiness assessment quantified this pain point: at ~500-network scale the current fixed-tier schedule demands ~178% of a single org's 10 req/s API budget, so rate-limiting pressure like you describe is structural, not a tuning issue. The fix is now a tracked program (label `v1-readiness`, milestone M4):
- #270 — rate limiter actually enforced per HTTP request and per-org keyed
- #541 — per-endpoint refresh intervals matched to data windows (biggest quick win)
- #545 — single 429-retry owner (today SDK retries × exporter retries multiply)
- #548 — perPage maxima (halves some pagination fan-outs)
- #542 — a quantitative sizing formula so you can predict budget use from your org shape
- #617 — an adaptive budget-aware scheduler (epic) so the exporter paces itself instead of saturating the org budget
- #585 — v1 will be one exporter instance per organization, with a sharding guide (#568)

Leaving this open until the sizing guidance (#542) lands so there's a concrete answer for large environments like yours.

Sizing guidance has landed - see the new Scaling Guide: https://m7kni.io/meraki-dashboard-exporter/scaling-guide/. Short version for your env: the pain is structural, not a tuning miss. A single org has a fixed 10 req/s API budget, and at ~500 networks the fixed-tier schedule demands ~178% of it - the dominant cost is 8 API calls per wireless network every cycle for network-health, so it's the wireless-network count that's blowing your budget, not device count. One thing in your config that isn't doing anything: `MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_RPS` isn't a real setting (no such key, so it's silently ignored) - the actual one is `MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND`, but note that only paces calls, it doesn't reduce how many a cycle needs. The levers that actually cut demand, in order: tighten `NETWORK_FILTER` to the wireless networks you care about (biggest win - drops 8 calls/cycle per excluded wireless net), raise `MERAKI_EXPORTER_UPDATE_INTERVALS__MEDIUM` from 300 to 600, and stretch the per-endpoint gates (`MS_PORT_USAGE_INTERVAL`, `MS_PACKET_<net-name-4>TS_INTERVAL` etc, all default 600). Practical envelope with today's defaults is roughly ≤150-200 wireless networks / ≤1,500-2,000 devices per instance. Since v1 is one exporter per org, you can't shard a single big org across pods to go faster - the budget is per-org - so for one large org it's filter + interval tuning until the adaptive scheduler (#617) lands. The guide has the full formula and worked examples for exactly your 500-network shape. Keeping this open until #617 automates the pacing, but the above should get you under the limit now.

Closing this out - everything it was blocked on has now landed.

Short version for your ~500-network env: the rate pressure was structural (one org = a fixed 10 req/s budget, and the old fixed-tier schedule wanted ~178% of it), not a config you were getting wrong. The v1 rate-limiting program is now merged:

- **adaptive budget-aware scheduler (#617)** - the exporter now paces itself against your org's actual API budget instead of firing every tier on a fixed clock. It stretches per-endpoint intervals to fit demand under `budget × target_utilisation`, and reacts to real 429s with AIMD backoff rather than saturating and eating them.
- if your org is still over budget even after it stretches everything to the caps, it now logs a **loud startup warning naming exactly which collectors to disable** - so you find out at boot instead of by hitting the limit.
- **per-endpoint refresh intervals** for the windowed network-health calls (#541) - the biggest single demand cut
- **one 429-retry owner** with bounded Retry-After (#545) - no more SDK-retries × exporter-retries multiplying
- **perPage maxima** on paginated fetchers (#548), and the OrgRateLimiter now enforced on every collector call, per-org keyed (#270)
- **sizing formula + scaling guide** so you can predict budget use from your org shape (#542, #568): https://m7kni.io/meraki-dashboard-exporter/scaling-guide/

Two notes from your config snippet: `MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_RPS` isn't a real key (silently ignored) - the real one is `MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND`, but with the adaptive scheduler you shouldn't need to hand-tune it. Tightening `NETWORK_FILTER` to the wireless networks you actually care about is still the biggest lever for more headroom, since it's the wireless-network count (~8 calls/cycle each) that dominates.

Grab `main` (or the next tagged image) and it should keep itself under the limit. Reopen if you still see 429 storms after the scheduler's had a cycle or two to settle.

comments.body: hey @Seji64. Do you have any other clients using the meraki API?

_Investigation below by Claude Code (model: `claude-opus-4-7` 1M context, effort: max)._

---

Hey @Seji64 — thanks for the detailed logs, they were essential.

First, on @rknightion's follow-up about other clients: even with no other API consumers, there's a fan-out pattern in the exporter that can saturate your org's 10 RPS budget on its own. With ~7 wireless networks on a single org, here's what happens every MEDIUM (300s) cycle:

`NetworkHealthCollector` runs 5 sub-collectors per network (RF health, connection stats, data rates, Bluetooth, SSID performance) and dispatches all wireless networks to those sub-collectors in parallel via `network_batch_size` (default 30). 7 networks × ~6 calls each ≈ 42 calls in a tight window. The token bucket (10 RPS / 20 burst) drains, and the SDK starts seeing 429s with `Retry-After`. That's why it's specifically these endpoints — they all live in this collector. The other collectors (org/device/config/alerts) mostly use aggregated org-level endpoints with far lower fan-out, which is why they don't show up in your log.

Two amplifiers in the current code, both already noted in [`docs/api-call-audit.md`](https://github.com/rknightion/meraki-dashboard-exporter/blob/main/docs/api-call-audit.md) (recommendations #1 and #4):

1. `RFHealthCollector._fetch_organization_devices` calls `getOrganizationDevices` **per-network** with a `networkIds=[…]` filter — the inventory cache already holds every device for the org. With 7 wireless networks that's 7 redundant calls per cycle.
2. `NetworkHealthCollector._fetch_networks_for_health` bypasses the inventory cache and re-fetches `getOrganizationNetworks` directly each cycle.

Both are now routed through the shared inventory cache (changes prepared locally; @rknightion to land them in the next release).

**Immediate workarounds you can apply via env vars:**

```
MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__NETWORK_BATCH_SIZE=2
MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS_PER_SECOND=7
MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__RATE_LIMIT_BURST=10
MERAKI_EXPORTER_API__SMOOTHING_MIN_BATCH_DELAY=2
```

`NETWORK_BATCH_SIZE=2` is the highest-impact one — it caps how many network bundles run in parallel, so per-second call density drops sharply. The lower RPS/burst leaves headroom if any other tool shares your API key.

One thing worth knowing: the 429s in your log aren't actually breaking metric collection — the Meraki SDK auto-retries using the `Retry-After` header and succeeds. So this is log noise + slightly degraded throughput, not missing data. But agreed it's not pleasant, and the fixes above should cut the volume substantially.

title: meraki_mr_radio_broadcasting

body: Hello, I'm using this exporter to gather metrics from a set of devices we have deployed, including MS and MX types. However, the MX devices only show an intermittent status of up `meraki_device_up == 1`. I can verify these devices are online though, because if I query `meraki_device_status_info{device_type="mx", status="online"}`, they return a value of 1. These devices also show device up status == 1 on an 15 minute interval, then returns back to down. Any ideas as to the root cause?

comments.body:
Interesting that you're only seeing it on mx devices. MX support was implemented in the blind as it's the only meraki device type I don't have access to test against. I'll do some digging!

edit; found it ( BaseDeviceCollector.collect_common_metrics() reads device.get("status_info", {}).get("status", DeviceStatus.OFFLINE) - defaulting to OFFLINE )
